duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
deadline_text: No application dates posted.

name: Champaign Park District Seasonal and Summer Jobs
what_you_do: These are seasonal park district jobs. Examples are lifeguard and swim instructor at Sholem Aquatic Center. Others are summer camp staff, Prairie Farm, sports and grounds positions.
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.
duration: Seasonal jobs run April to November and do not exceed 6 months; summer camp is a 10-week program
deadline_text: No application dates or deadlines listed on the page.

name: Champaign Park District Teen Volunteering
what_you_do: You can volunteer at parks and programs. Examples include special events and Prairie Farm (May to August). Others are Virginia Theatre, sports and summer programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteers register on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal.

name: Dual Credit and Dual Enrollment at Parkland College
what_you_do: You can take Parkland College classes while in high school. You can take them on campus, online or at your high school. You earn college credit. In some cases, you also earn high school credit.
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask the Early College office.

name: Champaign Public Library Volunteers
what_you_do: You can help with sorting and shelving. You can work bookstore cashier shifts. You can help with storytime. You can help with a summer Club Fred program. Other roles are listed. Training is provided.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Typically 2 to 3 hours a week; a 4-month minimum is preferred
deadline_text: No deadline.

grades: Rising 7th to 12th grade. Individual camps have narrower ranges, such as 7th to 9th or 10th to 12th.
name: Grainger Engineering Summer Camps
what_you_do: These are week-long camps. You do hands-on projects and tour labs. Illinois engineering faculty and students teach you. Areas include aerospace, bioengineering, electronics, AI and quantum.
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $1,500, commuter $750, day camp $550, each plus a $25 deposit. The Trail Blazer Scholarship covers 50% or 100% for students who meet its criteria.
duration: One week per camp (June to August in 2026)
deadline_text: All 2026 camps are listed as full. 2027 application dates are not posted.

name: Young Scholars STEMM Research Program
what_you_do: You do six weeks of real research in a University of Illinois lab. Topics include neuroscience, AI, physics and bioengineering. You take part in seminars. You give a poster. There is a final symposium.
pay_detail: No cost except transportation. Housing, meals and a monetary award are provided (the page calls it a fellowship payment; the amount is not stated).
duration: 6 weeks (research began June 17 and ended July 31 in 2026); 30 to 35 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications Closed for Summer 2026.

name: Counselor-in-Training (CIT) Program
what_you_do: You help lead summer day camp activities. You assist counselors and campers. You set personal goals. You meet weekly with other CITs.
pay_detail: No wage is listed on the page; it is described as training for future summer and part-time jobs. Confirm with the contact.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week, three days a week, June 3 to July 31 in 2026 (8:15 am to 3 pm)
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: FRESH Crew Teen Volunteer Days
what_you_do: Join Saturday stewardship days in local parks: collect prairie seed, pull invasive plants and clear trash. No experience needed.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn service hours and references.
duration: 2 hours per event (2 to 4 pm Saturdays)
deadline_text: No registration. Fall 2026 dates: Oct 3, Oct 17, Nov 7, Nov 21, Dec 5 (2 to 4 pm).

name: Youth Event Support Volunteer
what_you_do: Teen volunteers help library staff set up and break down, and help run programs and events for kids and teens.
duration: Ongoing; most needed in summer and on afternoons and weekends in the school year
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Youth Volunteer Shifts (Blue Ridge Area Food Bank, Charlottesville)
what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer shift at the Charlottesville warehouse. You can also pick an offsite food distribution site. Kids and teens volunteer with a parent or guardian.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts
duration: One shift at a time. Shift length is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for shifts on the online volunteer calendar. Group visits must be booked at least one month ahead.

name: Junior Volunteers (Charlottesville-Albemarle SPCA)
what_you_do: Help with community service tasks at the animal shelter and rummage store. Volunteers are part of the shelter's daily work. Tasks depend on the SPCA's needs and your skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The volunteer pays a $25 volunteer fee plus a separate $9 background check. The page does not say if either is refundable.
duration: Ongoing. Hours and length are not stated.
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick an orientation date on the SPCA's calendar.

name: CATEC Career and Technical Programs (Charlottesville Area Technical Education Center)
org: Charlottesville Area Technical Education Center (CATEC), run by Charlottesville City Schools
what_you_do: Take hands-on career and technical classes in Auto Service Technology, Carpentry, Cosmetology, Culinary Arts, Electricity, Emergency Medical Technician, Fire Science, Nurse Aide and Patient Care Technician, or Veterinary Science.
grades: Not stated on the pages read
pay_detail: Free for Charlottesville City and Albemarle County students. Students earn high school elective credits, can earn industry certifications, and some programs offer dual enrollment college credit. Transportation to and from your base school is provided.
duration: School year classes. Program lengths and schedules are not stated on the pages read.
deadline_text: No enrollment dates are posted on the pages read. Ask your school counselor or CATEC.

name: Community Attention Youth Internship Program (CAYIP)
what_you_do: These are paid part-time internships at local worksites. You must finish a required CAYIP Academy on workplace skills. A counselor visits your site at least once a week.
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
deadline_text: The page lists four school-year sessions and one summer session for 2026-27 but gives dates only for Fall 2026 (applications Aug 20-28, 2026, now closed). For reference, the Summer 2025 application window was April 1 to May 1, 2025 (5 pm).

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Monticello Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Monticello Composite Squadron (Virginia Wing)
what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets each Tuesday from 7 to 9 p.m. at Lakeside Middle School.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.

name: Lifeguard Training (Charlottesville Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Charlottesville Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
what_you_do: This is a lifeguard certification class. The city's aquatics staff runs it. You must pass an in-water pretest. You finish online assignments. You attend in-class sessions.
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Session dates were not listed on the page; use the Registration & Tickets link.

name: High School Leadership Training (Leaders in Training), Camp Kingfisher
what_you_do: Help camp counselors with groups of campers at Camp Kingfisher. You help run canoe ponds, play games with campers, and spend time with groups in grades K to 5.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs $500 per session for new LITs, $450 for returning LITs. You earn about 140 volunteer service hours per session.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, Monday to Friday about 8:30 am to 3:45 pm, plus a one-day training
deadline_text: Summer 2026 sessions ran May 26 to July 30 with training May 22. Applications are taken until the program is full. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Water Warriors
what_you_do: Join a student team that protects the Chattahoochee River. In the school year you do cleanups and talk to peers about the river. In summer, high schoolers can shadow staff in the field and lab.
pay_detail: Not stated. The page describes service hours and does not mention pay or a cost.
duration: School-year program Oct 2026 to April 2027; summer shadowing for high schoolers (dates not stated)
deadline_text: 2026-27 application closed Monday Sept 21, 2026. Next cycle not posted.

name: Astro Ambassadors
what_you_do: Teens see how the Adler plans guest visits behind the scenes. They learn to lead hands-on science activities and share ideas with staff. Then they run the activities for guests on the museum floor.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: Spring 2027 session; length not stated
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2027 session open in early 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Far Horizons Teens
what_you_do: Teens join Adler researchers to study light pollution in and around Chicago. One long study looks at how light affects trees. Teens also make a science poster and give a talk.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: Spring 2027 session; length not stated
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2027 session open in early 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Art Institute of Chicago Teen Council
what_you_do: A group of 15 teens works with museum staff. They plan programs and tools that make the museum more welcoming and useful for Chicago-area youth. Members meet at the museum and go behind the scenes.
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state the rate.
duration: Sept 12, 2026 to June 12, 2027; most Saturdays at the museum, plus some Wednesday after-school virtual meetings; about 3 to 4 hours a week
deadline_text: The 2026-27 Teen Council application was open through June 30, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.

name: Art Institute of Chicago Teen Summer Internship
org: Art Institute of Chicago with After School Matters
what_you_do: Interns help with festivals, gallery tours and workshops. They meet museum workers and local artists. They also plan and host creative events for visitors.
pay_detail: Paid (the page says all internships are paid). Rate not stated.
duration: June to August
deadline_text: Applications open in the spring through After School Matters. Exact 2027 dates not posted.

name: College First (grades 11 and 12)
org: Chicago Botanic Garden, Science Career Continuum
what_you_do: Rising CPS juniors and seniors take a college-level environmental science class and get a mentor. They do a summer research project. Through the school year they get help with college applications. The job is paid, with school-year stipends.
pay_detail: A paycheck in summer and stipends during the school year. Rates not stated.
duration: 7 weeks in summer, then monthly meetings through the school year
deadline_text: Page says the application deadline is Tuesday, April 15 (no year shown).

name: Science First (grades 9 and 10)
org: Chicago Botanic Garden, Science Career Continuum
what_you_do: Rising CPS freshmen and sophomores spend four weeks at the Garden. They learn about nature, biology, ecology and environmental justice. They do group projects and show them to family and friends. Students are paid.
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state the rate. Program is free; transportation is provided.
duration: 4 weeks, daily at the Garden
deadline_text: Page says the application deadline is Tuesday, April 15 (no year shown).

name: Summer at Columbia
what_you_do: A four-week program for high school students. You take a freshman-level college class in the arts, media or communications. Your teachers work in those fields. Credits can count if you enroll at Columbia later.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,698, including courses and weekday lunch. Scholarships of up to 50% are available and all applicants are considered automatically.
duration: 4 weeks (June 29 to July 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 registration has closed. 2027 dates not posted.

name: High School Science and Digital Learning Internship
what_you_do: Each summer, 15 Chicago-area high school students pick a Field Museum scientist or expert. They do a 5-week research project. They also learn digital media, tech and career skills.
pay_detail: $17.25 per hour (2026 page)
duration: Mid-June to end of July, Monday to Thursday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. The page says to check back in early 2027 for next summer.

name: Chicago Green Ambassadors Summer Program
org: The Field Museum, Keller Science Action Center (Roots and Routes Initiative and Youth Conservation Action)
what_you_do: Paid summer interns link their neighborhoods with the Burnham Wildlife Corridor. It is a nature area on the south lakefront. Interns work on real problems in the environment and in the community.
pay_detail: Paid internship. The page does not state the rate.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Dates and application not posted on the program page.

name: Field Museum Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens greet visitors and share science stories. They help young kids in the Crown Family PlayLab and show real specimens at interpretive carts in Stanley Field Hall.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn volunteer hours.
duration: At least 10 days over the summer; finishing it lets you apply for year-round volunteering later
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Jan 2026 to Feb 28, 2026. Interviews late March or early April; final notice by May 8. The page says check back in early 2027.

name: Free Spirit Media Teen Programs
what_you_do: Teens learn screenwriting, editing, camera work, audio and acting. Programs run after school, in school and in summer. Teens also get job skills training.
pay_detail: Stipend for program completion, plus snacks and Ventra transit passes. Amount not stated.
duration: Fall 2026 programs run Sept 21 to Nov 20, 2026; also after-school, in-school and summer offerings
deadline_text: Fall 2026 programs: Sept 21 to Nov 20, 2026. Registration deadline not stated.

name: Genesys Works Chicago paid year-long internship
what_you_do: Juniors get 8 weeks of training in business and tech skills. In senior year they work a paid internship at a partner company for about 20 hours a week. The internship lasts a year. They also get college and career coaching.
pay_detail: Students earn $10,000 to $13,000 over the senior-year internship, per the national students page (no hourly rate given)
duration: 8 weeks of summer training (160 hours), then a school-year internship at about 20 hours a week
deadline_text: Students at partner schools apply in fall or winter of junior year and finish the process in spring. Exact 2026-27 dates not posted on the pages read.

name: Goodman Musical Theater Intensive
what_you_do: A free summer program. Teens train in acting, singing and dancing with professional musical theater artists. They perform in a show at the Goodman.
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Thursday 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (July 6 to Aug 10 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; callbacks were Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Goodman PlayBuild Youth Intensive
what_you_do: A free summer theater program. Teens learn acting, creative writing, improv and physical theater from pros. They create an original show about civic issues.
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Thursday 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 22 to July 27 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; callbacks were Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Goodman Youth Arts Council (GYAC)
what_you_do: CPS students use theater to talk about issues that young people face. They plan and run events by teens for teens. They learn from Goodman artists and staff, and they act as ambassadors for the theater.
pay_detail: Travel stipends available. No wages stated.
duration: Meets every other Wednesday, 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., at the Goodman (2025/26 schedule began Nov 5)
deadline_text: Applications for 2025/26 are closed. 2026/27 dates not posted on the page read.

name: RISE Teen Program
org: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry (MSI Chicago)
what_you_do: A free program where teens explore careers in science, tech, engineering, arts and math. You do hands-on projects, LEGO engineering challenges and panels with pros and mentors. You can join a 12-week session or drop in.
pay_detail: Free. Participants get free museum admission, free parking, and volunteer hours on request.
duration: Fall 2026 session: 12 Saturdays, Oct 3, 2026 to Jan 9, 2027, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
deadline_text: Registration for the Fall 2026 session has closed. Next session dates not posted.

name: Chicago Metro History Day
what_you_do: Students pick a topic that fits the yearly theme and research it like a historian. Then they make a website, show, film, paper or exhibit. Volunteers judge the projects at yearly contests in the Chicago area.
pay_detail: No fee or pay stated on the pages read
duration: School-year project; 2027 regional contest on Feb 27 (Senior Division, grades 9 to 12) at UIC Student Center East
deadline_text: 2027 theme: Innovation in History. Teacher intent form due Dec 1, 2026. Student project registration due Feb 10, 2027; upload due Feb 17, 2027. Regional contest Feb 27, 2027 (grades 9-12). Junior Division (grades 6-8) Mar 6, 2027. National contest June 13-17, 2027.

name: Camp Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Teen volunteers help counselors run Conservation Camp for young kids. They set up activities, join in and help make camp fun. They earn service hours and an EcoLeader certificate.
pay_detail: Unpaid service-learning. You get service hours.
duration: About 5 weeks: Session A June 8 to July 17, Session B July 13 to Aug 14 (2026), plus required training days in spring
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Conservation Ambassadors Board
org: Lincoln Park Zoo with After School Matters
what_you_do: Each semester, teens study one conservation topic in depth. Then they plan and carry out a project and share it with peers and the public. They build skills in leadership, research, speaking, event planning, promotion and money.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page. Ask Lincoln Park Zoo.
duration: Two terms a year, March to May and September to November; Saturday meetings (Feb 28 to May 9 in spring 2026)
deadline_text: Spring 2026 application opened Jan 20 and was due Feb 1. A fall term also runs. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Nature Buds Internship
org: Lincoln Park Zoo with After School Matters
what_you_do: Interns help run nature play for the zoo's youngest visitors. There is music, art, story time and sensory bins. Interns also help kids and the adults with them find their way around the zoo.
pay_detail: Stipend of $17.05 per hour through After School Matters (2026 page)
duration: June to August, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 application opened the week of April 27 on the After School Matters site. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Malott Family Research Apprenticeship Program
what_you_do: Apprentices work with zoo researchers on a real science question. They learn research methods in the field and on computers. At the end of summer they show their results at a poster session.
grades: Entering grades 11 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday (June 22 to Aug 7 in 2026), plus a Saturday orientation
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Malott Family Zoo Intern Program
what_you_do: Interns teach zoo guests about animals and conservation. They learn how to share conservation messages. They meet zoo researchers and animal care staff. They finish with a project they present.
grades: Entering grades 10 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday (June 22 to Aug 7 in 2026), plus a Saturday orientation
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Zoo Teens events
what_you_do: Free events just for teens, led by zoo experts. You can make conservation art, learn to live next to city wildlife like bats and birds, and play a role-playing game.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Single events on select days through the year
deadline_text: Events listed for Saturday Oct 31 (Roll for Wildlife, Prism Games, Logan Square) and Saturday Nov 7 (Plants and Prints, Lincoln Park Zoo). The page does not state the year. Register on the page.

name: Marwen Art@Work summer internship
what_you_do: Nearly 20 young people are hired for paid 5-week internships. The jobs are at arts groups and creative businesses. Interns also go to Marwen workshops. Topics are resumes, interviews, public speaking and money.
pay_detail: 2026: $16.20 per hour, 14.5 hours a week for 5 weeks, about $1,174.50 before taxes (may change)
duration: 5 weeks, July to August; 12 hours a week at the site and 2.5 hours at Marwen
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open in spring 2027. For 2026 they were due April 11, 2026.

name: Teen Creative Agency (TCA)
what_you_do: Chicago teens meet each week with two lead artists. They spend time in the galleries and at other culture sites. They make art projects and public events, including the yearly teen show called 21Minus.
pay_detail: Up to $1,600 a year
duration: Weekly sessions during the program year; exact months not stated
deadline_text: Applications for TCA open next spring (spring 2027). Exact dates not posted.

name: CPS Student Advisory Council (Mikva Challenge)
what_you_do: Students from 20+ Chicago schools meet with CPS leaders. They gather ideas from peers and do research. Then they write advice on school issues. Past groups spoke to the CPS Board.
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program pages. Ask Mikva Challenge.
duration: Summer council with policy work; exact length not stated
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Safety and Justice Council (Mikva Challenge)
what_you_do: Youth who live in Chicago or Cook County give advice to the Cook County Board President. They talk about youth justice, safety in the community and holding police responsible. They write advice each year.
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Mikva Student Election Judge Program
org: Mikva Challenge Illinois with Chicago election officials
what_you_do: High school juniors and seniors work at polling places on Election Day. They do the same jobs as adult judges. They help voters, run the machines and close the polls.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.
duration: One election day, before the polls open until after they close
deadline_text: Each election cycle. No dates posted on the page.

name: Mikva Summer Fellows
org: Mikva Challenge Illinois with the Illinois Department of Human Services Youth Investment Program
what_you_do: Fellows work for six weeks in the offices of city, county, state and federal leaders. They also go to weekly workshops on leadership, setting goals and job skills.
grades: Placed after senior year of high school
pay_detail: $17 per hour, 30 hours a week
duration: 6 weeks between June and August
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Teen Health Council (Mikva Challenge)
what_you_do: Teens study the physical, mental and sexual health of Chicago youth. They make action plans. They share ideas with the Chicago Department of Public Health and CPS. They also learn about public health careers.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.
duration: Not stated; policy work happens over the summer in past years
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
what_you_do: This is a mentoring and job-readiness program for 13 to 15 year olds. Teens help with park programs. Programs include sports, games, nature and arts and crafts. You build leadership, communication and customer service skills.
pay_detail: The program page does not mention pay or a stipend. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around pay.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
what_you_do: Teens 16 and up can work in the parks. Jobs include lifeguard and day camp recreation leader. You can also be a special recreation leader. Those camps serve kids and adults with intellectual disabilities. Junior laborers do landscape work.
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.

name: Rush University Medical Center volunteer program
what_you_do: Volunteers greet visitors and walk them to where they need to go. They push wheelchairs, deliver flowers and mail, visit with patients and help with events. After six months you can apply for a role in one department.
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 100 hours you can ask a staff member for a reference letter.
duration: At least 6 months, 4 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis.

name: SAIC Early College Program (ECP) courses
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
what_you_do: High school students take art and design classes in fall, spring or summer. Examples are figure drawing, animation, fashion and comics. You build work for your portfolio for art school.
grades: High school; college credit only for those who finished sophomore year
pay_detail: Noncredit 10-week course $661; 1.0 college credit course $1,982; supplies about $50 to $200 extra. The Smith Scholarship covers 100% of noncredit course tuition for Illinois students. Limited need-based aid.
duration: 10-week courses in fall and spring; the page does not state a summer course length
deadline_text: Register online for each term. No fixed deadline stated on the pages read.

name: SAIC Early College Program Summer Institute (ECPSI)
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
what_you_do: Intensive 1, 2 or 4-week summer art and design courses at SAIC. Students earn one college credit for each week attended.
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,908 for 1 week, $3,816 for 2 weeks and $7,632 for 4 weeks. The page also lists housing and meal plan costs, supplies and personal spending. A $100 non-refundable tuition deposit applies to students who apply for aid or scholarships. Merit scholarships and limited need-based aid (US residents) are offered.
duration: 1, 2 or 4 weeks. 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31.
deadline_text: Page says registration opens November 1 (year not stated). The 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31. A priority deadline is mentioned but not dated on the page read.

name: Steppenwolf Young Adult Council
what_you_do: 30 high school students meet every Wednesday to learn how a big theater works. They see plays, join workshops with theater artists, and plan teen nights with the ensemble.
pay_detail: Weekly meetings appear unpaid; the page says community engagement and extra leadership work is paid. Rates not stated.
duration: Weekly Wednesday meetings at Steppenwolf
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. Next dates not posted.

name: CPS-UChicago Program
org: University of Chicago with Chicago Public Schools
what_you_do: Advanced CPS juniors and seniors take one college class each quarter at the University of Chicago. They sit in class with UChicago students. The classes go on the CPS transcript.
pay_detail: $800 tuition plus $75 lifetime transcript fee (books not included) if household income is over $60,000. $0 tuition, with books and fees covered, if under $60,000.
duration: Autumn, Winter and Spring Quarters; one course per quarter
deadline_text: For 2026-27 the application opened June 8, 2026 and closed July 15, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.

name: Chicago EYES on Cancer
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
what_you_do: Students work full time in a University of Chicago cancer research lab for two summers. They also get monthly career workshops, talks and mentors. They present at a research event.
grades: High school sophomore, junior or senior (or college freshman or sophomore)
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $5,000 per year
duration: Two summers of 8 weeks (2027: June 14 to Aug 6, 35 to 40 hours a week) plus monthly 2 to 4 hour online sessions from Feb 2027 to Dec 2028
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Nov 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. In-person interviews Jan 4, 2027.

name: Healthcare Experience and Research in Oncology (HERO)
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
what_you_do: A two-week online program where high school students work on a cancer genetics project and a patient case study, hear daily faculty talks and build skills. Students get a home lab kit.
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend
duration: 2 weeks, July 12 to 23, 2027, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to noon CT, online
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Mar 1, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Interviews in April 2027.

name: UChicago Medicine student volunteer program
what_you_do: Student volunteers help patients, families and visitors in the hospital. They welcome people and visit with patients. They help families find their way. Roles include Child Life and patient comfort teams.
grades: High school, college and graduate students
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for at least 6 months or one school year; 100 hours within a year
deadline_text: Fall window ran Aug 25 to Oct 1, 2026 (may close early). Next cycle starts Jan 10, 2027; closing date not posted.

name: researcHStart
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center with UIC, UIUC, Northwestern and Rush
what_you_do: High school students spend 8 weeks in a cancer research lab. They work 35 to 40 hours a week. The lab is at one of five Illinois universities. Students also get career workshops and mentors.
grades: High school junior or senior at time of application
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $4,000
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027, 35 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Jan 11, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. On-campus interviews in February 2027; acceptance notices March 1, 2027.

name: University of Chicago Summer Session pre-college programs
what_you_do: High school students take college-level courses in person (live on campus or commute) or online. Choices run from short programs to research courses. Examples are lab biology or fieldwork with Field Museum fossil experts.
grades: High school (programs open depend on your current grade)
pay_detail: Costs in 2026: Enrichment $3,000; Career Insight $5,890 ($4,100 commuting); Immersion $9,300 ($6,100 commuting); Practicum $15,200; online 3 to 5 weeks $4,980. Need-based partial aid is offered (not full), and Enrichment fees can be waived for income under $125,000. $75 application fee.
duration: Varies by program. Online courses run 3 to 5 weeks and the language institute runs 6 to 8 weeks; the page does not state a length for enrichment.
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines: priority Feb 11, regular Mar 12 (Practicum priority only). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Windy City Harvest Youth Farm
org: Chicago Botanic Garden, Windy City Harvest, with After School Matters
what_you_do: Teens grow food on urban farms, tend beehives, cook with what they grow, and sell it at farm stands and markets. They build leadership and job skills and explore careers in food and farming.
pay_detail: Stipend: 4 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 hours a week in summer. Rate not stated.
duration: Spring, summer and fall growing seasons
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
what_you_do: The City runs a summer youth jobs program. It places young people in paid jobs. Partners include the Park District, CPS and City Colleges. Others are the Chicago Housing Authority, the Forest Preserves and Lincoln Park Zoo.
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
what_you_do: This is a six-week summer program. It has workforce training, financial literacy training and career exploration. It has 120 hours of activities. You make a resume. You sign up for direct deposit.
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
what_you_do: Volunteer in a children's hospital over the summer, at least one 3-hour shift a week for eight weeks. Placements are at Arthur M. Blank, Hughes Spalding or Scottish Rite hospitals.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
what_you_do: You can join an Explorer post for teens who want a law enforcement career. You get training and mentoring from CHP officers.
deadline_text: Rolling.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)
what_you_do: You serve patients and visitors. You support hospital staff. You explore health care careers. You work one 4 hour shift each week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Three cycles a year: summer apply by April 30, fall by August 30, spring by December 30. The page lists month and day only, no year.

name: Living Coast Discovery Center Volunteer (ages 16 to 17)
what_you_do: Help at a nature center and wildlife rescue by supporting events, working on the grounds and in the office, and later in animal care. Orientations are held on weekends.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Ongoing, based on availability. In animal care, 3 absences within 60 days may result in losing your spot.
deadline_text: Accepted on a rolling basis. Orientations are on alternating Saturdays and Sundays at 10 a.m. each month.

name: 10x10 Teen Volunteer Team (Cincinnati Art Museum)
what_you_do: Help plan the 10x10 Teen Art Expo, a week long exhibition of more than 100 teen artists from the greater Cincinnati region. The team picks the theme that artists use for their 10 by 10 inch pieces and meets monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer team
duration: The team meets 4 to 6 p.m. on the first Thursday of each month plus extra dates as needed, and must be free for the opening on Saturday April 10, 2027. The exhibition runs April 6 to 11, 2027.
deadline_text: Volunteer applications for the 2026 to 27 team were due Friday September 4, 2026, with replies by September 11. Next year's dates are not posted.

name: Teen Workforce Development (Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati
what_you_do: Join the Clubs' teen Workforce Development programming. You explore careers with local businesses. You also explore careers with universities, trades and the military. You learn about money. You get ready for jobs. Driver's education is part of it too.
pay_detail: Free. The summer and school year programs are listed as completely free. The page does not say that teens are paid.
duration: Summer: June 1 to July 31, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. School year: August 17 to May 14, Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 7:30 p.m. (hours vary by Club).
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Enroll through the Club member portal.

name: High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You complete tasks under hospital staff supervision. This is in the pediatric setting. You work a 2 to 3 hour shift each week. You build teamwork and leadership skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
deadline_text: The deadline for the Summer 2026 session has passed. The page says the summer application is usually posted in January, with about two months to finish the packet.

name: Aquatics Jobs: Lifeguard and Pool Staff
what_you_do: You can work part-time or seasonal jobs at Cincinnati public pools. Lifeguards keep pool users safe. Gate and pool monitors handle customer service. They also watch behavior around the pool.
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. A 2026 lifeguard screening registration form is linked.

name: Youth to Work (Y2WK) Summer Jobs
what_you_do: You work a summer job with City departments or nonprofit partners. Examples include recreation centers, pools, parks, fire and police cadets. There are workshops on workplace etiquette and basic work skills.
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the pages read
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
deadline_text: The program page says the application is usually available February to March. In 2026 the deadline passed in March (WVXU reported about two weeks left on March 10, 2026). 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Teen Volunteers (Great Parks of Hamilton County)
what_you_do: Volunteer long term in parks. Jobs include habitat restoration, education programs and special events. You can work on golf course upkeep. You can grow native plants or garden. You can also care for animals. Role training and uniforms are provided.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Long term volunteering. Time commitment is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Long term volunteer information sessions have ended for 2026. Great Parks says it will host them again in March 2027.

name: Library Volunteer Opportunities (ages 12+)
what_you_do: You can volunteer at the Main Library or a branch. You can help with kids and teen events. You can also help with holds, clerical work, technology help and tutoring.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week
deadline_text: The library volunteer system says it is accepting new volunteer applications. No deadline is posted.

name: Youth Programs Volunteers
what_you_do: Greet visitors, help guests find their way and cover the museums' gallery spaces, working with museum teams. Teens set their own shifts and can stay until they graduate.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
deadline_text: Youth volunteers are recruited each year from January through March. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Youth Volunteer Opportunities (Cincinnati Nature Center)
what_you_do: Help collect data on the maple trees in the sugarbush during maple season. Help tidy the grounds in early spring. Teens ages 14 to 17 can also be Leaders in Training. They help camp counselors, including on nature hikes.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Seasonal work tied to maple season and early spring. The time commitment is not stated.
deadline_text: The volunteer page says recruiting and onboarding is closed for the 2026 season and to check back in the new year for 2027 dates.

name: Green Team Youth Summer Jobs
org: Groundwork Ohio River Valley with Cincinnati Parks
what_you_do: You improve and maintain trails, parks and community spaces. You remove invasive plants. You learn job readiness and natural resource skills. These skills help in the green industry.
pay_detail: Paid summer job; rate not stated
duration: Summer; length not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the pages read. The City post is undated.

name: Job Shadowing (TriHealth)
what_you_do: Follow a TriHealth staff member for a short look at the job. It is usually about 8 to 16 hours. Shadowing is observation only. You cannot talk with patients in a hands-on way or see their medical records.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned on the page.
duration: Typically about 8 to 16 hours (varies by department or unit)
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted. Check with the program.

name: Early IT Summer Camp (University of Cincinnati)
org: University of Cincinnati School of Information Technology
what_you_do: Attend a free, in person day camp on UC's main campus. Learn cybersecurity, software development, game development and data and cloud technologies. Hear from IT leaders. Build a team project with a college student mentor.
pay_detail: Free to attend. A light breakfast and lunch are provided each day. No pay.
duration: Three weeks, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The page lists June 1 to June 18 and does not print the year.
deadline_text: The camp page says registration is open and that the camp is first come, first served and spots fill up fast. It does not print a deadline or the year, so confirm the dates with the Early IT team.

name: Medical Sciences Summer Institute (University of Cincinnati)
org: University of Cincinnati College of Medicine
what_you_do: Take a week long, full day workshop at the UC College of Medicine. It is for rising high school juniors and seniors. They should be interested in medicine or health care. Tracks are Cellular or Molecular, plus one Medical Informatics session.
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: $1,100 (2026 price). A limited number of scholarships and financial aid awards are available.
duration: One week per session, Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. In 2026 there were five sessions between June 1 and June 26.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: ZooTeen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You volunteer at the Zoo for the summer. This includes one week of ZooTeen camp. It also includes Visitor Engagement shifts. You also join Lunch and Learns and events.
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application is open online Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027. Information sessions Nov 16, Dec 14 and Jan 11 (6 to 7 p.m.). Group interviews Feb 27, Feb 28, Mar 13 or Mar 14. Decisions by email April 2, 2027.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (California Wing)
org: Civil Air Patrol, California Wing (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
city: California (squadrons in eight regional groups, Los Angeles to San Diego)
what_you_do: Cadets join a local squadron for weekly meetings. They learn leadership, aerospace and fitness. They can take orientation flights and go to events and an encampment.
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available.
duration: Ongoing; weekly squadron meetings
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend about three meetings, then complete the application.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (Georgia Wing)
org: Civil Air Patrol, Georgia Wing (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
city: Georgia (squadrons across the state; wing office at Dobbins Air Reserve Base, Marietta, GA)
what_you_do: Cadets meet weekly at a local squadron. They learn leadership, aerospace and fitness. The national page says Saturday events are ideally once a month. There is one week-long encampment in summer.
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, per the national page. A very active cadet might spend about $300 to $600 in the first year before aid, with some help for uniforms and overnight fees.
duration: Ongoing. A weekly squadron meeting of about 2 hours, ideally one Saturday event per month, and one week-long encampment in summer (national page).
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron and attend at least three meetings.

name: FARMS Leadership Program
what_you_do: You are in a school-year group. The group visits farms, conservation sites, agriculture businesses and colleges. There are at least six field days. You build resume, interview and speaking skills.
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.

name: Urban Ag Internships
what_you_do: You get a year-long paid internship at a school garden. It includes weekly garden hours, a workforce class, field trips to farms and guest speakers.
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.
duration: year-long
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.

name: Cobb Youth Leadership (CYL)
what_you_do: Six evening sessions and one overnight retreat. You meet local, state and national leaders. Topics include community service, arts and the armed forces. Others are business and ethics. You also learn about career paths.
pay_detail: $850 tuition for selected students. The page says financial help is accepted for those who cannot pay.
duration: Aug to April: orientation, fall retreat and 7 sessions (2026-27 class)
deadline_text: 2026-27 class: orientation Aug 17, 2026, retreat Sept 12-13, evenings Oct 14, Oct 26, Nov 16, Dec 7, Jan 25, Feb 22, Mar 22, graduation Apr 19, 2027. Next application dates are not posted.

name: Cobb County Police Cadet Program (Post #5)
what_you_do: Weekly training in criminal law, crime scene work, gun safety, patrol and traffic control. You help at community events. You also compete in cadet contests.
pay_detail: Volunteer program. No fees are listed. The Post raises money to attend national contests.
duration: Weekly meetings: Thursdays 6 to 8 pm in the school year, 6 to 9 pm in summer
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Dates, times and places may change.

name: Cobb County Public Library Volunteers

duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.
deadline_text: Year-round. No application dates are posted.

name: College of San Mateo Dual Enrollment and Concurrent Enrollment

deadline_text: No application deadline stated on the pages read.

name: College Park Composite Squadron, Civil Air Patrol cadets

name: Shakespeare in the Parks Apprenticeship Program
org: Prince George's County Parks and Recreation (M-NCPPC)

pay_detail: Paid apprenticeship. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

deadline_text: Deadline to apply: March 1, 2027.

org: Prince George's County Parks and Recreation (M-NCPPC)

duration: Eight months, October 2026 to June 2027, with meetings every two weeks
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026 to 27 term ran Aug 1 to Oct 4, 2026 and are closed. Expect a similar August to early October window next year.

org: Prince George's County Parks and Recreation (M-NCPPC)

name: Discovering Engineering (University of Maryland)
org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering
what_you_do: Stay on campus for a week of lab work, demos, lectures and a team design project. You visit each of the eight engineering departments. Only 25 to 30 students are accepted per session.

deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was April 24, 2026, with notices by May 15. The 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Pre-College Scholars Program (University of Maryland)
org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering
what_you_do: Spend three weeks on the UMD campus. You get about 38 hours of SAT prep and 11 hours of college prep. You also hear department talks and join admissions and financial aid workshops. You get one on one help with college applications.
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (currently in 10th or 11th grade)
pay_detail: The whole program costs $400 per student. Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.

deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday May 8, 2026, with notices by May 22 and rolling spots after that. The 2027 dates are not posted.

name: SPARC Robotics Certificate Program (University of Maryland)
org: Maryland Robotics Center, University of Maryland
what_you_do: Take a three week robotics session. You need no robotics experience. It is for commuters. Topics include drones and 3D nanoprinting. Others are autonomous ground vehicles and soft medical robotics. You earn a non-credit SPARC certificate.
pay_detail: The Summer 2026 price was $5,000 for one 3 week session (project materials and activities; lunch and transportation are not included). The 2027 price is not posted. A limited number of need based scholarships are available, and payments are not refundable.

deadline_text: Application deadline: December 1, 2026. The 2027 topics will be announced soon.

org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering (Women in Engineering Program)

pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)

name: East Bay Regional Park District Youth and Student Jobs
city: Oakland, CA and parks across Alameda and Contra Costa counties

deadline_text: No jobs were posted on governmentjobs.com on Oct 7, 2026. Watch ebparks.org/jobs/youth and governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks.

pay_detail: Free federally funded program. No pay or stipend is mentioned.

what_you_do: This is free college prep for high school students. It includes advising, educational workshops and tutoring. It also includes field trips and college courses. You get fee waivers for college applications and SAT/ACT.

duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the page.

deadline_text: No dates on the Ecology Center page. Berkeley YouthWorks listed a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026 and said Summer 2027 information comes in Feb 2027, but that page does not mention this academy.

name: Foothill College High School Dual Enrollment
city: Los Altos Hills and Sunnyvale, CA
what_you_do: Take real Foothill College classes for college and high school credit while in high school, on campus, online, or at Sunnyvale Center. Free up to 11 units a quarter.
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.
duration: One quarter at a time
deadline_text: No single deadline stated. Submit the form before you register each quarter.

name: Forage Virtual Job Simulations
what_you_do: Free, self-paced online job simulations. They copy real work tasks. You can compare your answers to model answers. There are over 250 simulations from more than 90 employers.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Self-paced, usually a few hours
deadline_text: Always open.

name: Orange Coast Medical Center Volunteer
what_you_do: Volunteer in the hospital as part of the patient care team. You work in service areas. After an interview, the Volunteer Office finds you an opening.
pay_detail: Unpaid. If accepted you pay a $25 registration fee.
duration: 150 hours per year
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

duration: Seasonal and part-time
pay_detail: Pay is listed on each posting. It is not on the main employment page.
name: Seasonal and Part-Time Park District Jobs
what_you_do: Apply online for seasonal and part-time park district jobs. The page says positions range from teens seeking a first job to highly skilled professionals.
deadline_text: Postings go up through the year. The district holds an annual job fair in late winter. Past press releases gave Saturday, Feb. 22 (posted February 18, 2020, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., Prisco Community Center) and Saturday, March 11 (posted February 24, 2023, 9 a.m. to noon, Prisco). 2027 date not posted.

grades: Middle school, high school and college students
duration: One-day projects or monthly clean-ups (Adopt-A-Park runs April to September, or May to October)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
name: Volunteer Opportunities for Teens and School Groups
what_you_do: Join park clean-ups, adopt a park or trail, and help at events. The district welcomes middle school, high school and college students and school clubs, and says the hours can count toward service requirements.
deadline_text: No deadline. The Fall Day of Service was October 3, 2026. Adopt-A-Park runs April to September (or May to October).

name: Teen Corps
org: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
what_you_do: You grow produce in a community garden. You sell it at the Conservatory's Farmers Market. You learn plant care, healthy eating, running a business and speaking skills.
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)
duration: Summer program; length not stated
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 Teen Corps are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Conservatory Volunteer Program (age 15+)
org: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
what_you_do: You can help the horticulture, education or visitor experience teams. Tasks include weeding and planting. You can also help in the Children's Garden or at the Farmers Market.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: No minimum hours; weekly, monthly or seasonal
deadline_text: Opportunities are available year-round. No deadline is posted.

name: Fremont Unified Career and Technical Education
what_you_do: You can take career and technical education classes at Fremont Unified middle and high schools in 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. Some are inside California Partnership Academies or regional occupational programs.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No dates stated. Choose courses at your school.

name: Fremont Youth Advisory Commission
what_you_do: You raise issues that matter to teens and pass them to the City Council. You also help plan forums and workshops for other teens.
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.

name: Fullerton Library Teen Volunteer and Teen Advisory Board
what_you_do: Join the Teen Advisory Board to plan library programs and events. Or write book reviews for the library website. Each Board meeting you attend earns 1 hour of volunteer service. So does each approved review.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer service hours (1 hour per meeting or approved review).
duration: Board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m. (starting Sept 1, 2026)
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: St. Jude Medical Center High School Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Do clerical, non-clinical hospital tasks. The page gives examples for its medical units, such as answering phones and checking on patient needs, but does not list tasks for high school students. You work one 3-hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Minimum one year and 140 hours a year. Shifts: Mon to Fri 4 to 7 p.m. or weekends 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
deadline_text: The page says high school applications may open in early 2027. Spaces are limited and applications are only taken when there are openings.

name: CONNECTED Youth Leadership Program (CYLP)
org: Fulton County Government, Community Development (with 21st Century Leaders)
what_you_do: Do a year of online and live leadership training. You explore careers, plan your education path and meet other teens and professionals. Juniors and seniors can get paid summer internships.
pay_detail: Free to join. Members can win gift cards from $25 to $100 and other prizes. The page lists paid summer internships for juniors and seniors but gives no pay rate.
duration: One school year (2026-27 program)
deadline_text: 2026-27 enrollment ran Sept 14 to 28, 2026. Next enrollment dates not posted.

name: Teen Volunteers (Fulton County Library System)
org: Fulton County Library System (Atlanta-Fulton Public Library)
what_you_do: Help library branches with 1 to 2 hour shifts. Tasks include shelving and clerical work. They also include crowd control at events and helping the Friends of the Library. Some branches have Teen Advisory Boards.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts after orientation
deadline_text: Applications are always accepted, but most projects are full and most locations have a waitlist.

name: Marshal's Junior Deputy Program
what_you_do: Spend one summer week learning life skills and getting a close look at law enforcement careers.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost not listed.
duration: 1 week (June 23 to 27 in 2025)
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday June 13, 2025 at close of business; program ran June 23 to 27, 2025. 2026 and 2027 dates not posted.

name: Work-Based Learning, Fulton County Schools
what_you_do: Juniors and seniors earn high school credit. They work under supervision at an approved job site. This can be an internship, an apprenticeship or a clinical experience. The job must match the student's career pathway.
pay_detail: School credit. The district page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: Per school term
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator for the application window.

name: Fulton County Youth Commission
what_you_do: Serve as a Youth Commissioner. You share what teens think with the Fulton County Board of Commissioners. You give it advice. You also join planning meetings and community service projects.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The page does not mention a stipend.
duration: School year. Up to 20 hours a month for planning meetings and projects (over 120 hours a year).
deadline_text: The page says applications are usually open in May near the end of the school year. A past call (2024-25 term) closed May 24, 2024. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Teen Volunteers at Gail Borden Public Library
what_you_do: You help with library events. You refresh library spaces. You prepare crafts for programs. Listed sessions include Cleaning the Classics, Knitting for a Cause and Crafting for the Community.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A teen volunteer orientation is listed for Sunday, Oct 18, 1:00 to 1:30 PM at the Main Library Conference Room (the page does not print the year; Oct 18 is a Sunday in 2026).

name: Work-Based Learning (Internships), Gwinnett County Public Schools
what_you_do: Juniors and seniors work in a job linked to their career goal and earn school credit. The program also covers apprenticeships. Students must job search and interview themselves, with help from the school coordinator.
pay_detail: School credit. The GCPS page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: One semester at a time as a school elective
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Forms go to your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator; ask when the next semester deadline is.

name: Genesys Works Bay Area Internship Program
what_you_do: You take eight weeks of business technology and job skills training, then work a paid, year-long internship at a partner company. You also get college and career coaching.
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
deadline_text: No dates posted. Applicants get an interview, then summer skills training.

name: Volunteens at Geneva Public Library
what_you_do: Volunteer for library tasks. After you register, the library emails sign-up sheets showing when help is needed and you choose time slots that fit your schedule.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
deadline_text: Fall 2026 session runs Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026. No registration deadline is listed. Dates for the next session are not posted.

grades: Ages 8 to 18 (Senior Project Achievement is grades 9 to 12)
name: Georgia 4-H
city: Georgia (county Extension offices statewide; state office in Athens, GA)
what_you_do: Join clubs, camps and projects in farming, science, civics, leadership and health. Older teens can join Project Achievement contests. They can join state conferences and leadership programs.
pay_detail: Not a job. The page says 4-H does not require a uniform or club fees. Camps and some activities may have their own costs, not listed on this page.
duration: Ongoing; clubs, projects, camps and conferences run through the year
deadline_text: No enrollment dates listed. Ask your county Extension office.

name: Teen Volunteer Program (Georgia Aquarium)
what_you_do: Start as a Gallery Guide: talk with visitors, help at the touch pools, and in summer spend a week helping with Camp H2O. Finish with a group community project.
pay_detail: Unpaid. $45 administrative fee (check or money order) once accepted. Perks: volunteer pass, free parking on shifts, 5 one-time daily tickets after finishing.
duration: 4 months per session: Spring (Jan to Apr) 60 hours, Summer (May to Aug) 80 hours, Fall (Sep to Dec) 60 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 session starts onboarding with information sessions in October 2026; dates not posted yet. The 2026 summer/fall cycle on the page: info sessions in July, application deadline Aug 1, interviews Aug 16, orientation Sept 12.

name: Georgia Boys State (American Legion)
what_you_do: This is a week-long program. Young men run a pretend 51st state. It has cities, counties, two parties, elections and lawmaking. You learn how Georgia government works.
pay_detail: Not a job. The 2026 memo says delegates pay a one time $5.00 'state tax' at registration. The sponsoring Legion post handles transportation. The page does not list a program fee.
duration: One week. 2026 session was June 7 to 13, 2026, about 400 delegates.
deadline_text: 2027 information is listed as 'coming soon'. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 13, 2026. The 2026 memo says the Samsung scholarship application was due online by the first day of the program.

grades: Not stated on the pages read
name: Georgia DECA
what_you_do: Join a school DECA chapter to prepare for college and careers. Members go to conferences, compete in DECA's competitive events and can earn a share of scholarships. The state hosts events like a Fall Rally.
pay_detail: Not a job. Student dues are $16 ($8 national and $8 state), per the state page.
duration: Membership is for one school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed. The state calendar lists a Fall Rally on October 21, 2026 at Six Flags Over Georgia.

grades: Not stated on the page read
name: Georgia FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
what_you_do: Join a school business club. It has learning programs and contests. It has state projects. It offers scholarships and awards. It also has state and national conferences.
pay_detail: Not a job. Dues are not listed on the page read.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed on the page.

grades: Students enrolled in a Georgia agricultural education class (middle and high school)
name: Georgia FFA Association
org: Georgia FFA Association and Georgia Agricultural Education (Georgia Department of Education)
what_you_do: Take agriculture classes at school and join FFA: leadership contests, career development events, Supervised Agricultural Experience projects, and state and national conventions.
pay_detail: Not a job. The membership page lists a yearly affiliation fee of $9.05 per high school student ($5.05 national, $4.00 state) and $900 per chapter for middle school. The page does not say whether families pay it.
duration: Ongoing during the school year
deadline_text: No membership deadline listed on the page. Enrollment follows your agriculture class schedule.

grades: Girls who have completed their junior year of high school
name: Georgia Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Georgia
what_you_do: This is a week-long program. Girls run a pretend state government. They hold elections, write bills and hear guest speakers. You learn how city, county and state government work.
pay_detail: $350.00 registration fee, usually paid by the sponsoring unit or organization. The page says sponsors are listed for each girl.
duration: About one week. 2026 session was June 7 to 12, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: the 'I Want In' page said fee due April 20 and applications complete by May 20, 2026, while the Selection Criteria page said applications and fee due May 1, 2026. The two pages disagree, so plan for the earlier date and ask your unit. 2027 dates not posted.

grades: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors)
name: Georgia Governor's Honors Program (GHP)
org: Georgia Governor's Office of Education, Workforce and Strategy (GOEWS)
city: Georgia (summer residential campus; host campus not named on the page read)
what_you_do: This is a mid-summer residential program on a college campus. It is for talented sophomores and juniors. Students study an area they were nominated in. It can be a subject, an art or a career field.
pay_detail: Free to apply. The page says required costs are travel to the semifinalist event and the host campus, basic supplies and optional spending money. Meals and rooms are provided.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July (residential)
deadline_text: Local school selection runs August to early November (ask your school's GHP Coordinator now). Then nominees get the online application link Nov 13, info session Dec 3, application due Jan 8, semifinalists told Feb 5. The page shows weekdays but no year; they match 2026 to 2027. Confirm with GHP.

name: Georgia Senate Page Program
org: Georgia State Senate (Office of the Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of the Senate)
what_you_do: Serve for one legislative day at the State Capitol. Pages carry messages to senators on the Senate floor. They also watch votes and meet lawmakers.
pay_detail: $20.00 honorarium paid at the end of the day, plus a certificate of service (2025 welcome packet).
duration: One legislative day. Report about 1.5 hours before the Senate convenes. The Senate usually convenes at 10:00 AM (check the Senate schedule the night before).
deadline_text: No application deadline found. Pages choose a legislative day while the General Assembly is in session. The packet says the first 20 days of session fall in January and February. 2027 dates not read.

name: Dual Enrollment at Georgia State University (Atlanta Campus)
org: Georgia State University, Office of Undergraduate Admissions
what_you_do: Take college classes at Georgia State while you finish high school. The classes count for college credit and for high school.
pay_detail: State funding (Georgia Student Finance Commission) pays tuition and mandatory fees for up to 15 credit hours a semester from the approved course list. You pay lab fees, supplies, meals and travel. Joint enrollment (not dual) is paid by the family.
duration: By semester: spring, summer and fall
deadline_text: Deadlines listed without a year: Spring Nov 1, Summer Apr 1, Fall May 1. Late applications are not guaranteed a decision.

name: Dual Enrollment at Georgia Tech
org: Georgia Institute of Technology, Office of Undergraduate Admission
city: Atlanta, GA (online and some on campus)
what_you_do: Take real Georgia Tech college courses while you are still in high school. Several courses are online (distance courses), and a limited number are on campus.
pay_detail: Most Georgia students get state funding that covers enrollment (30 credit hour limit). Self-pay in fall 2026 is $353.93 per credit hour for Georgia residents, plus fees ($531 for online-only).
duration: By term: fall, spring and summer (summer is distance computer science only)
deadline_text: Windows listed without years: Fall apply May 15 to June 15. Spring apply Sept 25 to Oct 20. Summer (distance CS only) apply March 1 to 31.

name: STEP: Science, Technology and Engineering Program (Georgia Tech Aerospace Engineering)
org: Georgia Tech Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering
what_you_do: You work in a team. Your team solves an open-ended engineering challenge. The challenge is inspired by real Georgia Tech research. You work with a faculty mentor. You present results at a poster session.
pay_detail: Free to students (funded by industry donors). No stipend stated. Students provide their own daily transportation.
duration: 2-week day program (not residential); Atlanta session July 6 to 17 in 2026
deadline_text: 2027 dates not posted.

name: Summer Engineering Institute (Georgia Tech College of Engineering)
what_you_do: This is a free, overnight summer program on the Georgia Tech campus. Students do hands-on experiments and workshops. They meet professors and students. They learn about admissions and tour campus.
pay_detail: Free to participants in 2026 (page wording). Participants stay on campus.
duration: 2026 session was June 7 to 15, 2026, overnight on campus
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026 session is closed. No application deadline is shown. Next session dates are not posted.

name: Georgia Work-Based Learning (including Youth Apprenticeship)
org: Georgia Department of Education, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education
what_you_do: This is a state program with four options. Cooperative education is paid. Internship is paid or unpaid. Youth Apprenticeship is paid. Employability Skill Development is for students who already have a job. All of them link school courses to a work site.
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
deadline_text: Set by each school or district. No state dates are posted.

name: WorkSource Georgia Youth (WIOA)
org: Technical College System of Georgia, Office of Workforce Development (WorkSource Georgia)
what_you_do: A state youth employment program run through local WorkSource offices. Services listed include tutoring, paid and unpaid work experiences, leadership development, adult mentoring, counseling, financial literacy and GED services.
pay_detail: Free to join. The services page lists paid and unpaid work experiences, but the pages read give no pay rate.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates listed on the state pages.

name: Teen Gallery Guides @ Getty
org: J. Paul Getty Museum (Getty Center and Getty Villa)
what_you_do: You research artworks. Then you lead tours. You also lead gallery activities for school groups and visitors. This is at the Getty Center or Getty Villa. You build public speaking and teaching skills.
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
deadline_text: The page says the application window typically opens in early February each year. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Girls Inc. of Alameda County High School Programs
city: Oakland, CA (and Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
what_you_do: You can join free programs for high school girls. They include coding, with Code the Game for grades 10 to 12. They also include college access and leadership. Some programs offer paid summer internships at Bay Area companies.
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact Girls Inc.

name: Girls Who Code Clubs and Pathways
what_you_do: You can join a free coding club for grades 3 to 12. It meets after school or on weekends. You can also take the free, self-paced online Pathways program for high school students.
grades: Clubs: grades 3 to 12 (split 3 to 5 and 6 to 12). Pathways: high school.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
deadline_text: Ongoing.

name: Glendale Community College Dual Enrollment and Jump Start
what_you_do: Take college classes while in high school. Dual Enrollment is for Glendale and Burbank school district students on an approved class list. Jump Start covers other students and other classes.
pay_detail: Costs and fee waivers are not stated on the page. Ask dual@glendale.edu.
duration: By term
deadline_text: Registration opens Oct 19, 2026 for Winter 2027 (Jump Start only) and Nov 30, 2026 for Spring 2027 (Dual Enrollment and Jump Start).

name: Glendale Youth Alliance STEP (Student Training and Employment Program)
what_you_do: Get work training at Glendale Community College's Professional Development Center. Then do 120 hours of paid work at a worksite. The site is picked to match your skills and interests.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.
duration: 120 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Glendale Youth Alliance Summer Youth Employment and Youth@Work
what_you_do: Youth ages 14 to 24 get life skills, pre-employment training and paid work experience. GYA's home page says it provides up to 200 hours of paid work experience in retail, clerical and field worksites.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.
duration: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines posted. Use the Apply Now form and expect a call back in 3 to 5 business days.

name: Glendale Youth Alliance TEAM (Training, Employment and Mentoring)
what_you_do: Job readiness and mentoring for low-income youth. You learn to be on time, dress right and follow through on tasks. This helps you get ready for college and work.
pay_detail: Not stated whether TEAM itself pays. GYA says its other youth programs include paid work experience.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Glenmont Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes nurse assistant. It includes culinary arts and facilities maintenance. HVAC is another. There are more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

grades: Youth volunteers: grades 6 to 12. Innovation Center: grades 9 to 12. Teen Advisory Board: grades 7 to 11.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: monthly meetings and 3 to 5 programs in a one year term
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
name: Youth Volunteers, Innovation Center Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Board
what_you_do: Help with children's programs as a school year youth volunteer. Or keep the Innovation Center tidy and learn its 3D printers, laser cutters and sewing machines. Or join the Teen Advisory Board. It plans library events.
deadline_text: School year youth volunteer applications opened August 15 and no close date is stated. Returning volunteers do not need to reapply. Teen Advisory Board applications are open November 1 to 30, and new members are told December 14 (no year printed on the page).

name: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
org: George Mason University, College of Science
what_you_do: You work full time for 8 weeks. You do a one-on-one research project with a George Mason faculty mentor. It can be in person, remote or hybrid. You present at a final poster session.
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.
duration: 8 weeks, full time (Jun 18 to Aug 12 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 ASSIP Application is now closed. The page posts no date for the 2027 cycle.

name: George Mason University High School Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Take lower-level college courses (100 and 200 level) at George Mason while still in high school and earn college credit. You can take up to 11 credits in one semester.
pay_detail: An application fee and college course costs apply. The amounts are not stated on the page read.
duration: One semester at a time, up to 11 lower-level credits
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the page read. Admission is offered for one semester at a time.

name: Youth Employment Services (Y.E.S.)
city: Decatur, GA and other north Georgia career centers
what_you_do: Set career goals, take job readiness classes and get paid work experience. You earn high school credit for the job readiness classes.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The page does not give a wage.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates posted. Email to apply.

name: Grafton Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes carpentry, electrical and plumbing. It includes certified nurse assistant. There are more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

name: Grizzly Youth Academy (National Guard Youth ChalleNGe)
org: California National Guard / California Military Department
city: San Luis Obispo, CA (residential; serves listed central and southern counties)
