what_you_do: A free, live in, structured program for teens who are behind in credits or at risk of dropping out. Cadets work on academics, leadership and life skills, and many can earn a GED.
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).
duration: Residential phase followed by a long check-in phase. The site's pages disagree on the total length (17.5 months on one page, 5.5 months residential plus 24 months after on another), so ask the academy.
deadline_text: No class start dates or deadlines on the pages read. Start with the online Interest Form and a required virtual orientation.

name: High School Summer Internship (Georgia Tech Research Institute)
city: Atlanta, GA; Cobb County; Warner Robins, GA (in person)
what_you_do: Five week paid, in person internship at a Georgia Tech Research Institute site. Interns work up to 24 hours a week on STEM projects with GTRI staff.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not on the page.
duration: Five weeks, about June 14 to July 23, 2027; up to 24 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: Pre-application launch is planned for December 11, 2026. The closing date is not listed on the page. The page says dates are approximate and final dates will be in the pre-application.

name: Empower Gwinnett Government Internship Program
what_you_do: Two Saturday workshops in May, then a four-week paid internship in a county department. The page says interns develop leadership skills through workshops and on-the-job training.
pay_detail: $15 per hour for the two workshops and the four-week internship
duration: 2 Saturday workshops plus 4 weeks (June)
deadline_text: Last cycle (2026 page): apply Feb 9 to Mar 16, workshops May 9 and May 16, internship June 1 to June 26. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Gwinnett Youth Police Academy
what_you_do: A free one-week academy with classroom lessons and hands-on activities. Topics include CPR and AED, emergency driving, and crime scene and crash work. You also learn self defense. You see K9, aviation and SWAT demos.
pay_detail: Free. The page says the academy is free.
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm
deadline_text: Last cycle: application deadline May 29, 2026. The next deadline is not posted.

name: Junior District Attorney and Investigator Mentorship Program
org: Gwinnett Judicial Circuit District Attorney's Office
what_you_do: Get a hands-on look at courts, police, jails and prosecutors. You work with assistant district attorneys and investigators. You also work with office staff. You can earn community service hours.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page says participants can earn community service hours.
duration: Length not stated
deadline_text: Applications for the sixth group open in April 2027 and the summer experience begins in June 2027. No deadline is posted.

name: Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Council (Gwinnett County Public Library)
what_you_do: Volunteer at a library branch. Your role fits the branch, such as helping with programs or homework help. Teen Advisory Council members meet monthly. They help plan teen activities.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: 40 hours over 6 to 12 months, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Apply any time. Applications stay on file for six months.

name: Gwinnett County Parks Lifeguard Jobs
org: Gwinnett County Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
what_you_do: Work as a part-time seasonal lifeguard at county pools and water centers. First you must pass an In-Water Skills Test. You also take the American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification course.
pay_detail: Pay is not listed on the page.
duration: Part-time seasonal jobs at the county's year-round aquatic centers and seasonal pools. Dates are not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.

name: Gwinnett Parks Summer Camp Aide (volunteer)
org: Gwinnett County Parks and Recreation / Community Services
what_you_do: Volunteer as an aide at a county day camp for kids ages 5 to 13 for at least two weeks. Follow the camp supervisor's directions. No phones while volunteering.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. $21 for two required camp t-shirts, paid after you are accepted.
duration: Minimum of two weeks, picked from camp weeks between late May and July 31
deadline_text: 2026 form: turn in by Monday, April 20 (2026 camp weeks: June 1 to June 26 and July 6 to July 24, plus May 26-29 and July 27-31 at the Environmental and Heritage Center only; no camp June 29 to July 3). The 2027 form is not posted.

name: Gwinnett County Police Explorer Post 1808
what_you_do: Classroom and hands-on training in traffic stops, investigations, crime scene work and self defense. Compete for Gwinnett in state and national contests. Help at community events.
pay_detail: One-time registration fee of $61. Not a paid job.
duration: Three Mondays a month, 6:30 to 9:00 pm, at the Police Training Center in Lawrenceville
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.

name: S.M.I.L.E. Gwinnett (Summer Mentoring in Legal Education)
what_you_do: Spend Friday afternoons in summer learning about the legal system. You do debates and mock trials and watch live court cases. You tour places like the Gwinnett County Detention Center and the medical examiner's office. It ends with a graduation.
pay_detail: Free to students
duration: Friday afternoons over the summer
deadline_text: Applications were closed for 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Volunteer Gwinnett Internship Program
what_you_do: A volunteer internship in a Gwinnett County department. The flyer lists communications, IT, law and public safety. It also lists recreation and water resources. Health and human services are listed too. There are more.
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer internship. Pay is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The county page says volunteer internships are available year-round. No deadline is listed.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
what_you_do: You help build or repair affordable homes on construction sites. Younger teens can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page
deadline_text: Ongoing. No sign-up deadline stated.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
what_you_do: You help build and repair homes on a job site. Or you work in the ReStore. There you organize, price and stock items. You go to a one hour orientation first. Training, tools and safety gear are provided.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)
deadline_text: Rolling. Sign up for shifts after orientation.

name: Hack Club
what_you_do: You can join Hack Club. It is a free teen coding community. It has school clubs and an online Slack. It has game jams, hackathons and hardware events.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join anytime.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
what_you_do: In October you can join online challenges and livestreams, or go to one of over 500 local in-person fests. This year the event focuses on open source and open-weight AI.
pay_detail: Free
duration: All of October 2026
deadline_text: Runs through October 2026; sign in with MyMLH.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)
what_you_do: You can join monthly volunteer projects for younger volunteers. Find them on the HandsOn Community Calendar. Filter by age to see which are open to you.
grades: High school (for HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Council)
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
deadline_text: Monthly projects: sign up on the Community Calendar. HandsOn Tomorrow will not run in summer 2026 and no later dates are posted.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
what_you_do: Teens do animal meet-and-greets, help with animal care routines and work as camp helpers. Good for future zookeepers and vet techs.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed seasonally. The last orientation listed on the page was Oct 18, 2025 (old); no 2026-27 date is posted.

name: Harvey Mudd College Summer Session (high school students welcome)
what_you_do: Take college courses with college students, in person or online. Subjects are computer science, engineering, math and arts. There are also classes in humanities and social science.
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,250 per 3-credit course and $5,000 per 4-credit course (2026 prices). Financial aid on the page is only for Harvey Mudd students.
duration: 2026 Session I began May 26 and Session II began June 15
deadline_text: For summer 2026, registration began March 2 and the application with transcript was due May 7. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.

name: H.A.R.D. Volunteer Program (Hayward Area Recreation and Park District)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
what_you_do: Volunteer at district events and ongoing service projects such as senior programs, nature programs, special needs programs and theatre ushering. Teens can earn community service hours and work experience.
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.
deadline_text: Opportunities are posted throughout the year. No closing date is stated on the page.

name: Hayward Public Library Teen Volunteer Opportunities
what_you_do: Teens help the Children's Room librarians with tasks like cleaning books and craft prep, in 1-hour shifts. Teens can also attend Teen Library Council meetings.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted during the school year. No closing date is stated on the page.

name: Hayward Youth Commission
what_you_do: Youth commissioners advise three groups. Those are the Hayward City Council, the Hayward Area Recreation and Park District and the Hayward Unified School District. They advise on issues that affect young people. They also work on youth projects.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall on the second Monday of each month, September to June, except holidays. The 2021 notice said two-year terms.
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday, May 9, 2025. Interviews were on Friday, May 30, 2025. No 2026 cycle was found.

name: STEAM Squad teen internship
what_you_do: Teen interns work in teams of three. They research and plan activities. They lead science, technology, engineering, art and math activities. These are for kids at participating libraries.
pay_detail: Described as a hired position; the pay rate is not stated on the page
duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
deadline_text: Hiring dates are not stated. Sign up for Hennepin County job notifications to be told about openings.

name: Teen volunteers
what_you_do: Help at a local Hennepin County library. Positions vary by library.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Ask your local library whether it has a teen opening.

name: Hidden Genius Project Immersion Program
what_you_do: You can join a free 15 month program (800+ hours) for Black male high school students. It has two 7-week summers plus a year of after-school sessions in coding, entrepreneurship and leadership.
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed
duration: 15 months
deadline_text: The application page says applications are currently closed and to follow HGP social media or the newsletter for the 2027 application. The last posted deadline was Feb 21, 2025.

name: Teen Leadership Council (High Museum of Art)
what_you_do: Join 15 high school students. You learn about art and how a museum works. You talk with artists and tour the collection. You help with public programs. You plan events for other teens.
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
deadline_text: 2026-27 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed at midnight March 1 (2026); applicants were told by May 1, 2026. The page does not post the 2027-28 cycle.

name: Hiller Aviation Museum Flight Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens run hands-on STEM stations like Imagination Playground and virtual reality for visitors on alternating weekend days.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
deadline_text: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

name: Hire LA's Youth
org: City of Los Angeles Economic and Workforce Development Department (EWDD)
what_you_do: Get a starter job with work-skills training, career coaching and money lessons. One sub-program puts high school students to work helping elementary kids in LA's BEST after-school programs.
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
deadline_text: The site banner says it is accepting applications but gives no dates, and its document library page still shows a 2022 summer banner. Call EWDD at 213-744-7300 to confirm the current cycle.

name: Hoag Jr. Auxiliary / Candystripers (High School Volunteer)
what_you_do: You greet visitors in the lobby. You escort people. You work in the gift store. You help in the cancer center infusion area. Duties are limited because volunteers are minors.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The program is full. The page says to check back January 2027 for when interest forms will be taken again.

name: Holy Cross Health volunteer program (high school students)
org: Holy Cross Health (Silver Spring and Germantown hospitals)
what_you_do: Volunteer in a Holy Cross hospital or health center in a clinical, customer service, administrative or support role. Year-round and summer-only openings are listed.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Not stated on the main page
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: HOSA Future Health Professionals
what_you_do: You can join this student group for health science students. It has skills contests, leadership events and health career exploration.
grades: Secondary and college students (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your health science teacher.

name: Humane Society Silicon Valley Student Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Students under 18 can foster cats or dogs at home. They need a parent or guardian with them. They can also make no-sew fleece blankets for shelter animals. You earn service hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.
deadline_text: Rolling.

name: Bolsa Chica Conservancy Volunteer Days
what_you_do: Pull invasive plants, plant native ones and pick up trash at the Bolsa Chica wetlands. After a 3 hour training, long-term volunteers can lead wetland activities. They can also restore habitat. Some host visitors at the center.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Restoration events are the last Saturday of each month, 9 a.m. to noon. Long-term volunteers start with a monthly 3 hour training.
deadline_text: No deadline. Events happen monthly.

name: Huntington Beach Public Library Teen Volunteering
what_you_do: Pick a library role. Choices include tech helper, LEGO Club assistant and seed library packer. You can also help with a chess or D&D club. You can also do general branch help like crafts, cleaning and setup.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
deadline_text: Most roles take online applications with no deadline. The Teen Tech role lists applications Aug 29 to Sep 12 and interviews Sep 15 to 18, but the page gives no year, so check the date.

grades: High school (can apply the summer before 9th grade)
name: Huntington Beach Youth Collaborative
what_you_do: Sit on a city youth board of 10 to 15 students. Help run the Junior Citizens Academy and Youth in Government Day. Give ideas to city leaders. Volunteer at city events.
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a volunteer board
duration: 1 year term, from the start of the school year to May. Members can reapply until graduation.
deadline_text: The page says applications are now available, with no end date listed.

name: Illinois 4-H clubs and teen leadership teams
what_you_do: Join a local 4-H club and pick projects. Older teens can also join state teen teams, like STEM Ambassadors, Healthy Living Ambassadors or the Youth Leadership Team.
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the page. Ask your local Extension office.
duration: 4-H year starts September 1. Teen team terms are about one year (stated for the Art Ambassadors).
deadline_text: No sign-up deadline is posted. Teen team applications and dates are not posted on the main teen page.

grades: High school juniors (finished at least one semester of 11th grade)
name: Illinois Boys State (American Legion)
what_you_do: This is a week-long program. Young men run a mock state government on the Eastern Illinois University campus. There are scholarship contests. You also get lifelong alumni membership.
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
duration: One week, June 12 to 18, 2027 (90th annual session)
deadline_text: The registration page says registration for the 2027 session closes at 4:00 PM on June 12, 2027, when the session starts. Ask your local Legion post about its earlier sponsor deadline.

name: Illinois DECA chapters and state conference
org: Illinois DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
what_you_do: Join a DECA chapter to practice business skills in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism, or finance. Chapters compete at an Illinois state conference each spring.
pay_detail: $17 per member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local fees (not stated).
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Illinois DECA conference is March 4 to 6, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency O'Hare in Rosemont, IL. No membership deadline is posted.

name: ALA Illini Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Illinois
city: Illinois (location not stated on the site)
what_you_do: A week-long citizenship and leadership program for high school girls, sponsored by an American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Delegates must attend the full session.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages we read. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: Next session is June 20 to 26, 2027. The application deadline is not stated on the pages read; contact the Department office.

name: SRELO summer research at IMSA
org: Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA), Aurora
city: Aurora, IL (open to Illinois students statewide)
what_you_do: Spend two weeks on a research project with an IMSA faculty mentor. The 2026 projects included AI and cardiology or neuroscience, molecular modeling, Chinese history and building a game in Pygame.
pay_detail: No pay and no program cost are stated. The Research Fundamentals course has a fee that is refunded when you finish the course and program. A need-based scholarship exists for that course.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026 the sessions ran June 1 to 12, June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17.
deadline_text: The 2026 application portal showed closed. No 2027 dates are posted. Sessions in 2026 were in June and July.

name: ISBE Student Advisory Council
what_you_do: Research education topics that affect Illinois public school students. Meet with policymakers and community partners, then present policy ideas to the State Board of Education.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: One school year. Members meet several times a month, online and in person.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed June 30, 2026 and late applications were not considered. Finalists were emailed in July for a video interview.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Illinois Wing
what_you_do: Cadets fly, learn to lead, hike, camp and get in shape. Squadrons meet about 2.5 hours a week plus about one Saturday a month, with summer encampments and career academies.
pay_detail: Dues and uniform costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask the squadron.
duration: Weekly meetings all year
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.

name: Illinois YMCA Youth and Government
city: Springfield, IL (state conference), delegations across Illinois
what_you_do: Join a delegation and take a role in a student model of Illinois state government. Roles include legislator, attorney, lobbyist or press team. You use what you learn at a state conference.
pay_detail: $455 program fee. Your delegation decides how it is collected (full payment, deposit, or register first). Scholarships are available through the registration application.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
deadline_text: The scholarship portal closes October 1, 2026 and scholarship decisions come before November 1. Conference dates and a general registration deadline are not posted on the page read.

duration: September 28 to December 18, 2026
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page read.
name: IMSA AI Credential (online course)
what_you_do: Take a self-paced online course on how AI works, from machine learning to robotics, and on its ethics and safety. Weekly office hours with IMSA computer science faculty. You earn a certificate.
deadline_text: This cohort runs September 28 to December 18, 2026, and it started before October 9, 2026. The page does not say if registration is still open.
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL

duration: 2026 session: March 9 to May 29, 2026
pay_detail: $200. Scholarships are based on financial need. Students who get an SRELO mentor and finish the course get the fee reimbursed.
name: Research Fundamentals (online)
what_you_do: Take a self-guided online course. You plan and run a science investigation and write a science paper. It is the course you must take before the summer SRELO research program.
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened January 26, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL

duration: September 7, 2026 to May 31, 2027
pay_detail: $1,200. Scholarships based on financial need (free or reduced lunch or SNAP) require a $150 fee, with $100 refunded if you finish.
name: RISE: Research, Inquiry Skills and Experimentation
what_you_do: Do your own science research project in a year-long, mostly asynchronous online program. You find a mentor, write a research paper, make a poster and present at spring science symposia.
deadline_text: Registration opened Thursday, July 30, 2026 at noon. Spots are limited. Refund deadlines are mid and late September 2026.
city: Online, run by IMSA in Aurora, IL

name: Indiana DECA chapters and state conference
org: Indiana DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
what_you_do: Join a DECA chapter at a school with business or marketing classes. Members build business skills. They compete at the Indiana state conference.
pay_detail: $15 per member: $7 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Indiana DECA conference is February 26 to 28, 2027 at the Indianapolis Marriott Downtown. No membership deadline is posted.

name: WorkOne young adult (youth) services
org: Indiana Department of Workforce Development, WorkOne Career Centers
city: Statewide, with WorkOne centers in Lafayette and other Indiana cities
what_you_do: Career advising and job-readiness help for young people through WorkOne centers. Pay or work placements are not described on the page; ask the center what is offered.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Contact a WorkOne center.

name: Indiana FFA membership through your school ag class
what_you_do: Join FFA through your school's agriculture class. FFA is the student group tied to agricultural education in Indiana. Local chapters run the activities.
pay_detail: State dues are $14 per active member per year (includes national, state and district dues). Local chapters set their own local dues.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Indiana FFA says affiliation declarations are due October 1, rosters November 1 and student test numbers December 1. These are chapter deadlines for the teacher.

name: Hoosier Boys State
org: American Legion, Department of Indiana (Hoosier Boys State, Inc.)
what_you_do: For one week, build a mock Indiana state government. Delegates form two made-up parties, run for office, propose laws, negotiate bills and meet real officials.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages read. The About page lists scholarships for college. Bring no more than $30 spending money.
duration: One week
deadline_text: Registration opens January 11, 2027. The 2027 session is June 13 to 18, 2027. No registration deadline is posted.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Indiana Wing
what_you_do: Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character in a year-round cadet squadron. Cadets wear uniforms, learn drill, earn promotions and plan activities. You do not have to join the military.
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the pages read. The application lists payment options.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.

name: Indiana YMCA Youth and Government (INYaG)
org: Indiana YMCA Youth and Government (Alliance of Indiana YMCAs)
city: Indianapolis, IN (state conference), delegations across Indiana
what_you_do: Learn how government works by acting it out. Delegates research and debate public issues. They take mock legislative, executive and court roles. Then they serve as delegates at the state conference.
pay_detail: Program fees are not listed on the page read. Ask the program contact.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
deadline_text: 2026-27 conference and registration dates are not posted on the page read (it links only a 2024-2025 calendar).

name: Inova high school student volunteer sessions
city: Fairfax, Alexandria and Northern Virginia hospitals, VA
what_you_do: You volunteer one 3 to 4 hour shift a week at an Inova hospital. You can pick a spring, summer or fall session. You learn about patient care, retail and operations.
grades: High school (through the summer after graduation)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 4 to Jun 20, 2027; 1 shift per week, 3 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 registration opens Nov 5, 2026 at 4 p.m. and closes Nov 8, 2026 at 11:45 p.m. Inova also runs summer and fall sessions.

name: Iroquois Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes bricklayer, carpentry, electrical, painting and more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

name: Irvine High School Youth Action Team (HSYAT)
what_you_do: Student reps from local high schools organize teen activities. They speak for their peers at community groups. Check the Instagram account for upcoming events.
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: School year; follow the team on Instagram for events
deadline_text: The page does not list application dates.

name: Irvine Public Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: You help library staff with programs and crafts. You also help with the seed library and toy cleaning. You can help run the Summer Reading Program. Or join the Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for service projects. TAG also gives feedback on teen programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
deadline_text: The undated page says: Summer Reading applications ran May 9 to May 30, school-year roles reopen Saturday, August 1, and TAG is full with a wait list for applications after August 26. No year is shown, so confirm current openings.

name: UCI Summer Session for High School Students
what_you_do: Take one real UC Irvine college course in the summer, picked from a pre-approved list of courses numbered 1 to 99. Courses are taught at a college level.
pay_detail: The fee page lists high school students under visiting non-UC students: $400 per unit plus a $296 campus fee and $5.50 per unit tech fee. Some courses add materials fees.
duration: One summer course (Summer Session sessions)
deadline_text: Dates for Summer 2027 are not posted yet. Check the Summer Session calendar in spring.

grades: Grades K to 12 (grades 9 to 12 for most options)
name: Irvine Valley College Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Take regular IVC college classes while in school. You can take up to 11 units a semester, on campus or online. IVC also has high school partner classes and an Early College Pathway. It also runs an Irvine school district summer college.
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived for grades 9 to 12 (not for K to 8). You pay the college health fee and buy textbooks.
duration: By semester or summer session
deadline_text: No single deadline. Follow the steps for each term on the IVC page.

name: JA Launchpad (Junior Achievement, Fremont)
what_you_do: You will be able to join a new career center in Fremont, coming in early 2027. It offers a money-management simulation, a student business program and career summits with company mentors.
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)
deadline_text: The page says the center is Coming Early 2027. No opening date or sign-up is posted.

name: Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
what_you_do: Teens meet monthly at a branch. They suggest teen programs and library materials. They work on group projects. They earn volunteer credit.
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Teen Volunteers at JMRL
what_you_do: Teen volunteers prepare program and distribution materials. They make displays and set up meeting rooms. They help with the summer reading program at a library branch.
duration: Varies by branch
deadline_text: The page gives a cutoff date for summer volunteer applications of 5/28/26 and does not say which branches it covers.

name: Job Corps (Brunswick and Turner centers, Georgia)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free career training campus. The Georgia center pages list trades like construction and electrical pre-apprenticeships, bricklaying, carpentry, asphalt paving and Certified Nurse Assistant.
pay_detail: Free. The national site says it covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The application process usually takes about two months.

name: Job Corps: Hubert H. Humphrey Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. The center lists Advanced Transportation Service Worker, Building Construction Technology (pre-apprentice), Culinary Arts and Office Administration.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.

name: Job Corps Sacramento Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: You can get free live-in career training. Choose construction, carpentry, cement masonry or Certified Nurse Assistant. You also get help finishing high school. You can earn a high school equivalency.
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).
deadline_text: Ongoing enrollment. No dates posted on the Sacramento page.

name: Job Corps: Gary Job Corps Center (San Marcos)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. Programs listed include Advanced Cement Masonry (Pre-Apprentice), Advanced Electrical (Overhead Line Construction) and Advanced Transportation Service Worker.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.

name: Job Corps (Cascades, Curlew and Columbia Basin centers, Washington)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Sedro-Woolley, Curlew and Moses Lake, WA
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. Centers list computer and medical assistant, carpentry, cement masonry, human services, fire management and nursing assistant training.
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.

name: John Muir Health High School Student Volunteer Program (Walnut Creek Medical Center)
what_you_do: Help staff, patients and visitors at Walnut Creek Medical Center in a structured high school program. Students build skills in administration, patient interaction, communication, organization and leadership.
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
deadline_text: No application window is stated on the official page. Contact a partner high school (for example Acalanes, Campolindo, Las Lomas, Miramonte, Monte Vista, San Ramon Valley or Ygnacio Valley) to ask about the next intake.

name: Junior Achievement of Northern California (high school programs)
what_you_do: You can join Junior Achievement programs on entrepreneurship, investing and personal finance, led by volunteers. Job shadow and Finance Park experiences are also listed, and a Silicon Valley Launchpad center is coming in early 2027.
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No central deadline; ask JA.

name: KP LAUNCH High School Program
city: Northern California Kaiser Permanente service areas
what_you_do: You get a paid summer job. It is seven weeks and full time. The jobs are in healthcare support or admin roles. You also get weekly workshops, mentoring and networking. There is little patient contact.
grades: Current high school student (priority to juniors and seniors) or Class of 2027 graduate
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
deadline_text: Opens Nov 16, 2026 at 9am Pacific; closes Jan 8, 2027 at 5pm Pacific.

duration: Workdays are monthly. Cancelled when it is below zero.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
name: Volunteer Restoration Workdays (all ages)
org: Forest Preserve District of Kane County
what_you_do: Join a monthly restoration workday in the forest preserves. Volunteers work in natural areas. Longer roles include trail adopter and nature center host. You can also be a historic site guide or help at special events.
deadline_text: No deadline. See the monthly list of workdays on the volunteer page.

name: Kane County Workforce Development Youth Services (WIOA Youth)
city: Kane, DeKalb and Kendall Counties (Elgin area), IL
what_you_do: You can get paid work experience. You can do internships and job shadowing. Apprenticeships are also an option. You get resume and interview coaching. You can get GED prep and tutoring. You also get help with life skills, transportation and child care.
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.
duration: Varies by provider
deadline_text: No dates posted. You contact a provider and they explain how to start.

name: King County Library System Teen Advisory Boards
city: King County, WA (branches outside the city of Seattle)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers meet with a librarian. They give input on library services. They help design library programs and events.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit, and can ask for a reference letter after 10 hours of volunteering within 6 months.
duration: Ongoing; meeting schedules vary by branch
deadline_text: No deadline. The page lists upcoming meetings (for example Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way); contact the local library to join.

name: Keck Medicine of USC Summer Youth Volunteer Program
org: Keck Medicine of USC, Office of Volunteer Services
what_you_do: Volunteer for 8 weeks in summer. You work at Keck Hospital of USC or USC Norris Cancer Hospital.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: 8 weeks, at least 8 hours a week and 60 hours total
deadline_text: The page lists the application period as Feb 1 to April 30, with recommendation letters due April 30 (year not stated). Orientation is the second week of June.

name: Kennesaw Police Public Safety Cadet Program
what_you_do: Weekly classes on police rules and methods, criminal law and the U.S. Constitution. You also do real-world training scenes. Volunteer at city events like Taste of Kennesaw. The page says cadets can earn over 100 volunteer hours in one year.
pay_detail: Volunteer program. The page lists no fees.
duration: Weekly meetings. Day and time are not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.

name: Key Club (high school service club)
what_you_do: You do service, leadership and fundraising through a student-led club at your school. If your school has no club, you can start one.
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the pages read).
deadline_text: Join your school's club or start one. No cycle stated.

name: Keystone Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus and train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes bricklayer, carpentry, cement masonry, plumbing and more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

name: Khan Academy college and careers courses
what_you_do: You can take free online lessons on the Khan Academy Life skills page. Topics include financial literacy, personal finance, entrepreneurship, career exploration and college admissions.
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Always open.

duration: One school year, with monthly meetings
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It is a leadership role.
name: KidsMatter Senior High Board
what_you_do: Join a student board that meets monthly during the school year. Plan and run community events, like a self-care month and a service night at a museum, and speak for teens in the community.
deadline_text: 2025-26 board: applications closed May 17, 2026. The 2026-27 call is not posted on the page yet.

name: Kode With Klossy
city: Virtual and in-person (Oakland, San Francisco and more)
what_you_do: You can join a free coding program for girls and gender-expansive teens ages 13 to 18. Choices include a two-day Code-a-Bration or a two-week Camp in summer.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Code-a-Bration is 2 days; Camp is 2 weeks
deadline_text: Sign-ups are open for Code-a-Bration (Nov 7 to 8, 2026 in Oakland and virtual; Oct 17 to 18 in Chicago and virtual). Summer 2027 Camp applications open in February 2027; closing dates not posted.

name: Architecture Summer Academy
org: Kennesaw State University, College of Architecture and Construction Management
what_you_do: Two weeks of design practice in architecture. It includes a field trip to Atlanta. It ends with a talk about your work and an awards dinner.
pay_detail: $1,050 for 2026. Materials for modeling and drawing are included. Scholarships are not mentioned.
duration: 10 weekdays (July 6 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 session July 6 to July 17, 2026. Registration closed April 1, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.

name: DiscoverU Summer Camps (high school)
org: Kennesaw State University, Continuing and Professional Education
what_you_do: One-week hands-on career camps on campus. The 2026 camps are Baking and Pastry, Chef's Master Class and Medical Skills. The others are AutoCAD, Aerospace Engineering and Adulting 101.
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $499 for baking, AutoCAD, Chef's Master Class and Medical Skills; $399 for Adulting 101; $350 for Aerospace Engineering. Scholarships are not mentioned.
duration: One week per camp
deadline_text: 2026 camps ran June 1 to July 24, 2026. Summer 2027 dates and prices are not posted yet; the page has a contact form for updates.

name: Summer Arts Intensives and Music Camps (high school)
org: Kennesaw State University, Geer College of the Arts
what_you_do: One-week summer intensives in dance, theater, and arts and design. There are also music camps for jazz band, concert band, piano, choir and orchestra.
grades: Rising 9th grade through rising college freshman
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the main page. Check each program page.
duration: One week for the intensives. Music camps run 3 to 6 days.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 page: registration opens November 1. Music camps: Jazz Band June 13-18, Concert Band June 20-25, Piano June 28-30, Choir July 5-10, Orchestra July 11-16 (year not printed, page is headed Summer 2027). No deadline is listed; spaces fill fast.

name: LA County Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI) for rising high school seniors
org: LA County Department of Arts and Culture, with Bloomberg Philanthropies
what_you_do: Paid summer internship at an arts or culture group. You work 120 hours over 8 weeks. Monday to Wednesday you are at your worksite. On Thursdays and Fridays you join program days with other interns.
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated. Program Day participants also get a stipend for 90% participation, plus transportation help and lunch.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to August 6, 2027. Optional paid extension from September 2027 to April 2028 (22 weeks).
deadline_text: Student applications open in March 2027 when internship listings are posted. No student deadline is posted yet.

name: Los Angeles County Fire Department Explorer Program
what_you_do: Explorers learn what firefighting takes. They build leadership and discipline and do community service. They meet twice a month at their post and go on monthly ride-alongs. They also join yearly trainings and drills.
pay_detail: No cost or pay is stated on the page
duration: Ongoing after a two-day orientation; twice-monthly meetings
deadline_text: Open enrollment is usually held once a year in May. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Los Angeles County Junior Lifeguard Program (ages 9 to 17, with Cadets 16 to 17)
org: Los Angeles County Fire Department Lifeguards
what_you_do: A four-week summer ocean safety program at county beaches. Older returning teens can move up to the Life Saving Team (15 to 17) or Cadets (16 to 17).
pay_detail: About $635 per child for Summer 2026 (the page says the fee schedule was under review). Financial aid needs a federal tax return.
duration: Two 4-week sessions in 2026: June 15 to July 10 and July 13 to August 7
deadline_text: Summer 2026 swim tests ran March 14 to April 12. The page says new Junior Lifeguard information is posted each January or February, and parents can expect registration in February or March. Summer 2027 dates are not posted.

name: LA County Library Teen Volunteer and Teen Advisory Board
org: County of Los Angeles Public Library
what_you_do: You can help at your local library. Tasks include kids' storytimes and art activities. You can help with computer and printing help. You can clean and sort materials and make displays. Teen Advisory Boards plan programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.
duration: Varies by library
deadline_text: No deadline. Ask your local LA County Library about current openings.

name: LA County Youth@Work
org: LA County Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO)
what_you_do: Do a paid, part-time first job with a local employer while taking a work-readiness class. You sign up through a nearby America's Job Center of California (AJCC).
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.
duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Fill out the youth interest form and an AJCC contacts you within 48 hours. In 2025 the summer jobs started July 1.

name: LA Metro Youth Council
org: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro)
what_you_do: Teens help Metro learn what young people think about its plans, projects and programs. The council aims to listen, learn, engage, empower and build ridership.
pay_detail: The page does not mention a stipend or pay
duration: 1-year term, January to December
deadline_text: Recruitment for the 2027 council has closed. No dates are posted. A sign-up form on the page gets updates on youth opportunities.

name: Los Angeles Zoo Core Volunteer (students 14 and up)
what_you_do: Core volunteers help zoo guests and support the Zoo's guest engagement programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: 25 hours per year for students (50 hours per year for other volunteers)
deadline_text: Applications are closed now. The Zoo has a waitlist to tell you when they open. No dates are posted.

name: LACMA Teens
org: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
what_you_do: You learn how museum education works. You plan and run an art workshop with other teens. LACMA staff guide you.
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort: applications ran July 1 to Aug 21, 2026 (5 p.m.) and are closed. The page says LACMA will not accept applications again until next year.

name: Zoo Teens (ages 14-17)
org: Columbian Park Zoo, City of Lafayette Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: A structured summer volunteer program at the city zoo for teens curious about zookeeping, conservation and wildlife education. Builds customer service, time management and leadership skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: Summer; shift details are in the 2026 Zoo Teen Information Packet (not read)
deadline_text: 2026 application closed; materials were due March 13, 2026. The zoo page says to check back in January 2027.

name: Food Finders Food Bank volunteer shifts
what_you_do: Sign up for volunteer shifts at the food bank. Family Night projects include bagging produce and assembling senior boxes. Teens 14 and older can also volunteer at the Fresh Market.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is given at the start of your first shift.
duration: Single shifts you pick on the calendar
deadline_text: No deadline. You can sign up for shifts up to 3 months ahead.

name: C-PASA High School Camp (Cargill-Purdue Agriculture & STEM Academy)
org: Purdue University College of Agriculture, Office of Academic Programs
what_you_do: Spend a week living on Purdue's campus. You do hands-on work in agriculture and STEM. You visit research sites and labs. You tour agriculture companies. You meet Purdue students and faculty. You see what college life is like.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the camp page. Summer College for High School Students sets the price (see the Purdue Summer College card).
duration: 1 week, residential
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran July 12 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the camp page.

name: Pulsar Summer Residential (Purdue GER2I, grades 9 to 12)
org: Purdue University Gifted Education Research and Resource Institute (GER2I)
what_you_do: Live in a Purdue residence hall for two weeks. You take challenging courses with other gifted and talented students. The program also includes field trips and recreation.
pay_detail: 2026 listing: $2,990 per session for Star or Pulsar, plus a $100 application fee (refunded only if not accepted). Optional $100 Saturday field trip. A 5% early bird discount applied by Feb 17. A limited number of partial scholarships exist for students with financial need, first come, first served.
duration: 2 week sessions
deadline_text: 2026: registration opened Feb 2, 2026. Camp ran June 28 to July 25, 2026 in two sessions (June 28 to July 11, July 12 to 25). Payment was due June 1. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: STEP: Seminar for Top Engineering Prospects (Purdue)
org: Purdue University College of Engineering Honors Program
what_you_do: Spend a week on Purdue's campus. You work in teams of four on engineering design challenges. There is a final design competition. You also tour two engineering areas. You learn about 3D modeling, programming and robotics.
pay_detail: Attendance fee $2,500 for 2026. It covers activities, housing, meals and local transportation. You pay your own travel to Purdue. Need-based scholarships are available after you are accepted.
duration: 1 week, residential
deadline_text: 2026 sessions were July 5 to 11, July 12 to 18, July 19 to 25 and July 26 to Aug 1. Registration for 2026 has closed. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Summer College for High School Students (short-term residential courses)
org: Purdue University, Office of Summer and Winter Sessions
what_you_do: You live on the West Lafayette campus for one or two weeks. You take a short college course. It is for 1 or 2 credit hours. Subjects include coding, cybersecurity, pharmacy, nursing, nuclear energy and business.
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: $60 application fee. Tuition and fees $347.85 per credit hour for Indiana residents ($948.30 nonresident). Room and board $377.95 for a 1-week program, $907.08 for 2 weeks. Some courses add $60 or $200 program fees. Scholarships exist.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, residential, June and July
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens December 1, 2026. Last cycle: priority deadline February 1, final deadline April 1. 2027 deadlines not posted.

name: Teen Volunteers, Summer Reading Club
what_you_do: Help run the library's Summer Reading Club: explain how it works, sign kids up, update the database and hand out prizes. One 2-hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer Reading Club season; at least one 2-hour shift per week
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: apply by Friday, May 22, 2026; required training day May 16 or May 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Tippecanoe County 4-H
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club and do hands-on projects, including livestock and non-livestock projects. The county page also links to county fair entry and the Indiana State Fair.
grades: Grades 3 to 12 (Mini 4-H is grades K to 2)
pay_detail: $15 per child, $45 maximum per family. The fee covers insurance, project materials and club activities.
duration: Program year, enrollment starts Oct 1
deadline_text: Enrollment for the Indiana 4-H year begins October 1. The county page asks members to enroll by Jan 15 (and says Jan 1 to keep traditional involvement). The drop/add deadline for projects is May 15 each year.

name: Saddleback Medical Center Volunteer
what_you_do: Volunteer in the hospital as part of the patient care team. You work in service areas. After an interview, the Volunteer Office finds you an opening.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a volunteer uniform jacket ($25) and pay $5 in dues.
duration: 150 hours per year
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Teen Action Group (TAG) at East Lansing Public Library
org: East Lansing Public Library (City of East Lansing)
what_you_do: East Lansing High School students can log limited volunteer hours. They do this by joining our Teen Action Group.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No current dates found. The library is not currently accepting general volunteers; TAG is the exception named on the current page.

name: PAN: Physics of Atomic Nuclei (FRIB, Michigan State University)
org: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University
what_you_do: Spend a week at a world-leading nuclear physics lab. You explore nuclear astrophysics research, run your own experiments, and learn how the science is used in society.
pay_detail: Free. The program, room and board are free for all participants.
duration: About 1 week, residential
deadline_text: The program takes place in late July each year. Applications are open early December through March. Exact 2027 dates are not posted on the page I could read.

name: PING: Physicists Inspiring the Next Generation (FRIB, Michigan State University)
org: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University
what_you_do: Spend two weeks doing nuclear physics at the FRIB lab with undergraduate mentors. It can turn into a year-long research project. Students may present their work at national conferences.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the listing I could read.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was March 15, 2026 and the program ran July 12 to 25, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the listing.

name: Greater Lansing Food Bank Volunteer Shifts
what_you_do: You sort food and build Weekend Kits in the warehouse. Or you help at Mobile Food Pantries. In season, you can help with the Garden Project.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; weekday warehouse shifts are about 2 hours
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts any time; many shifts book 2 to 3 weeks out.

name: Michigan 4-H Exploration Days (at Michigan State University)
org: Michigan State University Extension, Michigan 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: Stay on the MSU campus with about 1,000 other youth and choose from more than 100 sessions taught by MSU faculty, staff and 4-H volunteers. You live in a dorm and eat in the dining hall.
pay_detail: 2025 cost was $250. It covers meals, a shared dorm room, sessions and a t-shirt. Your county MSU Extension office may have scholarship money.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 24 to 26)
deadline_text: The 2026 event was June 24 to 26, 2026. 2027 dates and the 2026 price are not posted on the listing I could read.

grades: Entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027 (or recent graduates)
name: High School Engineering Institute (HSEI) at Michigan State University
org: Michigan State University College of Engineering
what_you_do: A week on campus living in the dorms. Each day you learn about an engineering major with faculty and students, do hands-on team projects and tour research labs.
pay_detail: $1,199 program fee (covers activities, room and board). MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.
duration: One week, residential. Four sessions: June 13 to 17, June 20 to 24, June 27 to July 1, July 11 to 15
deadline_text: Applications open mid-December 2026. Deadlines by session: Session 1 June 4, Session 2 June 11, Session 3 June 18, Session 4 July 2. The page does not print the year; it is the cycle for students entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027.

grades: Entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027 (or recent graduates)
name: Making a Game of It, AI Assisted (MGIT-AI) at Michigan State University
org: Michigan State University College of Engineering
what_you_do: This is a residential week. You learn to code and design. You build your own video games. You use AI as a coding and creative helper.
pay_detail: $1,299 program fee. MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.
duration: One week, residential: July 18 to 23
deadline_text: Applications open mid-December 2026. Application deadline: July 9. The page does not print the year; it is the cycle for students entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027.

name: Zoo Teen Program at Potter Park Zoo
org: Potter Park Zoo (Potter Park Zoological Society and Ingham County)
what_you_do: You teach guests at conservation stations. You work with the goat contact yard. You help in the Zookambi summer camp. You learn about zoo careers from zookeepers.
pay_detail: $50 program fee (shirt, training materials, name tag), paid at orientation, not at application. Scholarships are available.
duration: At least 40 hours of service from June to August
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. Information session dates and May 2027 orientation dates will be posted in January 2027. You must attend an information session to get the application.

grades: Entering junior year of high school or older (junior and senior students at local high schools)
name: UM Health-Sparrow Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You can volunteer in one of six teen roles at the hospital. Examples are discharge, patient and visitor guide, bedside DJ and mother and baby. You work one short shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One semester (10 to 12 weeks): one 2 hour shift a week in the school year, or two shifts a week (max 4 hours) in summer
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are temporarily closed and are anticipated to reopen in mid-October.

name: Lao Family Community Development: Youth on the Move
what_you_do: You get a paid summer work experience of up to about 100 hours. You get job readiness training. It is through the City of Oakland's summer youth jobs program.
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage (MSYEP rule); exact rate not posted
duration: Up to about 100 hours
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Summer 2026 round is over; call for the next cycle.

name: LAPL Teen Volunteer, Teen Council and Teens Leading Change
what_you_do: You volunteer at your branch library. You organize the teen area. You build displays. You help kids with homework. You help with summer reading. Teen Council and Teens Leading Change add a community project.
pay_detail: Unpaid; you earn community service hours.
duration: Varies by branch; Teen Council members complete at least 20 community service hours
deadline_text: No deadline. Teens Leading Change projects form in September, but you can join anytime.

name: Summer Youth Volunteer Program
org: Livermore Area Recreation and Park District (LARPD)
what_you_do: Teens help Livermore Area Recreation and Park District staff. They run summer camps, sports, arts and crafts. They run recreation programs. They can join open space projects with park rangers. Volunteers earn community service hours.
pay_detail: Volunteer position. Earn community service hours; no wage is listed.
duration: Summer weekly shifts. The 2026 FAQ says sign-ups start with a maximum of 2 weeks, with more weeks added later.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: sign up for orientation by Friday, March 13, 2026. Orientations were March 19, 2026 (5 to 6:30 pm) and March 25, 2026 (4 to 5:30 pm) at the Robert Livermore Community Center. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Las Positas College CCAP Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: You can take free Las Positas College classes in high school. The classes focus on career technical pathways. Partner programs are in Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley. Tuition and fees are waived. Required materials are provided.
pay_detail: Free; tuition and fees waived and required materials provided (parking may cost extra for classes at LPC)
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.

name: Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program (BLDAP)
what_you_do: You spend six weeks in person at Berkeley Lab, at least 4 days a week. You work on machine learning and data science projects, take computer science classes and hear talks from scientists.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page (no stipend listed)
duration: June 16 to July 24, 2026 (6 weeks, 4 days a week)
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened Feb 2, 2026 and are now closed (the page gives no closing date). 2027 not posted.

name: Experiences in Research
what_you_do: You get a paid six-week summer research internship with a Berkeley Lab mentor. Areas include data science, experimental research, coding and science communication.
pay_detail: $500 per week for 30 to 35 hours
duration: 6 weeks (June 15 to July 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 window was Feb 2 to Mar 22, 2026. 2027 not posted.

name: SeA Bilingual STEM Camp
what_you_do: This is a free spring break camp at Berkeley Lab. It is for bilingual students. They are native Spanish speakers and English learners. It shows students careers in science, technology, engineering and math.
pay_detail: Free
duration: April 8 to 11, 2026 (spring break)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed; no 2027 dates posted.

name: LBWIN Youth Career Services Center
org: City of Long Beach Economic Development and Opportunity, Workforce Development Bureau
what_you_do: You can get free career help at a youth center. Services include work-readiness workshops and help finding jobs. You can get paid internships or work experience such as Youth@Work.
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. The competitive school-to-career programs (Long Beach Public Service Corps, Port of Long Beach internship, Fire Corps internship and others) open for set application periods.

name: League of Volunteers Teen Volunteers (Summer Recreation)
city: Newark, CA (serves Fremont, Newark and Union City)
what_you_do: You help lead activities. You assist staff at the League's summer recreation program for kids. The League says teen volunteers gain leadership experience.
duration: The 2026 summer recreation program ran July 6 to July 30, 2026, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at Mayhews Landing Park in Newark.
deadline_text: The homepage showed a 2026 summer teen volunteer call. No 2027 dates are posted.

name: LegiSchool Civics Virtual Institute
org: Sacramento State Center for California Studies with the California State Legislature
what_you_do: You can take a four-week online summer program about California policy. It includes talks from state leaders. It also includes professional skills workshops. You earn a stipend at the end.
pay_detail: Stipend paid after the program. The amount is not posted.
duration: 4 weeks, Mon/Wed/Fri afternoons (2026: starts June 22)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed May 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.

name: Teen Internship (Summer Camp Staff)
org: Lawrence Hall of Science, UC Berkeley
what_you_do: You help run science summer camps by leading games and activities, preparing materials and supporting campers. Training is in May, and the job is full time in summer.
pay_detail: $3,500 for the full summer ($72 deducted per missed day)
duration: June 1 to Aug 7, 2026, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; Saturday trainings in May
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed January 15, 2026. Expect a similar mid-January deadline for 2027.

name: Lawrence Hall of Science Youth Volunteers
org: Lawrence Hall of Science, UC Berkeley
what_you_do: You staff exhibits such as the planetarium. Others are Ingenuity Challenges, Outdoor Nature Lab and Animal Discovery Zone. The minimum is 21 summer hours. During the school year, it is 2 shifts a month.
duration: Summer minimum 21 hours; school year two 3-hour shifts a month
deadline_text: Paused: no new cohort in 2025, with a relaunch planned for 2026 (page text dates from Dec 2024). Last posted window closed Jan 16, 2024. No current cohort confirmed.

name: LifeLine Animal Project Youth Volunteers
what_you_do: Help animal shelters. You can make pet toys, socialize cats and help at events. You can run donation drives and wash laundry and dishes. Or make graphics and photos. You do not handle animals.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Ongoing. Orientation first, at one of three shelter locations.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up any time.

name: Livermore Area Youth Advisory Commission (LAYAC)
what_you_do: Youth members advise the City Council and the Livermore recreation district on what young people need. They also organize events that promote respect for diversity among Livermore youth.
pay_detail: Advisory commission seat. No pay is stated in the code.
deadline_text: Application dates not found. The city teen page that would list them returned an access block to our reads.

name: Discovery Program (Summer Health Sciences)
what_you_do: This is a two-week summer program on the Loma Linda campus. It is for high school students interested in health sciences careers.
pay_detail: $30 non-refundable application fee (fee waiver available for financial need). The page does not list a program cost.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to July 24), plus optional shadowing week
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Jan 12 to April 12, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect a similar January to April window.

name: Long Beach City College Individual Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: Take college classes at Long Beach City College while you are in middle or high school. Students with 12 or more units by senior year can earn a graduation medallion.
pay_detail: Tuition and enrollment fees are free. Course material fees, textbooks and supplies are not covered (a Textbook Loan Program exists for hardship).
duration: By term
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. See the college's Registration Dates and Academic Calendar pages.

name: Long Beach Commission on Youth and Children (youth seats)
org: City of Long Beach Parks, Recreation and Marine
what_you_do: Two youth members join seven adults to advise the Mayor and City Council. They give advice on city services for kids and teens. They also review the city's youth plan.
pay_detail: No pay is stated
duration: 2-year terms (up to 4 terms); meets every other 3rd Wednesday at 6 p.m.
deadline_text: No application window is posted.

name: Long Beach Junior Lifeguards Cadet Program
what_you_do: Cadets get advanced first aid and rescue training. They shadow Long Beach lifeguards and help instructors. The goal is leadership and a path to lifeguard or other public service jobs.
pay_detail: Cost or pay is not stated on the page
duration: Summer; the 2026 cadet calendar is listed as not set
deadline_text: Tryout is listed for April 26 at 8:30 AM (year not stated; the age rule uses July 1, 2027). Interviews that day 11 AM to 3 PM.

name: Long Beach Parks, Recreation and Marine Volunteer (13 and up)
org: City of Long Beach Parks, Recreation and Marine
what_you_do: Volunteer at local parks, after school sites and senior centers. You can also help at special events, youth sports and summer programs. Other spots are the Teen Center and El Dorado Nature Center.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Long Beach Recreation Program Leader (temporary)
org: City of Long Beach Parks, Recreation and Marine
what_you_do: Part-time city recreation job: plan and run activities for children, go to staff meetings and training, and keep kids safe. Hours can reach 40 a week from June through August.
pay_detail: Hourly by level: $16.76 (Specialist III), $17.31 (IV), $18.09 (V), $20.87 (VII). The level depends on your qualifications.
duration: Temporary; hours vary by week and may reach 40 per week June through August
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page mentions a job fair on Saturday, Jan. 24, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. at Houghton Park (year not stated).

name: Long Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Help the library staff. You put materials in order and support library programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Long Beach Youth Poet Laureate
what_you_do: Selected poets lead youth poetry programs. They get mentoring from local poets. They send work to the library book of poems. They read at a final show. The term runs May 2027 to April 2028.
pay_detail: $1,500 scholarship for the Youth Poet Laureate; $500 scholarship for each of 4 Youth Poet Ambassadors
duration: May 2027 to April 2028
deadline_text: Applications open Nov 14, 2026 and close Feb 27, 2027 (no late applications). Finalists told by April 2027. Finals May 22, 2027.

name: Teen Docent Program, Los Altos History Museum
what_you_do: Teen docents work with museum staff, lead tours of the exhibits and the J. Gilbert Smith House, greet visitors and help at special events. They also take on leadership roles.
grades: High school student enrolled in the 2026-27 academic year
pay_detail: Not stated on the current page. A 2024 article describes volunteer hours and work experience.
duration: August 2026 through June 2027, at least 4 hours per month. Two-day training on August 8 and 9 for accepted applicants.
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed (the page says the deadline for this year has passed). The museum says to check back next spring for the 2027-28 year.

name: Los Rios Dual Enrollment and CCAP (American River, Cosumnes River, Folsom Lake, Sacramento City)
what_you_do: You can take free college classes while in high school. You can enroll on your own at a Los Rios college (special admit), or take a college class at your high school through an agreement between your school and the college.
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Other fees may apply, such as the student representation fee. Books may cost extra.
duration: Per semester
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply and register by each college's term dates.

name: Madison Children's Museum Volunteers
what_you_do: You help kids play and learn at the museum. You can help with Rooftop Ramble animals and gardens. You can help in Art Studio or be a Play Ambassador. You can help in the outdoor Wonderground from April to October.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One 2-hour shift each week for at least two months
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Shifts are filled first come, first served.

name: TEENworks at Goodman Community Center
what_you_do: These are paid teen jobs at the community center, with training. All teens earn ServSafe certification and get event catering training. They can also earn high school credit.
pay_detail: Hourly wage; the rate is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates or enrollment status are posted on the page.

name: Zoo Teen Program
what_you_do: This is an eight-week summer program on conservation. You go behind the scenes at the zoo. You hear from local conservation groups. You work with animal care and environmental professionals.
pay_detail: $200 per teen for the summer. Scholarships are available. Applying is free and payment is due only after you are invited.
duration: 8 weeks, two days a week (June 22 to Aug 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 28 and closed Mar 1, 2026; notified Mar 2 to 13. 2027 dates not posted yet.

name: Henry Vilas Zoo Volunteer Program (teens 14 to 17)
what_you_do: Help at the zoo in roles such as gate greeter, goat yard attendant, events and wildlife champion. Training is given.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo does not do last-minute school hour confirmations.
duration: Seasonal; commitment varies by role
deadline_text: Applications for ongoing roles are posted each year between February and April.

name: MMoCA Teen Forum
what_you_do: Learn how an art exhibition is made. Create and run educational programs. Meet museum and arts professionals through job shadows.
pay_detail: Members are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated.
duration: 6 to 8 hours per month, in person at MMoCA, through the year
deadline_text: The page says applications were closed for the 2025 Teen Forum. No 2026-27 dates are posted.

name: Operation Fresh Start Legacy Program
what_you_do: You do paid, hands-on conservation or construction work. You get mentoring while you work toward a diploma. You earn an AmeriCorps Education Award when you finish.
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated). Finishers may earn an AmeriCorps Education Award of about $2,800 for college.
duration: At least 1,000 program hours (total length not stated)
deadline_text: No deadline listed. The page says Legacy is accepting applications.

name: Madison Public Library Volunteering (teens welcome)
what_you_do: Help a library branch with tasks. Tasks include pulling books for holds and packing maker kits. You can package seeds for the Seed Library. You can set up for programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Varies by branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings change by branch and season; several branches had no openings on the day the page was read.

name: Accelerated Learning Program (Badger Precollege)
what_you_do: Three weeks on the UW-Madison campus focused on one college-level course (95 class hours).
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,750; commuter $2,850; international $5,100; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 12, scholarships due Apr 1, application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Badger Summer Scholars (Badger Precollege)
what_you_do: Take a college-level course of your choice for two weeks on the UW-Madison campus. Residential students live in a residence hall.
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,450; commuter $2,600; international $4,800; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).
duration: About 2 weeks (July 19 to 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 12, scholarships due Apr 1, application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

grades: Current sophomore or junior (the page also says 'rising juniors and seniors', so confirm)
name: Engineering Summer Program (ESP)
what_you_do: This is a three-week program on campus. You study math, physics, chemistry and engineering design. You do hands-on workshops. You visit industry sites. Faculty mentor you.
pay_detail: Free: housing and meals included. No stipend is mentioned.
duration: 3 weeks (July 11 to 31 in 2026), residential
deadline_text: 2026 application is closed and decisions were sent. No 2027 deadline posted.

name: UW Health Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You volunteer in a UW Health hospital or clinic. You do it for a full semester. You need a placement interview and onboarding first.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: At least one full semester
deadline_text: Application closed now. Spring semester applications are expected to open Dec 2, 2026, with onboarding finished by Jan 8, 2027. Summer expected to open Apr 12, 2027; fall expected in July 2027. All dates are subject to change.

name: WIOA Youth Program (WorkSmart Network)
org: Workforce Development Board of South Central Wisconsin
what_you_do: This is free career planning, skills training and work-based learning. A career planner builds a plan with you.
pay_detail: Free. The page says all WorkSmart Network services are free of charge and does not say anyone is paid.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline. The page says the online application is coming soon.

name: Wisconsin Youth Apprenticeship (Dane and Jefferson counties)
org: Workforce Development Board of South Central Wisconsin
what_you_do: Spend part of the week in class and part on a paid job with a business mentor. There are 16 program areas. It lasts 1 or 2 years.
pay_detail: Paid while working; wage not stated.
duration: 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Virtual information nights (7:00 to 7:45 pm): Nov 18, 2026; Dec 16, 2026; Jan 20, 2027; Mar 17, 2027; and Feb 17, 2027 (UW Health sessions).

name: Major League Hacking (MLH) hackathons
what_you_do: Major League Hacking runs student hackathons. These are short coding contests. It also runs coding events. It has a 12-week remote Fellowship that pays a stipend. Most listed hackathons do not say high school students can enter.
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the pages read; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Weekend events; Fellowship is 12 weeks
deadline_text: Dates differ by event. See the 2027 season events list. California events listed: DiamondHacks (La Jolla, Apr 4 to 5, 2027) and LA Hacks (Los Angeles, Apr 16 to 18, 2027).

name: Marietta Police Public Safety Cadets
what_you_do: A club that trains like a police academy. You have classroom lectures and hands-on practice. Cadets help at road races, fundraisers, dinners and city events. Cadets get a personal letter of reference.
pay_detail: Not a paid job. You pay a yearly membership fee and buy part of the uniform. Competition travel costs up to $250 per trip.
duration: Meets about 3 Thursdays a month, 6 to 9 pm. Attend at least 2 a month, plus 5 volunteer hours a month.
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by going to meetings.

name: The Maryland Zoo Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Start as a Zoo Guide answering visitor questions, then choose a track such as guest engagement or conservation and research. Teens get training from zoo staff, a uniform and a badge.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. The page mentions no fees.
duration: At least one year: 4 shifts a month, one shift at a zoo event, and a one-week Boot Camp (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
deadline_text: Teen applications are closed. The page says to check back in 2027. For 2026, applications ran Jan 29 to Apr 9, interviews were in May, and Boot Camp ran in late June and early July.

name: Massachusetts 4-H
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club or a short-term 4-H program at a library or community center. Pick your own projects, build skills and enter competitions if you are 8 or older.
pay_detail: $40 per member each year, with a family cap of $120. Fee waivers can be requested through your 4-H Educator. The page says cash is not accepted.
duration: Annual membership; you re-enroll each year
deadline_text: No deadline posted. All members enroll every year.

name: Massachusetts Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Massachusetts
city: Massachusetts (2026 session at Stonehill College, Easton)
what_you_do: Spend a week running a pretend city and state. You campaign, write and debate bills, and learn how local and state government work.
grades: Finishing or just finished junior year of high school
pay_detail: No pay. Participants are sponsored by an American Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or community group. The student cost is not stated on the pages read.
duration: One week (2026: June 13 to June 19)
deadline_text: The 2026 session was June 13 to June 19, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
