name: Massachusetts Boys State
org: The American Legion, Massachusetts Boys State Committee
what_you_do: Spend a week at Stonehill College running a pretend state government. You take classes, run for office, join a band, court or newspaper, and play sports.
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: No pay. The goal is that tuition is paid by your local American Legion post, the Massachusetts Boys State and Girls State Foundation, a school or town, or a sponsor.
duration: One week: the 83rd Annual Session is June 12 to June 18, 2027
deadline_text: Session dates: June 12 to June 18, 2027. The site says applications open in late 2026. No closing date is posted.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Massachusetts Wing
what_you_do: Join a local squadron for weekly meetings. Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. Wear a uniform. Move up in rank as you take on more leadership.
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.

name: Massachusetts FFA
what_you_do: Join an FFA chapter at a school that teaches agricultural education. FFA builds leadership, personal growth and career skills. It does this through hands-on experiences.
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You join through your school.

name: UMass Amherst Pre-College Summer Programs
org: University of Massachusetts Amherst, University Without Walls
city: Amherst, MA (also online and the UMass Charles River Campus in Boston)
what_you_do: Take a faculty-led summer course for high school students in over 25 topics like STEM, art and design, and business. A six-week lab research option is also offered.
grades: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors (some programs only juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: $45 application fee. Listed fees: 2-week programs $4,119 residential or $2,337 commuter; 3-week $6,125 or $3,397; 6-week Research Intensives $12,813 or $7,247. Some programs add a $95 materials fee. Limited need-based partial scholarships (up to $1,000) for 1 to 3 week programs.
duration: 1 to 6 weeks, depending on the program
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed (2026 deadlines were May 1 extended to May 15, May 15 and May 31 by start date). Research Intensives 2026 deadlines were March 15, extended to April 15. The site says Summer 2027 program details and applications will be available in January.

name: Mattel Youth Ambassadors (UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital)
what_you_do: Support Mattel Children's Hospital and patient programs. You meet each week in summer and each month in the school year. You make art projects and hear from doctors. You also work toward a fundraising goal.
pay_detail: No fee, but each ambassador must raise $1,250 for the hospital to earn an awards package.
duration: Cohort 8 runs 2027 to 2028. Meetings are Wednesdays 3:30 to 4:30 PM, virtual; weekly in summer, monthly in the school year.
deadline_text: The 2026 window ran May 1 to June 6, 2026. Recruitment for Cohort 8 (2027 to 2028) is expected to open in May 2027.

name: Teen Art Collective
org: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego (MCASD)
what_you_do: This is a yearlong teen program. It includes workshops and visits from artists and museum staff. You get studio time and critiques. The program ends with a teen-organized exhibition and public event.
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications were due Friday Aug 28, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a late-summer deadline.

name: Teen Advisory Board at MCPL
what_you_do: You are a library teen volunteer. You give feedback on programs. You help librarians plan and run events. You speak up for youth services in the county.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Maryland 4-H Youth Development
city: Statewide, Maryland (a local Extension office in each county); state center in College Park
what_you_do: Join a county 4-H club or program. It has hands-on projects, camps and STEM contests. It also has animal and environmental science, leadership and community service.
pay_detail: The page says costs are kept to a minimum. No amounts are given.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs, camps and events set their own dates.

grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
name: Maryland Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Maryland
what_you_do: Spend a week in a model state government. Delegates run for city and state office. They take part in a political simulation. They hear from real leaders. There are college prep sessions too.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 26, 2027 at McDaniel College. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.

name: Maryland FFA
what_you_do: Join an FFA chapter through your school's agricultural education program. FFA builds leadership, personal growth and career skills through agriculture classes, projects and competitions.
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your chapter advisor.
duration: School year, ongoing
deadline_text: The state site lists a deadline to confirm or add chapter affiliation membership on Oct 15, 2026 at 5 p.m. The exact time for students to join is set by each chapter.

name: Maryland General Assembly Student Page Program
org: Maryland General Assembly, Department of Legislative Services
what_you_do: Serve as a page in the Maryland House or Senate in Annapolis. You serve for two separate weeks of the 2027 session. Pages hand out materials on the floor, run errands, help visitors and carry messages.
pay_detail: A meal allowance of about $50 per day worked. The Page Office arranges lodging for pages from outside Anne Arundel County who ask for it. Pages pay their own travel to Annapolis.
duration: Two weeks that are not back to back during the 13-week session (second week of January to early April)
deadline_text: Each county sets its own application deadline and may have extra requirements. The 2027 session will have pages. Contact your county page coordinator now.

grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
name: Maryland Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Maryland
what_you_do: Spend a week in a model state government. Girls run for city, county and state office, take part in legislative sessions and a mock trial, and learn how government works.
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 25, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 25, 2027 at Salisbury University. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.

name: Woodstock Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: This is a free career training campus. The center page lists pre-apprentice training in bricklaying, building construction and carpentry. It also lists Clinical Medical Assistant. More programs are under See More.
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.

name: Youth Volunteer Sessions at MedShare
what_you_do: Sort, label and pack medical supplies in a 3-hour morning or afternoon shift. The supplies go to hospitals and clinics.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: One session at a time: Wed and Fri 9 am to noon; Thu and Sat 9 am to noon and 1 to 4 pm
deadline_text: No deadline. Register for a session before you arrive.

name: MemorialCare Long Beach Medical Center High School Volunteen Summer Program
what_you_do: Summer volunteer spots in the hospital, based on what the hospital needs. They consider your wishes but do not promise them.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: 8-week session; 2026 ran June 29 to August 21
deadline_text: The 2026 program was full and its application closed. A waitlist was offered. Next year's dates are not posted.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services
what_you_do: Members help promote and improve the library's teen programs and materials. They plan events. They help with library projects. Members earn volunteer hours.
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.
deadline_text: Rolling membership. The page is accepting applications for new members and states no deadline.

name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC), City of Menlo Park
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services Department
what_you_do: Teens advise the Parks and Recreation Commission and city staff on youth needs, activities and programs, and help plan youth services. Members serve a one-year term.
grades: Entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The 2026-27 window ran May through July 2026 (page lists a July 17, 2026 deadline). The next window is not announced.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
org: Civil Air Patrol, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
what_you_do: Join the local Civil Air Patrol squadron's cadet program. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: Ongoing. Nationally the ideal time is a weekly meeting of about two hours, one Saturday event a month and a week long summer encampment. The squadron's meeting day and time are not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can ask to join any time.

name: K-12 Concurrent Enrollment (Merced College)
what_you_do: Take real Merced College classes while you are still in high school, tuition free (limitations may apply). Talk to your high school counselor about which courses fit your schedule.
grades: K-12 students (high school students check with a counselor)
pay_detail: K-12 students can enroll in Merced College classes tuition free (limitations may apply). Some physical activity courses need an extra K-12 Permit, and some fees may still apply.
duration: By semester, including summer
deadline_text: No dates are listed on the page. Registration timing is on the College's When is Registration page.

name: EMPOWER Program (Merced County Office of Education)
what_you_do: This program helps young people who are out of school. It offers tutoring toward a GED or a diploma. You may get paid or unpaid work experience. You learn job skills and leadership. You get a mentor. It also helps you get into college or career training.
pay_detail: Paid and/or unpaid work experience; wages are not stated.
duration: Not stated; follow-up services for at least 12 months after the program
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page; it has an online interest and application form.

name: High School Regional Occupational Program (ROP)
what_you_do: Take career classes in several industry sectors at your high school as part of the Merced County ROP. The page links to a program brochure and a Career Industry Day page.
pay_detail: Cost, pay and credit are not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.

name: Dual Enrollment and Merced College Classes (Merced Union High School District)
org: Merced Union High School District and Merced College
what_you_do: You can earn college credit in high school in three ways. Take online CCAP classes made for high schoolers. Take Merced College classes outside the school day. Or take college courses built into select high school classes.
pay_detail: Free: students can take college courses at no cost, up to 11 units a semester. Textbook fees are waived for CCAP classes; textbook fees apply for concurrent enrollment.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No dates posted on the district page; check with your school's Pathway Counselor.

name: Teen Library Volunteer
org: Montgomery-Floyd Regional Library (Blacksburg and Christiansburg branches)
what_you_do: You help with library programs. You plan youth programs. You decorate the teen area and tidy shelves. You do community service projects. Shifts are 1 to 2 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Michigan Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Michigan
what_you_do: Spend a week running a mock state government and court system with students from across Michigan. You learn how state government works. You also practice leadership.
pay_detail: Cost to the student is not stated on the pages read. The page asks people to donate to send a young woman to Girls State.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
deadline_text: The 86th session is June 13 to 19, 2027 at Michigan State University. The 2027 application is posted online. No closing date is stated on the flyer or page.

name: American Legion Michigan Boys State
city: Hillsdale, MI (2026 session at Hillsdale College); office in Lansing
what_you_do: Spend a week in a model Michigan state government. Citizens are split into two parties, hold city, county and state elections, and learn how state government works. It is for rising seniors.
pay_detail: $25 application fee paid by the student. The $400 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as a local American Legion Post or other community group (2026 brochure).
duration: One week (2026: June 21 to 27)
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 21 to 27, 2026 at Hillsdale College; application deadline was June 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the pages read.

name: Michigan DECA chapters and state conference
org: Michigan DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
what_you_do: Join a DECA chapter and learn business skills in marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship. Chapters compete at the Michigan state conference.
pay_detail: $17 per student member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Michigan DECA conference is March 11 to 13, 2027 at Huntington Place in Detroit. No membership deadline is posted.

name: Michigan FFA membership through a school ag class
what_you_do: Join a Michigan FFA chapter through a school agriculture class. FFA builds leadership and career skills. These are in agriculture, food and natural resources.
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No membership deadline is posted.

name: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
org: Michigan Technological University, Summer Youth Programs
what_you_do: Take a week-long exploration course at Michigan Tech. Topics run from STEM and engineering to business, the arts and the humanities. You can live on campus or commute.
grades: Middle and high school (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Exploration programs start at $1,175 live-in (tuition, fees, meals, room and board) or $700 commuter. A $150 non-refundable deposit is due at registration. Pathway program fees vary. Scholarships exist.
duration: Week-long programs
deadline_text: 2027 registration and program dates are not posted yet on the pages read. Balances are due in full by May 1 and most scholarships are reviewed on a rolling basis.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Michigan Wing
what_you_do: Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. Cadets lead small teams and study aerospace. They sometimes fly in CAP aircraft. They go to a week-long summer encampment.
pay_detail: Annual dues are $40 for cadets. The page estimates a fully active cadet could spend $300 to $600 in the first year, minus help for uniforms and overnight fees.
duration: Weekly 2-hour meeting, about one Saturday event a month, and one week-long summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.

name: WIOA Youth Program through your local Michigan Works! agency
org: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, delivered by local Michigan Works! agencies (Michigan Works! Southeast for Washtenaw County, Capital Area Michigan Works! for the Lansing area)
what_you_do: This is free job-readiness help for young people who face barriers. It includes tutoring and mentoring. You can get paid and unpaid work experience. That includes summer jobs. You get skills training and help planning for college or a career.
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.
duration: Varies by local agency
deadline_text: Operated year round by local Michigan Works! agencies. No state deadline is posted.

name: YMCA Michigan Youth in Government
what_you_do: Join a school or YMCA delegation. You take part in a student-run model government. There are fall district conferences. There is a big Lansing conference in February or April.
pay_detail: The base fee is not stated on the page read. A $25 late fee applies to late Lansing registration. A financial aid application is linked on the page.
duration: Fall district conference, then a Lansing conference of about four days
deadline_text: 2026-27: February Lansing conference Feb 18 to 21, 2027, regular registration Nov 10 to Dec 27, late Dec 28 to Jan 13. April Lansing conference Apr 22 to 25, 2027, regular registration Nov 10 to Feb 28, late Mar 1 to 17. Fall district conferences are scheduled Oct 2 to Nov 9, 2026 (registration closes two weeks before each), so some may already be closed.

name: Opportunity Youth Program, Middlesex College
what_you_do: This program provides education and job training for out-of-school youth. It offers high school equivalency prep. It also offers paid training in in-demand jobs. You do career exploration, work readiness and work experience.
pay_detail: Paid training and work experience are listed; the wage is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates listed.

name: Milpitas Youth Advisory Commission
what_you_do: Youth commissioners advise the Milpitas City Council. They advise on matters that affect youth and teens. The commission meets monthly at the Milpitas Teen Center.
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)
deadline_text: The city says commission applications are accepted year-round, and appointments are made as needed. No closing date is stated.

name: Teens at Mingei
what_you_do: Join a cohort of teens. It has 15 Wednesday evening sessions from October to May. You earn a $750 stipend for full participation.
pay_detail: $750 for full participation
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications ran March 2 to April 1, 2026, with interviews April 20 to 24 and notices in August. Next cycle not posted; expect a similar spring window.

name: Step Up (Foundations level)
org: City of Minneapolis, Community Planning and Economic Development
what_you_do: You get a paid summer internship. Employers include parks, community groups, public agencies and nonprofits. The internship builds your first work experience. You get mentoring. You must finish a required orientation first.
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 window was Jan 5 to Mar 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted; the city says applications open each January and offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.

name: Minnesota 4-H
org: University of Minnesota Extension, Minnesota 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: Join a local 4-H club or county program. You learn by doing and grow as a young person outside of school.
grades: Kindergarten through one year past high school (grade 13)
pay_detail: Minnesota 4-H does not charge a state membership fee. Some local clubs or programs charge dues, and help may be available.
duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: No fixed deadline on the Join page. Membership lasts Oct. 1 to Sept. 30 and you re-enroll each year.

name: Minnesota American Legion Boys State
what_you_do: Spend a week at Saint John's University running a pretend government. You elect city, county and state officials. You go to classes and mock trials. You hear political speakers.
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted. Each sponsor sets its own. Ask your school counselor or a local American Legion Post.

name: Minnesota DECA (high school)
org: Minnesota DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
what_you_do: Join your school's DECA chapter to learn business and marketing. You take part in DECA programs and contests, such as role plays. Minnesota DECA holds a yearly state conference.
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines are set by the state advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 28 to Mar 2, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency Minneapolis.

name: Minnesota FFA
what_you_do: Join an agriculture class and your school's FFA chapter. You build leadership and career skills. Members can go to leadership conferences, a winter leadership summit and the State FFA Convention.
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.

name: Minnesota House High School Page Program
org: Minnesota House of Representatives, Sergeant at Arms Office
what_you_do: Spend one week at the State Capitol. You page on the House floor, sit in a mock committee meeting, and meet legislators, judges, lobbyists and reporters.
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
deadline_text: Complete applications are due by end of business on Nov 10, 2026 for the 2027 session. Selected students are told by email by mid-December.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Minnesota Wing
city: Statewide, MN (squadrons in Duluth, St. Paul, Alexandria and more)
what_you_do: Join a local squadron to learn leadership, aviation, fitness and character. You wear an Air Force style uniform and earn promotions. You plan activities. You have no duty to join the military.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron meeting first.

name: Minnesota Youth Council
what_you_do: Be one of the young people who advise the Governor and state lawmakers on issues that affect youth. You research issues, meet your legislators and hold a town hall in your district.
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
deadline_text: The 2026 round (for the 2026 to 2028 term) took applications from January to March 2026: Feb 28 for priority consideration, Mar 31 for all applications. No 2027 dates are posted. Seats also open when members graduate or step down.

name: ZooTeen volunteers
what_you_do: Help run Zoo Camps: keep track of campers, help with crafts and activities, and be a role model for younger kids.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
deadline_text: Applications for the Summer 2026 ZooTeen camp season are closed. The page says to check the website in 2027 for next summer.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment
what_you_do: High schoolers take Mission College classes. Enrollment fees are waived and you pay only for books and materials.
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. Follow the term dates.

name: MOCA Teen Program (paid)
org: The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles (MOCA)
what_you_do: Teens work with local artists and museum staff, plan and run MOCA Teen Night, and manage the Teens social media account. The group meets at MOCA on Thursday nights and some weekends.
pay_detail: Teens are paid. The page does not give an amount.
duration: 2026-27 group starts mid-September 2026
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed (over 130 applied). The next window is not posted.

name: Montgomery County Recreation seasonal part-time jobs
what_you_do: Seasonal county jobs such as camp counselor, scorekeeper, field supervisor, lifeguard, swim instructor and cashier at pools, recreation centers, camps and parks.
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer camp positions fill in spring.

name: Summer RISE
org: Montgomery County Public Schools, Department of Partnerships
what_you_do: You get a 5-week, 50-hour summer work experience. It is with a business, agency, college or nonprofit. The field is one you choose. It can be in person, virtual or both.
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Student registration opens in January and runs January to February (year not stated on the page). Placements are announced in April or May.

name: TeenWorks Employment Program
what_you_do: You work as a county employee at a host site. Host sites include afterschool programs, a farm, communications, finance and special events. You have a coach. You get 30 hours of job training. You finish a capstone project.
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
deadline_text: Application windows on the page: Jan 2 to Mar 30 (spring/summer) and Aug 1 to Nov 30 (fall/winter). The page does not state the year, so the fall/winter window may be open now.

name: Montgomery Parks volunteering and Student Service Learning hours
city: Montgomery County, MD (park sites countywide; office in Wheaton)
what_you_do: Help at stream and park cleanups and natural surface trail workdays. Some chances are approved for Student Service Learning hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Browse the opportunities list and sign up for events.

name: MSM S.T.E.A.M. Academy (Grades 9 to 12)
what_you_do: Choose a 3-week series of health and STEAM workshops. Or choose a 6-week research project with an MSM mentor. You work alongside faculty and graduate students.
grades: Rising 9th to 12th (3-week option). Rising 10th to 12th (6-week research option)
pay_detail: 3-week option $1,000. 6-week research option $1,500. No stipend listed.
duration: 3 weeks (June 1 to 19, 2026) or 6 weeks (June 2 to July 10, 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 26 and closed Mar 25, 2026 (reviewed on a rolling basis). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Summer Pre-College Program
what_you_do: Take online college courses taught by Morehouse faculty. Plan on about 50 minutes a day, Monday to Friday. You earn Morehouse College credit for each course you pass.
pay_detail: $3,500 flat fee for up to three courses, plus up to $100 per course for books and a $30 non-refundable application fee
duration: About 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026, finals July 6 to 10)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Jan 5 to Mar 15, 2026, decisions Apr 5, payment due May 1. 2027 dates not posted.

grades: New applicants enter 7th, 8th or 9th grade this fall (Tree Monitor spots for new people are for high school age)
duration: June through August, with some optional fall weekends
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
name: Youth Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Help in the Children's Garden as a Naturalist or Gardener. Or track how trees change through the seasons as a Tree Monitor. Returning volunteers can help at the summer science camp.
deadline_text: The page says applications are reviewed in April each year. An exact deadline is not posted. Email youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org to get deadline notices.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center
what_you_do: Teens join summer camps as Junior Leaders, help swim lessons as Junior Lifeguards, or assist at Deer Hollow Farm camps as interns. Training is included and it is free.
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 Teen Summer Volunteer Program open in late winter or early spring 2027. No closing date posted yet.

name: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
what_you_do: Middle and high school students advise the City Council on teen issues, support The View Teen Center and plan teen events. Meets twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated
duration: School year, August to June
deadline_text: Page still shows an 'Apply now for 2026-2027' banner but gives no closing date; applications opened Feb 6, 2026. Recruitment for the next school year opens each February.

name: GROW CELLS Cancer Research Summer Program
org: Morehouse School of Medicine, Cancer Health Equity Institute
what_you_do: Learn about cancer research in summer sessions. You do fieldwork and a practicum. You go to a cancer research symposium.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask the program about cost or stipend.
duration: 2026: presentations June 1 to 19 (Mon to Thu, 10 am to 3 pm), fieldwork July 7 to 18, symposium July 21 to 22
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application deadline May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: High School Ambassadors Track (Health Careers Exposure Program)
what_you_do: Four weeks of hands-on health science. You do lab work, tutoring, SAT/ACT prep and workshops. You also job shadow and do community projects.
pay_detail: $1,000 program cost
duration: 4 weeks (2026 program dates not stated on the page)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: apply Feb 1 to Mar 27, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)
org: Metropolitan Transportation Commission (with ABAG, BCDC and the Bay Area Air District)
city: Bay Area (virtual sessions, final session in San Francisco)
what_you_do: A summer program introducing high school students to regional problems like transportation planning, housing, environmental justice (how pollution and development affect different communities) and air quality. You hear talks from experts at partner agencies.
pay_detail: Stipend paid after completion; amount not stated
duration: 2026: virtual Thursday evening sessions in July plus a final in-person session at Bay Area Metro Center, San Francisco (July 31, 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 program is over. The 2026 call was announced March 24, 2026; exact open and close dates are not on the page. 2027 not posted.

name: Summer Camp Youth Volunteer
what_you_do: Youth volunteers help camp staff set up the classroom each day. They work directly with campers. They help with experiments, projects and activities.
duration: Camp weeks; schedule not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No 2027 deadline posted on the pages read. Check with the museum in early 2027.

name: NAACP/JMRL Paid Library Internship and Scholarship
org: Jefferson-Madison Regional Library and Albemarle-Charlottesville NAACP
what_you_do: This is a paid library internship. It has 200 hours of library work experience. It aims to get local students to think about library careers. There is also a yearly scholarship.
grades: Entering 12th grade, or age 17 or older
pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)
duration: 200 hours of library work
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications due 5 pm, March 27, 2026; award announced by April 30, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

duration: One day, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
pay_detail: The fair itself is free. Employers there hire for paid jobs.
name: Naperville Community Job Fair
what_you_do: Meet hiring managers face to face. Past fairs also offered resume reviews, mock interviews and money basics. There was also a high school panel on career paths in Illinois.
deadline_text: Saturday, January 2, 2027, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., Fort Hill Activity Center, 20 Fort Hill Drive, Naperville.

duration: Application in fall. Event runs 30 to 90 minutes in June, July or August 2027
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library pays for the program supplies.
name: Teen Pitch Program
what_you_do: A team of 2 to 5 teens pitches an idea for a library event. If your team is picked, the library pays for supplies and helps you plan and run the event in summer 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026 application ran August 1 to September 30, 2026 and is closed. The page does not give 2027 dates. Teams picked for the in-person pitch are contacted by mid October 2026.

grades: Volunteers: 9th grade and up. TAG: grades 6 to 12
duration: TAG meets once a month for two hours at rotating library locations
pay_detail: Unpaid. TAG members earn community service hours for each meeting.
name: Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
what_you_do: Volunteer at the library. Or join TAG, a monthly group. Teens work with teen librarians on events, books, games and teen spaces.
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.

duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. Ask the city.
name: Mayor's Chief of Staff Internship (KidsMatter)
what_you_do: Support the mayor at community events. You greet people, answer questions and take photos. Hours follow the event schedule, with some evenings and weekends.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.

duration: Seasonal. Summer jobs include Centennial Beach and the Paddleboat Quarry.
pay_detail: Pay is listed on each job posting, not on the main employment page.
name: Seasonal and Part-Time Jobs (Centennial Beach, camps, parks)
what_you_do: Apply for seasonal and part-time park district jobs. Jobs include lifeguard, swim teacher, camp counselor and paddleboat attendant. You can also work at concessions, park upkeep or a golf course.
deadline_text: The page's table says Centennial Beach jobs (lifeguard, concession, swim instructor), paddleboat jobs, camp counselors and Knoch Knolls nature camp jobs are usually posted in mid December. Other jobs post in May, June or August. The Community Job Fair is January 2, 2027.

duration: Dates listed this fall (no year printed; the weekdays match 2026): Kids' Night Out on Fridays, Nov 20 to Dec 18, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m. Santa's Workshop on Dec 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17 and 20.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The district can sign off on volunteer hours for school.
name: Volunteer Programs and Events (ages 14 and up)
what_you_do: Help run park district events. Examples are Kids' Night Out (climbing, crafts and games) and Santa's Workshop (greeting families, photos, goody bags). There are also Nature Champion volunteer days. You can get proof of your hours for school.
deadline_text: Apply at least two weeks before the date you want to volunteer. Santa's Workshop runs December 1 to 20 and Kids' Night Out runs November 20 to December 18 (no year printed on the page; weekdays match 2026).

duration: Ongoing, two meetings a month
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Cadets help with security and traffic control at events.
name: Police Cadet Program
what_you_do: Meet at the police department twice a month for training. You help with security and traffic at community events during the year.
deadline_text: No deadline is stated on the page.

grades: In high school or entering high school
duration: 6 weeks, Thursday nights 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: Free
name: Youth Academy
what_you_do: Take a free six week course on police work. It covers patrol, K-9 dogs, investigations, the special response team and forensics, with hands-on demos.
deadline_text: 2026 class: June 11 to July 23, 2026, applications due June 4, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.

duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term; most boards meet in the evening
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer role.
name: Student Representatives on City Boards and Commissions
what_you_do: Sit on a city board or commission as a student rep. You might join the Library Board, Planning and Zoning, the Riverwalk board or the Transportation Advisory Board. You start with a leadership orientation.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.

name: NASA Citizen Science Projects
what_you_do: Join one of 49 NASA science projects online. Examples include classifying images or tracking clouds. You need only a phone or laptop.
pay_detail: Free
duration: Whenever you want
deadline_text: Always open.

name: NASA GeneLab for High Schools (GL4HS)
city: Virtual (hosted by NASA Ames, Mountain View, CA)
what_you_do: This is a 12-week online program. You go at your own pace. It takes about 20 hours a week. Topics include space biology and bioinformatics. Bioinformatics means using computers to study biology data. Computational biology is also a topic.
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (and college freshmen)
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026, or until 1,000 applicants. 2027 dates not posted.

name: High School Career Academy
what_you_do: This six-month program introduces you to several health care career paths. It includes paid shadowing. You have a chance to earn credentials that the industry recognizes.
pay_detail: Paid; amount not stated
duration: November to April; two evening sessions a month (4:30 to 8 p.m.)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026-2027 is closed. 2027-28 dates are not posted.

name: Youth and Young Adult Employment Program (paid summer work experience)
what_you_do: You get a paid summer placement. It is a work-learning job in a hospital department. It is about 4 hours a day. It includes career exploration. You also get mentorship and financial literacy.
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated
duration: 4 or 8 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 30)
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Feb 2 and closed March 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: North Carolina 4-H teen programs
org: North Carolina 4-H, NC Cooperative Extension (NC State and NC A&T)
city: Statewide, North Carolina (local 4-H office in every county)
what_you_do: Join 4-H through your county office. Then take part in teen leadership and service programs. They are NC 4-H Congress, the State Council, the Honor Club and the new Clover Crew.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages read. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Programs and events vary by county and have their own dates on the NC 4-H calendar.

grades: Middle and high school (the page says national FFA has members in grades 5 to 12)
name: North Carolina FFA
org: North Carolina FFA Association (NC State University Agricultural Education)
what_you_do: Join an FFA chapter at your school. Learn hands-on agriculture skills. Run a supervised agricultural experience project. Compete in leadership and career events.
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $12 for high school students ($7 national plus $5 state) and $8 for middle school students ($7 national plus $1 state). Many chapters collect these through the school.
duration: Membership year runs Aug 1 to July 31
deadline_text: The membership year runs Aug 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027. The state membership deadline is March 1, 2027.

grades: High school students or recent high school graduates
name: North Carolina Governor's Page Program
org: North Carolina Office of the Governor, hosted by VolunteerNC
what_you_do: Spend a four-day page week in Raleigh working on state government. Pages develop a policy proposal with officials. They tour government and historic sites. They do tasks for state departments. They plan a service project.
pay_detail: $200 stipend per week to help with travel and lodging costs. A limited number of host families provide meals and rides for a $100 fee paid by the page.
duration: One page week of four days (Monday afternoon, then Tuesday to Thursday)
deadline_text: The application for 2026 is closed. The page says applications are taken on a rolling basis until spots are filled, so apply as soon as the next application opens. No 2027 dates are posted.

name: North Carolina Governor's School
city: Raleigh and Greensboro, NC (Meredith College and Greensboro College)
what_you_do: Live on a college campus for four weeks and study one subject in depth: English, math, natural science, social science, Spanish, or an arts area. There are no grades or tests.
grades: Grade 11 when nominated (grades 10 and 11 for dance, choral music and instrumental music)
pay_detail: $600 tuition per student, collected through the school or district. Need-based scholarships are offered by the NC Governor's School Foundation. Families pay for travel.
duration: Four weeks (June 20 to July 17, 2027)
deadline_text: Application forms were released in Sept 2026. Local school deadlines vary and come in fall 2026. Selection news goes out in early to mid March 2027.

name: North Carolina House Page Program
org: North Carolina General Assembly, House of Representatives
what_you_do: Serve for one week in the state House of Representatives in Raleigh. Pages work in the House chamber and at committee meetings, deliver messages and bills, and help with mailings.
grades: Current sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12)
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.
duration: One week, Monday to Thursday, while the legislature is in session
deadline_text: Information on the 2027 House Page Program will be posted late this fall (2026). Applications are taken on a first-come basis until all spots for the session are full.

name: Job Corps in North Carolina (Schenck, Kittrell, Oconaluftee)
org: U.S. Department of Labor, Job Corps
city: Pisgah Forest, Kittrell and Cherokee, NC
what_you_do: Live on a free career training campus. You train for a trade. You also finish a high school diploma or equivalent. Schenck and Oconaluftee are Forest Service conservation centers. They have wildland firefighting and forestry training.
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.

name: Lady Cardinal Mentorship Program
org: NC Department of Administration, Division for Women and Youth
what_you_do: Work for four weeks in a North Carolina state agency in the Raleigh area. You work next to women leaders in science, technology, engineering or math careers. You finish a group project.
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (girls; rising 9th graders cannot apply)
pay_detail: $1,700 stipend, paid on the second to last day of the program. No housing is provided.
duration: 4 weeks, 40-hour weeks Monday to Friday (July 2027, exact dates not posted yet)
deadline_text: 2027 plan: applications open early Jan 2027 and close in Feb 2027 (the FAQ says the firm deadline is the end of February). Phone interviews in March, notices in April, program in July 2027.

name: Junior Curators
org: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
what_you_do: Teens support the museum's conservation work. They help with programs and events. They also do field experiences and service projects. They care for the live animal collection. The work runs September to April.
pay_detail: $75 per year (snacks, T-shirt, boots and protective eyewear); optional trips may cost extra for travel
duration: September to April. One monthly meeting with Living Collections staff plus two monthly group meetings with scientists (3:30-5 pm).
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period has closed. Applications reopen in January 2027 and are due in March 2027 for 2027-28 (exact day not posted).

name: Junior Interpreters
org: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
what_you_do: Teens work on the museum floor for 10 summer weeks. They talk with visitors. They use natural history specimens to teach. They build speaking and customer service skills.
pay_detail: $75 per summer (covers orientation, food, T-shirt, nametag and props)
duration: 10 weeks, June 15 to August 19. One shift a week (Tue, Wed or Thu, 10-1 or 1-4). Required orientation Saturday May 15.
deadline_text: Applications open mid-January 2027 and are due 5 pm Monday, March 22, 2027. Group interviews April 13-15, 2027, 3:30 to 5:00 pm; top applicants are invited.

name: North Carolina Senate Page Program
what_you_do: Spend one week working in the state Senate in Raleigh. Pages work on the Senate floor and in committee meetings, deliver messages and papers, and help with office tasks.
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.
duration: One week during the legislative session: report Monday afternoon, work Tuesday to Thursday
deadline_text: The 2026 program is full. Available weeks for the 2027 session will be posted early next year. When it opens, applications are taken on a rolling basis until weeks are full.

name: SkillsUSA North Carolina
what_you_do: Join a SkillsUSA chapter in your career and technical education class. Build job skills and take on leadership roles. Compete in state and national skills contests.
pay_detail: Student membership is $14, per the NC SkillsUSA join page.
duration: School year
deadline_text: To compete at the national level, a student must be joined in membership on the SkillsUSA national site by March 1 each year.

grades: Second or third year of high school (rising juniors and seniors)
name: Summer Ventures in Science and Mathematics
org: North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics (NCSSM), state funded
city: Appalachian State, East Carolina, UNC Charlotte and UNC Wilmington campuses, NC
what_you_do: Live on a UNC system campus for about four weeks. You do a hands-on STEM research project with faculty. You often work in a small team. Recent topics include ecology, biochemistry, DNA analysis and cybersecurity.
pay_detail: No cost to accepted students. Meals and housing on campus are included. It does not pay a wage.
duration: About four weeks between mid-June and end of July 2027, depending on the campus
deadline_text: Application opens Oct 15, 2026 at cfnc.org. Essays are due Jan 5, 2027. Transcripts and teacher and counselor forms are due Feb 28, 2027. Decisions come Apr 2, 2027.

name: Tar Heel Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of North Carolina
what_you_do: Spend a week in a pretend state government. Delegates run for office, pass bills, hold court sessions and learn how city, county and state government work.
pay_detail: $500 per delegate for lodging, meals and two uniform shirts. A local American Legion post, business or community group often pays it. Families with money worries are told to contact the program.
duration: One week (the 87th session is June 20 to 26, 2027)
deadline_text: Application opens Nov 1, 2026. No closing date is posted yet.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, North Carolina Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, North Carolina Wing
city: Statewide, North Carolina (squadrons in many towns)
what_you_do: Cadets fly, learn to lead, hike, camp and get in shape. Teens meet weekly with a local squadron and can go to summer encampments and other wing events.
pay_detail: Annual cadet dues are $60 for North Carolina in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the pages read.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time through a local squadron.

name: North Carolina Youth Apprenticeship
city: Statewide, North Carolina (employers and community college partners)
what_you_do: Work a paid job with a mentor at an employer while taking related classes at a community college or training center. You can start as early as 16 while in high school.
pay_detail: Apprentices are paid employees from day one, with raises as you gain skills. The wage depends on the employer and is not stated.
duration: Varies by apprenticeship
deadline_text: No single deadline. Each employer or program sets its own hiring.

name: Youth Legislative Assembly
what_you_do: Take part in a mock legislative session with other high school students. You debate and vote on issues about local, state and national government.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.
duration: A conference of about three days (the 2025-26 session was March 13 to 15, 2026)
deadline_text: The 2025-26 conference was March 13 to 15, 2026. Dates for the next conference are not posted yet.

grades: Rising 6th graders through recent high school graduates (Junior Wildlife Assistant: grades 10 and 11 when you apply)
name: North Carolina Zoo Teen Volunteer Program
org: North Carolina Zoo and Botanical Gardens
what_you_do: Volunteer at the zoo each summer. High school teens can be Junior Wildlife Assistants at the Wildlife Rehabilitation Center. Jobs are diets, cleaning, feeding and vet observation. Teens can also join Camp Crew. Middle schoolers have other roles.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time $20 onboarding fee for new volunteers, which can be waived for families with financial hardship.
duration: Summer only, May through August. Junior Wildlife Assistant: 6 weeks, 13 to 15 hours a week (last season June 17 to July 31)
deadline_text: Recruitment for this season has ended. The FAQ says summer-only applications opened April 9 in 2026, and the Junior Wildlife Assistant page listed an April 22 deadline (no year printed). Check the site again in spring 2027.

name: NC State Rising 11th-12th Grade Residential Engineering Camps
org: NC State College of Engineering, The Engineering Place
what_you_do: You live on the NC State campus in Raleigh for a week. You work in one engineering workshop. Hours are 9 am to 4 pm, Monday to Thursday. There are evening activities. A Friday showcase is for families.
pay_detail: $1,550 camp fee in 2026, no refunds. A limited amount of financial aid is available for demonstrated need.
duration: 1 week (2026 weeks: June 14-19, June 21-26, July 5-10, July 12-17)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: portal open January 12 to February 27, 2026; decisions March 27, 2026. The page says to watch for 2027 camp information.

name: Soup Kitchen Volunteering, Elijah's Promise
what_you_do: You help prepare and serve meals. You clean and greet guests. This is at the Elijah's Promise soup kitchen. Shifts are on weekday and Saturday mornings.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Court-ordered service hours are not accepted.
duration: One shift at a time, Monday to Saturday between 8:00 am and 12:30 pm
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts online; if none show, they are filled.

grades: Entering 9th or 10th grade (apply in 8th or 9th grade)
name: Rutgers 4-H STEM Ambassadors Program
what_you_do: This is a year-round, multi-year STEM program. It includes a summer week at Rutgers-New Brunswick. You take lab tours and do research projects. You go to monthly meetings. You lead STEM activities for younger kids.
pay_detail: Free: direct summer program expenses are paid by a scholarship valued at $1,000. No wage or stipend is listed.
duration: Year-round, multi-year; 2026 summer program at Rutgers-New Brunswick was July 6 to 10
deadline_text: 2026 cohort application closed. The page says check back in early 2027 for the next cohort.

grades: Current high school students (graduating seniors not eligible)
name: Rutgers Summer Scholars Program
org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick Pre-College Summer Programs
what_you_do: You can take up to two approved college-level courses at Rutgers-New Brunswick. You earn college credit. You take them during the summer.
pay_detail: 2026 rates per credit: in-state $482 (Arts and Sciences) to $551 (SEBS), out-of-state $1,148 to $1,338, plus a one-time $162 student fee. Courses are typically 3 credits; up to two courses.
duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened February 2; last day to apply May 17 (Session I) and June 28 (Session II). 2027 dates not posted.

grades: Entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in fall 2026, with at least one high school biology course
name: Toxicology, Health and Environmental Disease (THED) High School Summer Program
org: Rutgers Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences Institute (EOHSI)
what_you_do: This is a one-week summer camp in the daytime. It is on the Rutgers Busch campus. It focuses on basic lab techniques and toxicology topics.
pay_detail: $975 non-refundable camp fee covers tuition, manuals, materials, safety equipment, lab supplies and lunch. Need-based financial aid may be available. No housing or transportation provided; no stipend.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: enrollment opened January 5, 2026; deadline was Monday, March 2, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics
what_you_do: This is a four-week residential summer program on the Busch campus. It is for math-talented high school students. You solve discrete math problems.
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
deadline_text: 2026: reviewed first come, first served from February 2026; completed application, including solutions to the problems, by March 31 if seeking a scholarship; financial aid applications by April 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Teen / High School Volunteers, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
org: RWJBarnabas Health, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
what_you_do: You greet, direct and escort visitors. You visit patients on nursing floors. You help with patient discharges. This is at the hospital's New Brunswick or Somerset campus.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
deadline_text: No application deadline or dates are listed on the page.

grades: High school students who completed a high school biology course
name: Waksman Institute Summer Experience (WISE)
org: Waksman Institute of Microbiology, Rutgers University
what_you_do: This is two weeks of lab work and bioinformatics. The work is on duckweed DNA at the Waksman Institute. Students' vetted sequences are published on GenBank with their names.
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
deadline_text: 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and was first come, first served (sessions expected to fill). Application forms for the Summer 2027 WISE Programs will be posted in late January 2027.

name: New Jersey 4-H Youth Development
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club, after-school program or camp and learn by doing. Topics are science, arts, healthy living, outdoors, leadership and citizenship.
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Ongoing clubs and programs; camp is a week in summer
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs and programs run through the year.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Jersey Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New Jersey
city: New Jersey (2026 session at Centenary University)
what_you_do: Spend a short summer session in a mock government. You learn how city, county and state government work by holding pretend offices.
grades: Junior in high school when applying
pay_detail: No pay. Sponsors (units, posts or other groups) enroll and sponsor delegates; the site does not list a fee to the student.
duration: About 5 days (2026: Sunday June 21 to Thursday June 25)
deadline_text: 2026 sponsorships were filled and no applicants were being accepted. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: American Legion Jersey Boys State
org: American Legion Department of New Jersey
what_you_do: Spend a week in a mock state government. You hear speakers, join discussions, run for office and take part in a sports program.
grades: 11th grade (junior) with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Post-sponsored: parents pay a $50 non-refundable fee and the post pays the rest. Self-sponsored: $50 non-refundable application fee plus $325 tuition if accepted (food, housing and supplies included). Scholarships may be available.
duration: One week; delegates arrive on Father's Day (the 80th session began June 21, 2026)
deadline_text: For the 2026 session (began June 21, 2026) the home page said applications were open through June 7. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, New Jersey Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, New Jersey Wing
city: New Jersey (local squadrons across the state)
what_you_do: Join a local squadron for weekly meetings. Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. Wear a uniform. Move up in rank as you take on more leadership.
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.

name: Governor's School of New Jersey in Engineering and Technology
org: Rutgers School of Engineering / State of New Jersey
what_you_do: This is a free, four-week residential summer program for rising seniors. You take four courses. You do a small team research and design project. You visit companies. A final research symposium ends the program.
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
deadline_text: 2027 application not posted on the pages read. The state page (updated 11/13/25) said 2026 applications were open; decisions are emailed in early April. Ask your school counselor about the school nomination deadline.

name: New Jersey Youth Corps
org: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development
city: New Jersey (local sites across the state)
what_you_do: Work in crews of 6 to 10 on community service and conservation projects. You spend about half your time on school work. It goes toward a diploma or equivalent.
pay_detail: Corpsmembers get a stipend while enrolled. The amount is not stated on the state page.
duration: Full time, year-round program; length of each cohort is not stated on the state page
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The program is described as year-round.

name: New Jersey Youth Institute (World Food Prize)
org: Rutgers School of Environmental and Biological Sciences, with the World Food Prize Foundation
what_you_do: Write a paper on a global food or hunger issue, then present your research and ideas in a short speech and small groups at Rutgers. Some students are invited to a national event in Iowa.
pay_detail: Free to take part (no registration cost). For students invited to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines, most expenses are covered by the World Food Prize, but travel is not included.
duration: One day (2026 date: March 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: registration and paper due by February 6, 2026; the Institute was March 6, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: New York State 4-H
org: Cornell Cooperative Extension, New York State 4-H
city: New York State (run through county Cornell Cooperative Extension offices)
what_you_do: Join a 4-H club or independent membership. Do hands-on projects. Topics are science, agriculture and arts. Others are leadership and community service.
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the pages read. Ask your county office.
duration: 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30; you can re-enroll each year
deadline_text: No single deadline. The 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, New York Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, New York Wing
city: New York (local squadrons across the state)
what_you_do: Join a local squadron for weekly meetings. Learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. Wear a uniform. Move up in rank as you take on more leadership.
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.

name: NYS DEC Summer Camps (Colby, DeBruce, Pack Forest, Rushford)
org: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
city: New York State (camps in Franklin County, the Catskills, Allegany County and the southern Adirondacks)
what_you_do: Spend a week at a DEC camp. You learn outdoor skills like backpacking, canoeing and fishing. You study habitats and ecology. Some weeks offer hunter education.
pay_detail: $350 per camper per week, with meals and trips included. Transportation to and from camp is not included. Many campers are sponsored by local conservation groups, clubs and community groups.
duration: One week, Sunday afternoon to Friday afternoon (2026 teen weeks ran July 12 to Aug 7, depending on the camp)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026 opened Sunday March 22, 2026 at 1 PM and weeks fill quickly (waitlist available). 2027 dates are not posted.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Empire Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New York
city: New York State (check-in at SUNY Brockport)
what_you_do: Spend a week as a citizen of a pretend 51st state. You run campaigns, write and debate bills and fill county and state offices.
pay_detail: A non-refundable application fee is required. The amount is not stated on the pages read. Optional extras (shirts, survival kit) have order forms.
duration: One week: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027 (from the site's save-the-date notice). No 2027 application deadline or registration opening is posted.

name: New York State Parks Lifeguard
org: New York State Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)
city: New York State (state parks, pools and beaches; Long Island has its own process)
what_you_do: Work as a lifeguard at a state park pool or beach during the summer season. You pass a qualifier and complete lifeguard training. On Long Island the training is 40 hours and paid.
pay_detail: Paid job. Candidates are in pay status during the mandatory 40 hours of training. The hourly rate is not stated on the page read.
duration: Seasonal; the page says the peak operating season is May through September
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted on the page read. Register for a lifeguard qualifier; the page links the qualifier dates.

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: You can help in the Children's Department. Tasks include the Summer Reading Program and craft materials. You can write book reviews from home. You can join the Young Adult Advisory Council.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
what_you_do: You volunteer next to city Recreation staff. Work at summer day camps, Pint-Sized Camp, the Marina Park Sailing & Boating Center and city events. You build leadership and work skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
what_you_do: Build a marine science project and share it with museum visitors. You learn about museum research, collections and careers, and practice public speaking.
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.

duration: Program seasons are 6 to 8 weeks. Volunteers are asked to commit for the full season.
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Part-time jobs (1 to 20 hours a week) are paid, but pay is not on the page read.
name: NISRA Volunteers and Summer Camp Jobs (Elgin and 12 other member communities)
city: Elgin and 12 other member communities, northern Illinois
what_you_do: Volunteer to give one-on-one help in recreation programs for people with disabilities. Or apply for part-time jobs like program helper and summer day camp counselor. Programs meet once a week for 1 to 3 hours.
deadline_text: No deadline. NISRA says it hires summer camp staff each winter and spring. Postings are on the ADP Workforce Now site.

grades: High school juniors and seniors when you apply
name: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP), Gaithersburg
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
what_you_do: Spend seven summer weeks in a NIST lab on the Gaithersburg campus. You work with staff scientists and engineers on your own research project and may show it at a poster session.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
deadline_text: For 2027, the job announcement is expected to open on USAJOBS in mid-October 2026, and applications are due at the end of January 2027. Another line on the page says applications generally open Nov 1 and close in the last week of January.

duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 tuition: $5,530 residential camp or $3,125 day camp. Financial aid for qualified students is given on a rolling basis while funds last.
name: Civic Leadership Institute (CTD Summer Camp)
org: Northwestern University Center for Talent Development
what_you_do: Take a 3 week college-level course on social and political issues. Do service projects with local nonprofits, meet community leaders, and make an action plan for change. Earn service hours.
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran June 28 to July 17, 2026. 2027 dates and prices are not posted yet. The program has said to apply early for aid.

duration: One day a week for 8 weeks between May and August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
name: Summer Volunteer Service for Students
org: Northwestern Medicine (Delnor in Geneva, Central DuPage in Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburban hospitals)
city: Geneva, Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburbs, IL
what_you_do: Volunteer one day a week for eight weeks in a hospital in the summer.
deadline_text: 2027 summer applications are open December 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027. The 2026 summer period is closed.

grades: Current high school juniors (rising seniors), no exceptions
duration: 4 weeks (June 27 to July 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition $5,000 including room and board. Up to $100,000 in financial aid and scholarships is available. $55 application fee.
name: Medill Cherubs Journalism Institute
org: Northwestern University, Medill School of Journalism
what_you_do: Spend 4 weeks on the Northwestern campus learning to report, write and produce news. Work with journalism faculty and professionals.
deadline_text: No applications before December 1, 2026. All materials are due by noon Central on March 1, 2027. Decisions by March 24, 2027.

duration: 4 or 6 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: $3,500 for the 4 week institute, $5,000 for the 6 week institute. $60 application fee.
name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Policy Debate Institute
what_you_do: Train in policy style debate in a 4 week or 6 week summer institute. The 2026 institute was fully online.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens this winter. Rolling admission through April or until the labs are full. 2026 dates were June 28 to July 25 (4 weeks) and June 28 to August 8 (6 weeks).

duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Film and Video Division
what_you_do: Spend 5 weeks on the Northwestern campus making films. Take courses such as acting for the screen, sound and on-set work, and finish with a festival of student films.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 9, 2026 and regular deadline March 13, 2026, with rolling late applications for some concentrations. 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.

duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Theatre Arts Division
what_you_do: Live on the Northwestern campus for 5 weeks. Take acting, voice and movement classes, work on a crew, and rehearse a full play with professional directors. Tracks: Performance, Stage Management and Design/Tech, Musical Theatre.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 2, 2026 and regular deadline February 27, 2026 (online form). 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.

name: Waterpark seasonal jobs with free training
org: NOVA Parks (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority)
city: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Alexandria and Arlington waterparks)
what_you_do: You can work summer jobs at a NOVA Parks waterpark. Jobs include attendant, lifeguard, water safety instructor and cook. Uniforms and training are free.
pay_detail: Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
deadline_text: Page says NOVA Parks is hiring; no deadline stated.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
what_you_do: You can get free career coaching and training if you are an eligible young adult. You can also take a paid internship of about 400 hours if you are 18 or older. If you are 17, you can start with coaching and work readiness.
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
what_you_do: You can get a paid summer conservation job at a national park, working outdoors on park projects. Each park runs its own program.
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.

name: ACE Mentor Program of Greater New York
org: ACE Mentor Program of Greater NY
city: Teams in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island, White Plains and Riverdale (and remote)
what_you_do: Join a free after-school team of 20 to 30 students and 12 to 15 pros in architecture, engineering and construction. You learn design software and present a team project at a year-end showcase.
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned. Scholarship and internship chances are listed as benefits.
duration: Late October through May (about 2 hours after school per meeting). Some teams start in January.
deadline_text: Team selection emails start in September. The page gives no registration dates and no closing date, and does not say whether registration is open now.

name: Arts & Entertainment Production Internship (Apollo Theater Academy)
what_you_do: A paid after-school internship at the Apollo. You see how teams build an event. Teams include fundraising, education and marketing. Others are operations, production and programming. You help shape the summer Teen Takeover event.
pay_detail: $17.00 per hour
duration: The 2026 internship ran Apr 21 to May 21, 2026, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 3 to 6 PM. The page calls it six weeks in one place and eight or ten weeks in others.
deadline_text: The spring 2026 application closed Friday, Mar 27, 2026. The next cycle is not posted. Check the Apollo page for the next cycle.

name: Technical Stage Production Internship (Apollo Theater Academy)
what_you_do: A paid summer internship with the Apollo production crew. You work on lighting, sound, video, building sets and stage design. You help put on the summer Apollo Teen Takeover event.
pay_detail: $17 per hour
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday, on site. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 21, 2026.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed June 26, 2026. Interviews were June 30 and July 1. The 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
what_you_do: Grow and harvest food in the Children's Garden, learn botany, and teach garden lessons to kids ages 4 to 12. You move up through four tiers over the years.
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
deadline_text: Submit your materials before Dec 4, 2026 to be invited to an interview. No final deadline is posted. Info session Sat Oct 17, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.

name: Upward Bound Math & Science
org: Bronx Community College (CUNY), Federal TRIO program
what_you_do: A free STEM college-prep program for high school students. In the school year you go to Saturday classes and tutoring on the BCC campus. There is also a six-week summer program, with a three-week stay in a college dorm.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the pages read. The pages do not list a cost.
duration: Academic year: 21 Saturdays from September to April, 10 AM to 2 PM plus STEM labs 2:30 to 4:30 PM. Summer: six weeks, with three weeks as a commuter at BCC and three weeks at a residential site.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the pages read.

name: Teen Council and Teen Summer
org: The Bronx Museum of the Arts
what_you_do: Paid youth internship at the museum. You meet and interview artists, help curate exhibitions, make a zine and make your own art with 11 other teens. There is also a four-week Teen Summer session.
pay_detail: Teens are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated on the pages.
duration: Teen Council: two four-month sessions a year (fall and spring), twice a week after school. Fall 2026 runs late October 2026 to mid-February 2027, Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM. Teen Summer: four weeks, three afternoons a week.
deadline_text: The Fall 2026 application closed Oct 4, 2026. The spring and summer 2027 dates are not posted yet. The page says teens can apply for fall, spring and/or summer sessions each year.

name: Brooklyn Interns for Arts and Culture (BIAC)
