what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.

grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
what_you_do: This is a 10-day commuter camp. It has lectures and lab experiences. The topics are current topics in neuroscience.
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was April 3, 2026. The page says 2027 Summer Institutes information will be posted this winter.

name: Immersion Science Program (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
what_you_do: Take an 11 week laboratory research training course on Saturdays at Fox Chase (about 30 lab hours), then present your results on week 11. The program says it is nearly all cost free for students.
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
deadline_text: The application launches in mid to late October each year and stays open about 3.5 weeks. The exact 2026 dates are not posted on the page read. Interviews are in early to mid December and letters go out by email before December 31.

grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
what_you_do: This is a free four-year STEM program. It starts in 9th grade. Each year has STEM programming. Rising seniors are paid for a 10-week lab research experience.
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.

name: Philadelphia Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Philadelphia, PA (campus; page lists transportation and no dorms)
what_you_do: Train for a career at no cost and work toward a high school diploma or equivalent. The center provides transportation. Training includes certified nurse assistant, clinical medical assistant, culinary arts, emergency medical technician, and more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

name: Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program (MSAP)
what_you_do: Work full time for eight weeks on a research project with a Monell scientist. The program is described as paid, and apprentices cannot work more than 35 hours a week.
grades: Currently enrolled in high school or an undergraduate school
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Summer 2027 program will open in October 2026. The deadline is not posted yet.

name: Art Education high school programs (Mural Arts Philadelphia)
what_you_do: Take part in an art program that meets twice a week at a high school site, in school or after school. The page says students can go on to apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the pages read. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
duration: Twice a week. The 2026 to 27 school year programs begin in late September 2026 (the page says they end in early June and prints the year 2026, which looks like a typo for 2027).
deadline_text: Rolling admission is open. The page says the fall session begins in late September 2026.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: You train for free. You earn Red Cross lifeguard certification. Then you work as a lifeguard at a city pool through the summer.
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
deadline_text: Free training is offered year-round; reserve a slot on Eventbrite.

name: Parks and Rec Summer Youth Employment Program
what_you_do: You can work at recreation centers, playgrounds and Playstreets. You can also work on special initiatives. You help younger children. You build communication and leadership skills.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Summer
deadline_text: The page still says registration closed for the C2L-PHL Summer 2025 program. No 2026 or 2027 dates posted.

name: Provost's Summer Mentorship Program (Penn)
what_you_do: Spend four weeks on Penn's campus. Pair up with one of five Penn graduate and professional schools to see careers up close. Get lessons on financial literacy, study skills, time management, SAT prep and personal statements. It usually ends with a college fair.
grades: Currently 9th or 10th grade (entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2027)
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the pages read, so ask the program before you plan around either.
duration: Four weeks, on campus. Exact summer 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: The page says the Summer Mentorship Program for 2027 will begin taking applications in January 2027. The deadline is not posted yet.

grades: Academies and Online Seminars: current 9th to 11th grade. Pre-College: current 10th to 11th grade.
name: Penn Arts and Sciences High School Summer Programs
org: University of Pennsylvania, Penn LPS High School Programs
what_you_do: Summer Academies (2 or 3 weeks, non-credit, residential), Pre-College (residential or online, for credit) and Online Seminars on topics like biomedical research, economics, forensic science and neuroscience.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
deadline_text: 2026: May 1 for Academies and Pre-College Residential/Online Session I; June 1 for Online Seminars and Pre-College Online Session II. Rolling admissions. 2027 dates not posted.

grades: Rising 9th to 12th grade (Junior PYNtern rising 9th to 10th; Senior PYNtern rising 11th to 12th)
name: PYNtern Program
what_you_do: This is paid work-based learning. It includes classroom training in professional skills. You get mentoring and career coaching. Rising juniors and seniors do about 100 hours at a paid worksite in the city.
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
deadline_text: Summer cohort applications open early March; Fall/Winter cohort open early August; Winter/Spring cohort open in November. Page says Now Recruiting for Summer + Fall 2026.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE), School District of Philadelphia
what_you_do: Career programs in over 43 occupational areas (healthcare, IT, culinary, construction and more), a three-year course of study with work-based learning such as internships and apprenticeships.
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: Follow the School Selection timeline for middle schoolers; high schoolers ask their counselor.

name: Counselor-in-Training Program, Camp Schuylkill
what_you_do: You volunteer as a counselor-in-training. You work with the Camp Schuylkill nature day camp. You help lead younger campers.
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026. Camp Schuylkill runs on a weekly schedule from June 21 to August 13, 2027.

name: Wildlife Clinic Support Volunteer, Schuylkill Center
what_you_do: You support the wildlife clinic. The clinic treats injured and orphaned wild animals. Clinic Support is for ages 16 and up. Animal Care requires age 18.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)
deadline_text: 2026 in-person info sessions were February 7 and February 28; virtual sessions as needed. Fill out the application to hear about future sessions.

name: High School Program in Biomedical Research (Wistar Institute)
what_you_do: Spend four weeks at the Wistar Institute (3601 Spruce Street) learning biomedical research, with 15 students in the program. Students attend Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.
deadline_text: The 2026 program has ended. The page says to check back in January for the 2027 summer program. Last year's cycle had interviews in April and decisions in the first week of May.

name: Volun-TEENS, Philadelphia Zoo
what_you_do: Teach zoo guests about animals and conservation. You use games and hands-on activities. You build public speaking, leadership and time management skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The page says to stay tuned for details about the next recruitment period; no dates listed.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at Piedmont Atlanta Hospital
what_you_do: Volunteer at a major Atlanta hospital over eight summer weeks. You work at least one weekday shift a week for at least six of the eight weeks and explore health careers.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $25 program fee. Uniform shirts are provided.
duration: June 8 to July 30, 2027: at least one shift a week for at least six of the eight weeks
deadline_text: Application period Feb 26 to Mar 12, 2027. Mandatory orientation Monday June 7, 2027. Up to 30 teens accepted.

grades: Grades 6 to 12 (high school volunteers: grades 9 to 12 and at least 14)
name: Teen Volunteer Program, Piscataway Public Library
what_you_do: Help with library programs and special projects. Middle schoolers can join Adopt-a-Shelf. They help keep teen spaces and collections neat. They also advise on new purchases.
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours
duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training
deadline_text: Adopt-a-Shelf: the Session 1 application period has ended; Session 2 applications open November 2 (year not stated on the page). High school volunteers attend an orientation session; check the library calendar for dates.

name: Teen Workforce Pathways (Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania
what_you_do: Get hands-on experiences, mentors and a look at real careers in several industries. Join councils and internship pathways. Get help with resumes and interview prep through the Career Works High program.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the pages read, and the page does not mention paid work. Financial assistance is available for Club membership.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Carnegie Museums)
org: Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh (Natural History, Art and Powdermill Nature Reserve)
what_you_do: Help museum staff and camp educators. You help with learning activities that support campers. The camps are run by three groups. They are the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, the Carnegie Museum of Art and Powdermill Nature Reserve.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Summer camp season. Hours and camp dates are not stated on the volunteer pages.
deadline_text: The Natural History form says the application period has closed and to check back in early 2027 for the next cycle. Dates for the next cycle are not posted.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Allegheny County Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Allegheny County Composite Squadron
what_you_do: Go to weekly squadron meetings of the Civil Air Patrol. Cadets across the country learn leadership. They also learn aerospace, fitness and character. They do things like flying, contests and summer encampments. There is also a Cyber and STEM Badge Program.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Tuesdays from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Baldwin High School, 4653 Clairton Blvd, Pittsburgh, PA 15236.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.

name: CS Scholars
what_you_do: You spend four weeks living on the CMU campus. You learn computer science through classes and group projects. You hear faculty lectures and visit tech companies. All costs are covered.
pay_detail: Fully funded: tuition, housing and meals are free; limited travel help for families with transportation barriers
duration: 4 weeks, June 26 to July 24, 2027, residential
deadline_text: Application deadline February 1, 2027. Decisions released April 1, 2027.

name: Pre-College Programs (paid tracks)
what_you_do: Live on or commute to the CMU campus for 3 to 6 weeks. Study architecture, art, design, drama or music. Also study computational biology or writing. You can also study culture. Pick the National High School Game Academy or college summer courses.
grades: 10th or 11th grade at time of application
pay_detail: 2026 prices ran from about $5,999 (3-week music, commuter) to $14,688 (summer session, residential, 2 courses), plus a $75 application fee and an $800 enrollment deposit. 2027 prices are posted in November 2026. Full scholarships for students with financial need.
duration: 3 to 6 weeks depending on the program (summer 2027 starts June 26)
deadline_text: Scholarship application deadline February 1, 2027 (decisions April 1, 2027). Basic application deadline March 1, 2027 (rolling decisions).

name: Summer Academy for Math and Science (SAMS)
what_you_do: Six weeks on the CMU campus taking math and science courses, doing a STEM research project, and getting college application help. Fully funded and merit based.
pay_detail: No cost to scholars beyond travel to and from Pittsburgh
duration: 6 weeks in person, June 26 to August 7, 2027, plus a short virtual jumpstart June 21 and 22, 2027
deadline_text: Application deadline February 1, 2027. Decisions released April 1, 2027.

name: Pittsburgh Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
what_you_do: Live on campus. You train for a career at no cost. You also earn a high school diploma or equivalent. Training includes highway construction. It includes cement masonry. Phlebotomy is another. So is clinical medical assistant. There are more.
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
org: Kamin Science Center (formerly Carnegie Science Center)
what_you_do: Greet visitors, help with exhibit demos and support science programs. Full training is provided. No science background is needed.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: Summer Teen Program and School Year Teen Program (hours per week not stated)
deadline_text: Summer Teen Program: applications open in January, deadline March 1. School Year Teen Program: applications June 1 to August 1 only. Both were closed on the day this page was read; the posted pattern is by month, with no year.

name: Summer Learn & Earn
org: Partner4Work, Allegheny County and City of Pittsburgh
what_you_do: Work a paid summer job at a local business, nonprofit or community group. You get coaching on workplace skills and career paths.
pay_detail: Paid wages (hourly rate not stated on the program page)
duration: Tier 1 and 2: June 22nd, 2026 - August 7th, 2026. Hours per week are not stated on the page.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran March 2 to June 5, 2026 and are closed. The page says applications are accepted in the spring; 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You help run bird shows and lorikeet feedings. You help at summer camp. You lead education cart activities. You prepare enrichment for the birds. Staff mentor you each day.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: 10-day sessions; orientation with a parent or guardian in late May
deadline_text: The 2026 application period has closed. For 2026 the group interviews were April 11 and April 18, 2026 and the orientation was May 30, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: EcoLeader Academy
what_you_do: Take a seven-week course at Phipps. Topics are climate change, energy, pollution, food, environmental justice and green careers. It has classes, workshops and service projects. It ends with a Youth Garden Summit.
pay_detail: Free to join. Participants receive a stipend (amount not stated on the page).
duration: Seven-week course, one afternoon a week (12:30 to 4:30 p.m.) at Phipps, plus a Youth Garden Summit at the end
deadline_text: The 2026 group is closed. The page offers a form to be told when the next group opens. The 2026 classes ran mid June to late July.

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Phipps)
what_you_do: Help camp instructors design and prepare crafts. Work with children ages 2 to 12. Clean up after daily activities at Phipps summer camps.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Clearance fees are reimbursed.
duration: Summer camps held June to August. Hours are not stated.
deadline_text: The volunteer page says applications are due Thursday, October 22, 2026. The page does not say whether that date applies to teen volunteers, so ask Phipps. Camps run June to August.

name: Gene Team
org: University of Pittsburgh, Department of Biological Sciences
what_you_do: Spend weekdays in a Pitt lab working on a current research project with other high school students, with Pitt faculty nearby for help. Weekly sessions cover applying to college.
grades: Finished one year of high school biology
pay_detail: $1,000 honorarium, paid at the end of the program
duration: Described as a four week summer program. Summer 2027 is tentatively June 28 to July 16, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open in spring 2027 and are due at the end of March, with interviews in April and acceptance notices by mid May. The exact due date is not posted yet.

name: Public Health Science Academy
org: University of Pittsburgh School of Public Health
what_you_do: This is a four week summer program at Pitt Public Health. It has talks and panels on public health careers. It has a team research project and a poster symposium. It also has field trips. You are matched with a Pitt faculty mentor.
pay_detail: Students who finish receive a $1,000 award at the end. Public transportation support to and from campus is provided, and transportation for field trips.

org: City of San Diego Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
what_you_do: You work at city pools. Recreation Aides give customer service to the aquatics community. They train to be lifeguards. Pool Guards need no certification.
pay_detail: Hourly pay is not stated on the page; see the posting on governmentjobs.com.
duration: Flexible hours that work around school and sports
deadline_text: Year-round hiring. Pool Guard hiring events are monthly; Recreation Aide interviews are quarterly.

name: San Diego Youth Commission
org: City of San Diego (Office of Child and Youth Success)
what_you_do: Advise the Mayor and City Council about youth issues. Examples are school, jobs, housing and mental health. You learn about city life, public policy and leadership. You also practice networking.
pay_detail: Not stated; this is an advisory board
duration: 2 year term, monthly meetings (currently Saturday mornings at a public library)
deadline_text: The page says some of the 20 seats are unfilled and invites youth to apply. No deadline is listed.

name: Teen Service Learner
what_you_do: You help branch staff organize library materials. You take part in library events. You earn community service hours and work experience.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.
duration: Flexible hours, weekdays and Saturdays
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Ask your branch.

name: Cuyamaca College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment
what_you_do: Take college classes for credit while still in high school. Classes can count for both high school and college. You can take up to 11 units (4 classes) on campus or online.
pay_detail: Tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay minimal fees and buy textbooks.
duration: By semester or session
deadline_text: Start at least one month before the semester or session. No set deadline on the page.

name: Feeding San Diego Volunteer
what_you_do: Help pack and hand out food. In the Distribution Center, volunteers are 6 and up. At food distributions out in the community, volunteers are 14 and up.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; you sign up for dates that work for you
deadline_text: No deadline.

name: San Diego Fire-Rescue Cadet Program
org: San Diego Fire-Rescue Department (City of San Diego)
what_you_do: Learn firefighting skills in classes taught by SDFD staff, such as hose lays, ladders, search and rescue, CPR and first aid. Certified cadets can do ride-alongs with fire crews. A one week academy runs each summer.
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a youth program
duration: Ongoing. A one week Cadet Academy is held each summer.
deadline_text: New cadets are accepted quarterly. No dates are posted.

name: San Diego Food Bank Volunteer Shifts
what_you_do: Sort and bag produce, pack food boxes and bags, and help at community food distributions. No training needed. A short orientation starts each shift.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One shift at a time. You can come once or on a regular basis.
deadline_text: No deadline. All volunteer visits must be scheduled in advance.

name: La Jolla Playhouse Summer Conservatory
what_you_do: Take an acting intensive with Playhouse artists. Rising 8th and 9th graders do a 9 day program. Rising 10th to 12th graders do a 3 week program with advanced training.
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $500 for Junior Conservatory, $850 for Conservatory. A scholarship application is offered.
duration: 9 days (Junior) or 15 weekdays (Conservatory)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Apr 6, 2026. Summer 2027 applications are expected to open on or around Feb 1, 2027. 2027 dates are not set.

name: Playhouse Teen Council
what_you_do: Join a group of high schoolers who learn how a pro theater works. You see shows and meet artists. You plan events that bring young people to the Playhouse.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: One school year (2026/27 first Teen Council meeting is listed for Oct 12, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026/27 applications ran Aug 3 to Sept 4, 2026. Next year is not posted yet; expect a similar late summer window.

name: Camp Aides (Youth Volunteers)
org: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat)
what_you_do: Help professional educators run summer camps at the museum. The camps are for Pre-K through 8th grade.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
deadline_text: Page says recruitment for camp aides begins in May. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Palomar College Concurrent Enrollment for High Schoolers
city: San Marcos, Escondido, Fallbrook and Rancho Bernardo, CA
what_you_do: Take real college classes at Palomar on campus or online while you are in high school. Dual enrollment classes can also be taught at some high schools. The classes count toward a college certificate or degree.
pay_detail: The $46 per unit tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay for books and some fees. Dual enrollment at partner high schools is free.
duration: Up to 7 units in fall or spring and 5 units in summer without a petition
deadline_text: No single deadline. Check the Palomar calendar for each term.

name: Palomar UC San Diego Health Junior Volunteer
what_you_do: Volunteer at the Poway or Escondido hospital. The page lists general roles such as lobby ambassador, escort, desk, book cart and rehab, but does not say which are open to juniors. You complete at least 100 service hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time processing fee; the amount is not on the pages read.
duration: 100 hours minimum. Juniors can do a 4-hour shift every week or every other week.
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year.

name: San Diego Parks and Recreation Volunteer Program
org: City of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department
what_you_do: Help with park clean-ups, tree planting, youth sports and recreation programs. You can also help at community events. There are roles at Tecolote Nature Center, aquatics, golf and AgeWell Services.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One-time events or regular roles
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: San Diego Police Cadet Program
org: San Diego Police Department (City of San Diego)
what_you_do: A volunteer role with no police powers. Cadets train twice a month and go on ride-alongs. They help with traffic control and security at community events.
pay_detail: Described as a voluntary position
duration: Ongoing. You finish a Cadet Academy first, then go to two meetings a month (first and third Tuesday, 6 to 9 p.m.). Time ranges from 4 hours a month to over 40.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Recruiting meetings are held on the second Tuesday of each month at 5 p.m.

name: Teen Team Program Assistant
org: San Diego Public Library (City of San Diego)
what_you_do: Join a branch Teen Team. Help library staff plan and lead programs, support teen outreach at community events, and work on special projects.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time through the City volunteer system.

grades: Grades 8 to 11 (College Apps Academy is for grade 12)
name: Reality Changers College Town
what_you_do: A free after-school and summer program. You get tutoring, mentoring and college workshops and tours. You also go on service trips, try career experiences and practice public speaking. The page says partners offer access to internships and college courses.
pay_detail: Free for students and families. Not a paid program.
duration: 3 or more hours a week after school, plus summer
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year. All applicants are added to a waitlist, and staff follow up with next steps.

name: Research Experience for High School Students (REHS)
org: San Diego Supercomputer Center, UC San Diego
what_you_do: Work for 8 weeks on a real computing research project with a UC San Diego mentor and grad students. You learn to test ideas with code and finish with a scientific poster.
pay_detail: Free to apply. Registration fee is $2,000 if accepted. Full and partial scholarships are available based on need.
duration: 8 weeks, 10 to 20 hours a week (2026 ran June 8 to July 31)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Sharp Grossmont Hospital Junior Volunteer
what_you_do: Volunteer at Sharp Grossmont Hospital for at least one year, with one shift a week or two shifts a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a uniform shirt for a small cost.
duration: At least 1 year, one shift a week or two a month
deadline_text: As of Oct 9, 2026 the page says it is no longer accepting applicants from the high school class of 2028. That means current 9th and 10th graders (classes of 2029 and 2030) may still apply. No deadline is posted.

name: Sharp Memorial and Mary Birch High School Volunteers
org: Sharp Memorial Hospital and Sharp Mary Birch Hospital (Sharp HealthCare)
what_you_do: Greet and guide patients and families, help on nursing units with phones and errands, work in a gift shop, or join Arts for Healing programs. Shifts are 3 to 4 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits listed include a cafeteria discount, meal credit and free parking.
duration: At least 1 year and 100 service hours, with 75 percent attendance
deadline_text: The high school application is closed, and the page does not say when it will reopen. The adult application reopens Oct 19.

name: UC San Diego Bioengineering Research Scholars
org: UC San Diego Department of Bioengineering and Division of Extended Studies
city: La Jolla, San Diego, CA (live online)
what_you_do: Take live online bioengineering courses with a loaner lab kit. Start with an intro course, then a research workshop, then plan and carry out your own project with a university lab.
pay_detail: Tuition $2,700 for the BE-BOAT intro course. Other course prices are on the course pages.
duration: About 7 weeks (Winter 2027 intro course: Jan 9 to Feb 27, 2027)
deadline_text: Winter 2027 application deadline Dec 18, 2026, with a last call through Jan 3, 2027. Space is limited and may fill sooner.

name: UC San Diego Health Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Help patients and staff in hospitals and clinics. Tasks include moving patients, running errands, stocking and lab deliveries. You also greet visitors and visit with patients.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for at least 100 hours over 6 to 8 months. Summer-only option: about 12 weeks and at least 100 hours.
deadline_text: Year-round application. Summer-only applicants must apply between Mar 1 and Apr 15, and say so on the application.

name: UC San Diego Marine Science Research Scholars
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies (with Scripps Institution of Oceanography mentors)
city: La Jolla, San Diego, CA (live online)
what_you_do: Take live online ocean science courses in three levels. Level 1 teaches marine biology. Level 2 is hands-on research with Scripps graduate students. Level 3 builds science writing and a chance to publish.
pay_detail: Fall 2026 Tier 1 course cost $2,000 in tuition. Scholarships were listed but closed.
duration: About 7 weeks per course (Fall 2026 Tier 1 ran Sept 22 to Nov 12)
deadline_text: Winter 2027 applications are listed as coming soon. The Fall 2026 deadline (Sept 17, 2026) has passed.

name: San Diego Workforce Partnership youth career services
what_you_do: You can sign up for free career centers. They offer training and one-on-one coaching. Some people get paid on-the-job work experience.
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.

name: San Jose Middle College (San Jose City College)
org: San Jose Unified School District with San Jose City College
what_you_do: Juniors and seniors take 2 to 3 free college classes. Those are 6 to 9 college credits. They also take 4 high school classes. This is on the San Jose City College campus. You earn a high school diploma and transferable college credit.
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Teen Book Reviewer)
what_you_do: Join Teens Reach, the library youth council, to help with kids crafts and Summer Learning sign-ups and to speak up as a library advisor. Or earn service hours by writing book reviews as a Teen Book Reviewer.
deadline_text: Rolling. Each branch has its own Teens Reach sign-up. No single deadline.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
what_you_do: You can get paid work experience and job help in San Jose. If you are 14 to 18 and face barriers to work, you can be placed in paid jobs and training. Job services are open to ages 16 to 29.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
what_you_do: Teens advise the San Jose Mayor and City Council on youth issues. The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is open now; Youth Commission recruitment is closed.
duration: Two-year term
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.

duration: At least 4 months
name: San Leandro Library Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: You help library staff run programs for younger kids, or help with kit assembly, shelving and displays. You work one shift of 2 to 3 hours a week.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.

name: San Leandro Youth Advisory Commission
org: City of San Leandro Recreation and Parks
what_you_do: You give the City Council feedback. The feedback is on issues that affect young people. You help run city events like Pumpkin Splash and the Egg Hunt.
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
what_you_do: You can take free job-skills workshops. You can use a members-only job and internship board. There are twenty $2,000 scholarships a year for San Mateo County youth. The county summer internship is for ages 18 to 21.
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
what_you_do: Teens shelve books, help with kids' crafts and STEM programs, join outreach events or support the makerspace.
duration: 6 months or 1 semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.

name: SPARK High School Internship
org: Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute
what_you_do: Spend six summer weeks as a fully paid intern in a biomedical research lab.
pay_detail: Described as fully paid; the page does not state an amount.
duration: 6 weeks, starting mid-June
deadline_text: Next application dates not posted on the page. Use the Request Info form or email the program director.

name: City of Santa Ana Student Intern
org: City of Santa Ana Human Resources
what_you_do: Work in a city department. Go to quarterly workshops to build job skills. Build mentor ties with department leaders. The city lists a Student Intern level for people enrolled in high school.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page
duration: Not stated. Interns keep their spot by sending proof of school enrollment and their GPA after each semester.
deadline_text: The city recruits interns about once a year or as needed. No dates are listed on the page.

name: City of Santa Ana Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer in City of Santa Ana departments. Fill out the volunteer handbook forms and apply through the city volunteer page. Some roles involve working with children.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Santa Ana Youth (SAY) Employment Program
org: Santa Ana WORK Center (City of Santa Ana)
what_you_do: Get a paid work placement at a public agency or a local group. The Youth Service Corps version works on climate action and food access. It also works on school and public service projects.
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the pages read.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week; hours are flexible around school
deadline_text: Conflicting city pages. The main program page says applications are now open, while the interest page says the program is currently closed to new applications and offers a form to get a notice when it reopens. Call (714) 565-2600 to confirm before applying.

name: Santa Ana Zoo Volunteers (including Zoo Buddies)
org: Santa Ana Zoo (City of Santa Ana)
what_you_do: Volunteer at the zoo, either as a short-term Zoo Greeter or in a long-term role. Younger teens can join as a Zoo Buddies pair with a parent or guardian.
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short-term: 40 hours or less (Greeter shifts Fri to Sun, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Long-term: more than 40 hours (shifts every day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
deadline_text: No deadline. Long-term volunteers do an online and an in-person orientation offered every other month.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Santa Barbara Composite Squadron 131
org: Civil Air Patrol, Santa Barbara Composite Squadron 131
what_you_do: Join weekly squadron meetings. You get hands-on flight time, STEM projects and leadership milestones. Cadets can serve on search and rescue missions as a Ground Team Member or Mission Radio Operator. They can also help at community events.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron pages do not list its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets every Wednesday from 6:00 to 8:30 p.m. and has one Saturday activity a month.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron to schedule a visit.

name: Volunteer Program (Santa Barbara Humane Society)
what_you_do: Volunteer with dogs, cats, the clinic or outreach. You go through a virtual meeting, orientation and role training, then start solo shifts.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: The page asks for at least 8 to 12 hours a month, and in another place at least two hours a week for 4 to 6 months.
deadline_text: No deadline. The page says the dog and cat volunteer opportunities are currently full.

name: Teaching Assistant Program (Santa Barbara Museum of Art)
what_you_do: Assist a Teaching Artist in art classes and camps for kids. You prepare materials. You help with hands-on art-making. You act as a role model. It includes an orientation and mentoring.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Counts toward required community service hours.
duration: Per class or camp: Winter After-School Class Tuesdays Jan 12 to Feb 16, 2027 (3:30-5:15 PM); Spring Camp Mar 29 to Apr 2, 2027 (9 AM-3 PM)
deadline_text: Winter After-School Class: apply by Dec 29, 2026 (confirmations Jan 5, 2027). Spring Camp: apply by Mar 15, 2027 (confirmations Mar 22, 2027).

name: Counselors in Training (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: You help run Nature Adventures summer camps for young children. The camps are at the Museum and Sea Center. You do crafts, exhibit visits and activities. You earn community service hours. You also learn to teach.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours. $20 uniform shirt (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: At least 3 full weeks of camp (2026 camps ran June 15 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. CIT training was June 12, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

grades: Must be in 8th or 9th grade (or that age) to apply
name: Quasars to Sea Stars (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: This is a three-to-four year program for high school teens. It has museum studies classes and learning from scientists. It includes camping, field trips and volunteering. After 60 community service hours, you become a paid Museum employee.
pay_detail: Unpaid for the first 60 community service hours, then paid Museum employee shifts. The pay rate is not stated.
duration: 3 to 4 years; stay active year-round until graduation
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications were due April 3, 2026, with in-person interviews in April and orientation week June 21-27, 2026. The page says applications for 2026 opened Feb 1, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

name: VolunTEENS (Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History
what_you_do: You help guests at interpretive tables and science games. You work in the Museum's Backyard, Butterfly Pavilion or Observatory. Shifts are on summer weekends. You earn community service hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours for the SBUSD graduation requirement. Uniform shirt purchase required (waived with SNAP/CalFresh EBT).
duration: Up to 16 two-hour weekend shifts, Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day (2026: May 23 to Sept 6)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. Training was May 16-17, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

name: Junior Counselor Program (Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: You help summer camp counselors with daily activities. You earn volunteer service hours. You build leadership skills.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer service hours.
duration: Summer camp season; length not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. Use the Register link or call Parks and Recreation at 805-564-5418.

name: Parks and Recreation Seasonal Jobs (lifeguard, camp staff)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation
what_you_do: These are seasonal and part-time jobs. They help build workplace skills and experience. Titles include Lifeguard, Camp Counselor, Recreation Leader and Seasonal Program Staff.
pay_detail: Hourly, set by position. A March 2024 City notice listed $18.78 to $23.92 an hour for lifeguards, camp counselors and swim instructors; check the current posting.
duration: Summer camps and pools; aquatics hires through the year with more hiring before summer
deadline_text: Aquatics hires year-round; summer hiring is announced in the spring (March 2025 release: tryouts and interviews in April, training before June).

name: Teen Job and Volunteer Fair (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: Meet local employers and nonprofits face to face. Look for summer jobs, internships and volunteer roles. A teen interview skills workshop is held the following week.
pay_detail: Free to attend.
duration: One afternoon, 2 hours
deadline_text: 2026 fair: Wednesday, April 15, 2026, 4:00 to 6:00 PM at Central Library (workshop April 22). The 2027 date is not posted; the library calls it annual.

grades: Book reviews: grades 7-12. Teen Advisory Board: high school students.
name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: You earn community service hours at the library. You can join Teen Volunteer Time. You can join the Teen Advisory Board to plan teen programs and shape the collection. You can also write book reviews.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours (1 hour per book review, up to 5 reviews a month).
duration: Teen Volunteer Time: Thursdays 4:15 PM at Central Library (or Saturdays 11 AM to 12:30 PM at Eastside Library). Advisory Board: twice a month on Tuesdays, 5-6:30 PM, during the school year and once a month during the summer.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board applications are taken at the start of each school term. Teen Volunteer Time and book reviews are ongoing.

name: Teens Teach Tech (Santa Barbara Public Library)
what_you_do: You learn robotics and coding. Then you work in pairs. You plan and lead one robotics program for children. You plan and lead one for teens at the library. There are six programs in all.
pay_detail: Unpaid. About 52 community service hours in total.
duration: November 2026 to June 2027, about 2 hours a week (schedule to be set)
deadline_text: Apply by Saturday, October 24, 2026.

name: Dual Enrollment (Santa Barbara City College)
what_you_do: You take real college courses while in high school. Santa Barbara and Carpinteria Unified students can take them at their high school. All high school and home school students can take them on the SBCC campus or online.
pay_detail: Applying to SBCC is free. High-school-based courses cost nothing. For online and campus courses, enrollment fees are waived but students pay student fees and textbooks.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Fall 2026 dual enrollment registration began July 1. Deadlines for each term are on the Dual Enrollment calendar on the SBCC page.

name: Sea Center Volunteers (Ty Warner Sea Center)
org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, Ty Warner Sea Center
what_you_do: Help guests at the Stearns Wharf aquarium meet live animals, from sea anemones to small sharks. You do hands-on demos and live animal talks. Teens 14 and up can train as aquarist volunteers.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A $45 program fee covers uniform, badge and administration; email scvolunteer@sbnature2.org for a fee waiver before your first training.
duration: One shift per week for at least 4 months
deadline_text: The Museum's teen page says the Sea Center accepts volunteer applications year-round.

grades: 10th or 11th grade (outstanding 9th graders considered case by case)
name: Research Mentorship Program (UCSB Summer Sessions)
what_you_do: You do a college-level research project. A mentor helps you. The mentor can be a grad student, a postdoc or a faculty member. You go to a research talk series. You take part in university life for about seven weeks.
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $5,675 total ($75 application fee + $1,000 deposit + $5,600 tuition and program fees); residential $13,274 total (adds $7,599 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 8, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

name: Summer Research Academies (UCSB Summer Sessions)
what_you_do: You pick a research track in STEM, humanities or social sciences. You take a 4-unit university course. You build a research topic with an instructor. At the end, you present your findings at a capstone seminar.
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $3,475 total ($75 application fee + $900 deposit + $3,400 tuition and program fees); residential $9,874 total (adds $6,399 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 25 to July 23, 2027).
deadline_text: Application window Dec 15, 2026 to Mar 22, 2027. Reviews start in January and decisions are rolling.

name: Santa Barbara Youth Council
what_you_do: Speak for teens to City Council and city departments, recommend youth programs and policies, and plan teen events. Meets twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid (the City lists compensation as none).
duration: Two-year term, July 1 to June 30. Meets the 1st and 3rd Monday at 5:15 PM at Franklin Neighborhood Center (monthly in July and August).
deadline_text: Fall 2026 City advisory group recruitment: applications due Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Applications are accepted year-round for future rounds.

name: Santa Barbara Zoo Jobs for Teens (Guest Experience Specialist and seasonal)
what_you_do: These are entry-level seasonal jobs. Examples are Guest Experience Specialist and Zoo Camp positions. The Zoo says most openings are for applicants 14 and older. It welcomes first-time workers for entry-level roles.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page; see each job listing.
duration: Seasonal, mostly spring and summer
deadline_text: No dates posted. The Zoo says the busiest hiring is a month before spring and summer school breaks.

name: Zoo Teen Volunteers (Junior Camp Counselor, Leader in Training, Teen Conservation Club)
what_you_do: You help run Zoo Camp. You can be a Junior Camp Counselor or a Leader in Training. Or join the Teen Conservation Club. It has monthly meetings and conservation projects.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.
duration: Junior Camp Counselor: 7 hours a day, Mon-Fri, 3 summer weeks plus 1 fall week and 2 winter weeks
deadline_text: No application dates are posted. The Zoo volunteer page says it is not taking new volunteer recruitment applications at this time (that line sits in the adult sign-up steps), yet the teen sections still show application links. The Leader in Training dates (June 17 to Aug 23) have no year.

name: Santa Clara County Teen CERT Academy
what_you_do: You take a weekend emergency response course. It covers fire safety, search and rescue, stop the bleed and disaster psychology. After it, you can help your community in disasters. You can earn 20+ volunteer hours.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
deadline_text: Join the waitlist for the next academy. The site shows January 8 to 10 with no year printed. The last academy was March 13 to 15, 2026.

duration: September to May, up to six years
name: Santa Clara Youth Commission
what_you_do: You advise the City Council on issues that affect teens and help plan events like a 5K run. Fifteen teens serve, and the group meets monthly during the school year.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 recruitment is closed. The page does not give 2027-28 dates.

name: Santa Clarita Public Library Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
what_you_do: Teens give input to the library, meet other teens and can earn service hours. Meetings run September through May.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Participation can earn service hours (the number is not stated).
duration: Meetings September through May
deadline_text: New members are always welcome. No deadline.

name: County of Santa Clara Intern and Earn
org: County of Santa Clara Employment Connection
what_you_do: You get an eight week paid county internship, plus job-readiness workshops, hiring events and coaching from an Employment Counselor. You work up to 30 hours a week.
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
deadline_text: Posted 2026 cohorts: Summer deadline May 20, program June 29 to Aug 7. Fall deadline Sept 19, program Oct 19 to Dec 11. The page also says it is accepting applications now; call to ask about the next cohort. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers (tutor a K-6 student)
what_you_do: Teens 14 and older can volunteer at the Santa Clara County Library District. One job is tutoring a student after school. The student is in kindergarten through grade 6.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No deadline posted.

name: County of Santa Clara Student Internship Program (Level I, high school)
org: County of Santa Clara Employee Services Agency
what_you_do: High school students can work as paid student interns in county departments. They help professional staff. They work under close supervision. Tasks depend on the department.

what_you_do: You take a two-week hands-on medicine course with skills like ultrasound, dissection and suturing. This is a fee-based program. You pay to attend, and it is not a job.
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $6,580 on campus, $4,580 virtual, $2,480 for the 10-week fall virtual option. Application fee $95 for summer ($75 fall). Fee waivers for U.S. citizens or green card holders under $80,000 household income or in low-income support programs, limited and first come first served.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 13 to 24 on campus; July 27 to Aug 7 virtual)
deadline_text: All 2026 programs closed. The page says the next cycle opens Jan 1, 2027; no 2027 deadline posted. Last cycle: Nov 1, 2025 to Feb 9, 2026.

name: Pediatrics Internship Program at Stanford (PIPS)
what_you_do: You do a seven-week summer internship in pediatrics at Stanford, about 30 hours a week. It is for students from nearby counties.
pay_detail: No fee. $3,000 stipend for students who show financial need.
duration: 7 weeks, 30 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Feb 23, 2026 (decisions Apr 1, 2026). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
what_you_do: You can take one live online college-style course, Monday to Friday for two weeks, as a middle or high school student. You may take only one course per summer.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.
duration: Two weeks, live online (2026: June 15 to 26 or July 6 to 17)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was Mar 13, 2026 (decisions mid-May 2026). 2027 dates not posted.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
what_you_do: You do eight weeks of full-time biomedical lab research with Stanford faculty and graduate student mentors. Morning lectures are held at the start.
grades: Juniors and seniors (classes of 2027 and 2028 for the 2027 program)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: the 2026 application fee was $50 (waivable for family income under $80,000). No program cost. Most students get no stipend; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist.
duration: 8 weeks, about 40 hours a week, tentatively June 7 to July 29, 2027
deadline_text: Application opens Dec 18, 2026 at 5pm Pacific; due late February 2027 (exact date not posted). 2026 deadline was Feb 21, 2026.

name: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
what_you_do: You can join a five-week, tuition-free summer program on Stanford's campus to explore medicine. It is for current juniors from low-income and first-generation backgrounds.
pay_detail: Tuition free. Housing and stipend not stated.
duration: About 5 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 26)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 23, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Stonecrest Next Gen Youth Leadership Program
what_you_do: Meet one Saturday a month. You meet city leaders and learn how city government works. You also learn about public safety and leadership. You learn about community and economic development. One trip is to the Georgia State Capitol.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 6 Saturday sessions, 10 am to 1 pm, Oct 2026 to Mar 2027
deadline_text: The city's Sept. 3, 2026 notice says registration opens that day. No deadline is listed. It closes when all 30 spots are filled. Sessions: Oct 24, Nov 14, Dec 12, 2026; Jan 30, Feb (Capitol date to be set), Mar 20, 2027.

duration: Summer reading volunteers help 2 to 6 hours a week for the 8 week program. Shelving volunteers commit to a weekly 2 hour shift for at least 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens can earn service hours.
name: VolunTEENs and Service Hour Projects (ages 13 to 18)
city: Sugar Grove, IL (Kane County, near Aurora)
what_you_do: Shelve books, help with grounds care, help at the summer reading check-in table, or do a short service hour project. The library has a VolunTEENs program just for ages 13 to 18.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer reading volunteering is seasonal.

name: Sunburst Youth Challenge Academy (National Guard)
org: California National Guard and State of California (Sunburst Youth Academy)
what_you_do: This is a free, live in leadership academy for teens who are behind in school. Cadets work on discipline, life skills and school credits. The site says up to 65 high school credits. There is support for 12 months after graduation.
pay_detail: Free to attend (page wording).
duration: 22 week residential program (per the site's video text), then support for 12 months. Class 39 begins January 2027.
deadline_text: Class 39 begins in January 2027. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. The next in person orientation is October 24, 2026 at 1 PM at 4022 Saratoga Ave, Bldg 21, Los Alamitos. A Final Roll Call is held in December; without a finished application and roll call you will not be considered for Class 39.

name: City of Sunnyvale Youth Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Youth 13 and older can volunteer. They can help at special events or do office tasks. They can also work with young people or seniors. Library roles are included.
deadline_text: Ongoing. Roles are posted as needed.

name: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (SVCTE)
org: Silicon Valley Career Technical Education (Metropolitan Education District)
what_you_do: High school job-skills classes in 22 career tracks, including AI engineering, auto repair, culinary arts, nursing, heating and cooling (HVAC), animation and fire science. Some give college credit, and some prepare you for an apprenticeship (paid job training).
pay_detail: Not stated. Dual enrollment courses earn college credit. The site links a Schedule of Fees page that was not read, so ask about costs.
deadline_text: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your counselor for enrollment dates.

name: Dual Enrollment at Technical College System of Georgia colleges
org: Technical College System of Georgia (including Atlanta Technical College)
what_you_do: Take college and career courses at a technical college while in high school and earn high school and college credit at the same time. Funding covers tuition, fees and books for the first 30 hours.
pay_detail: No tuition, fees or books for the first 30 hours for eligible students. Not a paid job.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
deadline_text: Each college sets deadlines. Atlanta Technical College lists June 1 for fall, Nov 1 for spring and April 1 for summer (no year stated).

name: The Tech Interactive Teen Volunteer Program (Holiday Helper)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers lead hands-on science, tech and art activities for museum visitors. This is during the holiday season. Volunteers complete six shifts. Each shift is 3 to 4 hours.
duration: Six shifts in the peak windows: Nov 21 to 29 and Dec 19 to Jan 3
deadline_text: The official page gives no application dates as of Oct 9, 2026.

name: Teen Line Volunteer Listener (peer hotline)
org: Teen Line, a program of Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services
what_you_do: Teens train to give peer support to other teens by hotline, text and email. Adult mental health pros guide the work.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns community service hours.
duration: Training of 65+ hours (the main Teen Line page says over 100), then at least two evening shifts a month
deadline_text: The page says applications are due "Monday September 8, 2026 by 5pm" (that date is a Tuesday, so confirm the day), which has now passed. Training runs three times a year (Fall, Spring, Summer). Next dates are not posted; the page has an email interest list for future applications.

name: Texas 4-H
what_you_do: Join a county 4-H club and pick at least one project. Take part in club meetings, events and contests. The program offers hands-on leadership, community service and career discovery.
pay_detail: Youth fee is $25 if you enroll by October 31 and $30 from November 1 through the end of the 4-H year.
duration: One 4-H year. Every membership resets to inactive on August 15, so you re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: Enroll by October 31 for the lower fee ($25). After that the fee is $30 until the end of the 4-H year. Memberships reset every August 15.

name: Texas Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Texas
what_you_do: Spend a week running a pretend city, county and state government. You join one of two practice political parties, run for office, hear speakers and debate.
grades: Just finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: American Legion Posts or other community groups often pay the fee, so the cost to the boy is often little to nothing. The fee amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: One week. The 2026 session ran Sunday June 7 to Friday June 12, 2026.
deadline_text: 2027 dates and the application deadline are not posted on the pages read. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 12, 2026. The site shows an Applications Now Open banner, but it posts no deadline or 2027 dates, so ask your school and local Post.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Texas Bluebonnet Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Texas
what_you_do: Spend a week at Texas Lutheran University in a pretend 51st state. You set up your own city, county and state governments and take a trip to the State Capitol.
grades: Junior year (11th grade) of high school
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per delegate, not including travel to Seguin. Rules say a unit, school or community group pays it, never the student or her family.
duration: One week. The 2026 session was Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20, 2026.
deadline_text: 2027 dates are not posted. In 2026, units could reserve spots Feb 1 to May 1 and schools Feb 15 to May 1. The page says spots fill fast, so act quickly.

name: Texas ChalleNGe Academy
what_you_do: Live on the Eagle Lake campus in a free residential program for teens who are disengaged from school. After the on-campus phase there is a follow-up phase with a mentor.
pay_detail: Free. The page says the program is tuition free to the families it serves.
duration: The page lists a tuition-free 22-week residential program. It also lists a 20-week Residential Phase and a 5 and a half month on-campus phase, then a 12-month Post-Residential Phase. The page says the program requires a 17 and a half month commitment. Confirm with a recruiter.
deadline_text: Classes start in January and July. The application cutoff is normally at least 30 days before class starts.

name: Summer Junior Volunteer Program (North Austin)
what_you_do: This is four weeks of full-day volunteering at a children's hospital. You take three to four assignments a day. Examples are a tea cart, craft cart, library, physical therapy and supply chain. You also get a lunch and learn.
grades: Enrolled in high school for the following school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program
duration: About 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 1 to June 25 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 application opened Monday Feb 9 and closed Friday Feb 13, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Texas DECA (high school)
org: Texas DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
what_you_do: Join your school's DECA chapter to build business and marketing skills. Take part in DECA programs and contests. Texas DECA runs a yearly state career development conference.
pay_detail: Student membership is $16 total: $8 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines come from your chapter advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 25 to 27, 2027 at the George R. Brown Convention Center in Houston.

name: Texas FFA Association
what_you_do: Take an agricultural science class at school and join your local FFA chapter. FFA is a student-led leadership group. Members earn degrees and can join contests, speaking events and leadership programs.
grades: Agricultural science classes start no earlier than 7th grade. Junior FFA starts at 3rd grade.
pay_detail: National dues $7 plus Texas dues $9 is $16 a year, not counting area, district or local dues. Junior FFA is $9 a year (state only).
duration: School year, tied to your agricultural science class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.

name: Texas HOSA Future Health Professionals
what_you_do: Join a HOSA chapter at your school to explore health careers. Texas HOSA runs a state leadership conference each year. Membership comes through school chapters.
grades: Middle school grades 6 to 8, and high school (secondary) students
pay_detail: There are membership fees, but the amounts are not on the pages read. The site links to a 2026 to 2027 fee schedule.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No membership deadlines or conference dates are on the pages read. Ask your advisor for dates.

name: Texas State Parks Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer at a Texas state park. Jobs include special events, gift shop and office help, trail and grounds work, plant restoration, and leading tours and nature programs.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ mentions no volunteer fees or costs.
duration: Varies by opening
deadline_text: Apply any time. Openings are listed in the online portal.

name: REACT @ TAMU Chemistry (summer research training)
org: Texas A&M University, Department of Chemistry
what_you_do: Spend part of the summer on campus in a hands-on chemistry research training program. Up to 20 students learn lab skills, see research demos and prepare for chemistry research in high school.
grades: High school students (the 2026 page says as of Fall 2026)
pay_detail: Applying is free. The registration fee is $250, due after you are accepted (2026 page). Lunch is provided.
duration: The 2026 header lists July 13 to 24, 2026 and also calls it a 6-day in-person program. The 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: The 2027 application opens Jan 19, 2027. No closing date is posted. In 2026, students were notified April 24, 2026.

name: Summer Earn and Learn (SEAL) for students with disabilities
org: Texas Workforce Commission, Vocational Rehabilitation, with local workforce boards
what_you_do: Get a paid summer job placement of at least five weeks. You earn a paycheck while learning new skills and gaining work experience.
pay_detail: Wages for hours worked. Each local board sets one hourly wage for its program. The amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: At least five weeks of paid work, with at least four hours in a week to count as a week. No more than 40 hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates for summer 2027 are posted on the pages read. It is a summer program. Ask your local office in the fall or winter.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Texas Wing
what_you_do: Join a local squadron to learn leadership, aerospace and STEM, fitness and character. Cadets can go to summer and winter encampments. They can take part in real Civil Air Patrol missions.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Year-round program with squadron meetings, plus encampments and other events
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend three squadron meetings first.

grades: High school students and recent graduates
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
name: The Trade Collective (skilled trades student sign-up)
what_you_do: This Evanston group links students to local firms and to job training. You learn skilled trades. Trades include plumbing, HVAC and automotive. Others are electrical, aviation and manufacturing. Students meet business owners. The owners can help start careers.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: Travis County Health and Human Services with Austin Public Health
what_you_do: You get paid summer work experience at a host site. There are more than 80 host sites. They are businesses, nonprofits and government offices. You first complete a required job readiness training.
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page
duration: not stated
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed and the page is labeled Expired. 2027 dates are not posted; the county has a 2027 interest form to get notified when applications open.

name: TreePeople Volunteer Events (all ages with parent consent)
what_you_do: Sign up for tree planting and other volunteer events. They are listed on the TreePeople events calendar.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Single events; calendar posted at least a month ahead
deadline_text: Sign up for each event on the Events Calendar. No program deadline.

name: Youth Tree Team
what_you_do: Do paid green jobs with Trees Atlanta staff to get hands-on experience. Weekly sessions teach job-search skills and money basics.
grades: Currently in high school or about to start high school
pay_detail: Starting at $12 per hour
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 12:30 pm
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: opened Nov 15, 2025, closed Feb 2, 2026, job ran June 1 to July 17, 2026. The page says 2027 details are coming later.

name: Tri-Valley ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
what_you_do: You can take free career classes through your high school. Your high school is in Dublin, Livermore or Pleasanton. There are 30 or more courses. They cover about 10 career areas. Examples are building trades, health science, IT and public services.
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is closed. Talk to your school's College and Career Specialist or counselor.

name: Trybe Summer Jobs and Paid Internships (East Oakland)
what_you_do: You can get skills building, leadership training and paid internships with Trybe, an East Bay youth program. The City's summer jobs list shows that Trybe offers a 100 hour summer job for East Oakland youth.
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).
duration: About 100 hours
deadline_text: No current dates posted. The old 2022 posting took applications until May 31.

name: Tucker Youth Council
what_you_do: Meet monthly, September to April, with city leaders. Explore civic issues, serve as ambassadors for peers, and learn how local government works. Members commit to a full year term.
pay_detail: Unpaid civic role
duration: One-year term. Meetings on the third Wednesday, September to April.
deadline_text: The 2026 council application closed Aug 19, 2026. Meetings: 9/16, 10/21, 11/18, 1/20, 2/24, 3/17, 4/21, with optional dinner 4/26 and celebration 5/7. The next application is not posted.

name: Conservation Corps Youth Education: Youth Interns
what_you_do: Learn about nature and caring for natural areas. Build outdoor skills. Finish community projects with a crew led by young adults. You are based at a nature center or park in the Twin Cities area.
pay_detail: Most Youth Interns are paid starting at $13.50 an hour. Some positions are unpaid. Pay may be higher depending on your age and whether Step Up, Right Track or the Corps employs you.
